docs.text: ❌ Don't ✅ Do Instead prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", ...) inline in every node prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", advanced_mode) yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1]... repeated 5× data = parse_yaml_response(response) try: enc = tiktoken.get_encoding(...) in 3 different methods tokens = count_tokens(text) (model-calibrated) provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER") + if/else in 2 nodes provider, model, endpoint, key = resolve_llm_settings() / max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared) safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95) safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level) thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level") in a node thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") Redefining import re inside functions when it's already imported at the top Use the top-level import

docs.title: When to Create New Helpers
docs.text: If you find yourself writing the same block of code (≥3 lines) in 2+ nodes, extract it as a module-level helper function. Name it descriptively and add a docstring explaining what it does, what it takes, and what it returns.

docs.title: main.py Modular Design
docs.text:
main() is a short orchestrator (~40 lines). All logic is extracted into module-level functions:

Function Signature Returns Description parse_arguments () -> tuple[ArgumentParser, Namespace] (parser, args) All argparse setup; returns parser (for .error()) and parsed args resolve_mode_and_project (args) -> tuple[str, str] (mode, project_name) Handles --advanced legacy flag, derives project name from args build_shared_store (args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name) -> dict shared dict Constructs the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes resolve_thinking_plan (args) -> tuple[str, dict, list[str]] (profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides) Pure (no emit), runs before init_output() so string translation uses the plan's translate_strings level _validate_thinking_args (args, invalid_overrides) -> None — Emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE (exit 1), WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED (override names a node not in thinking.MODE_NODES[mode]), and WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE — after init_output() detect_llm_config (args) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int] (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length) resolve_llm_settings() + context length display_config (args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan) -> None — Emits all CFG_* strings to console (startup order) — — parse_arguments → resolve_thinking_plan → init_output(auto_translate=False) → _check_quoting_errors / _validate_thinking_args → standalone --cleanup → check_llm_auth() (exit 1 on failure) → translate_missing_strings() → notice_legacy_cache() → mode/project resolution → flow. Translation is an LLM call, so it runs only after arguments and credentials are checked. _emit_usage_summary () -> None — In finally: one LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY per provider used (llm_common.get_usage_summary(): calls, input incl. cached / cache write, output/thinking, refusals, fallbacks, truncations, cost via token_utils.format_cost), then LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER and one LLM_USAGE_STEP row per step (get_step_summary(): calls, LLM-cache hits, billed vs estimated input with deviation, output/thinking, cost) _run_cleanup () -> None — Removes llm_cache_v2.json (+ .tmp), legacy llm_cache.json, llm_token_calibration.json (+ .tmp), and the logs/ directory

docs.title: Depth-First File Ordering (api-reference mode)
docs.text:
In DeterministicFileMapper.post(), chapter_order is sorted by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical within same depth). This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files in WriteChapters, making their summaries available as previous_chapters_summary context when processing higher-level files.

shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
    chapter_order,
    key=lambda idx: (-modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep), modules[idx]["original_path"].lower()),
)

This ordering is language-agnostic — it works for any codebase (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.) because it exploits the universal convention that utility files live in deeper directories.

docs.title: 17. LLM Providers & Thinking Flows
docs.text: Notes for AI: utils/llm_anthropic.py is the ONLY file that imports the anthropic SDK. utils/thinking.py is the ONLY place that defines per-node effort. Nodes never hard-code a thinking level.

docs.title: Thinking Plan (utils/thinking.py)
docs.text:
Every LLM call site has a NODE key. main.resolve_thinking_plan() builds shared["thinking_plan"] once: --thinking-override NODE=LEVEL > --thinking-level LEVEL (all nodes) > --thinking-profile table (+ per-mode adjustments). Nodes read their level with resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") (falls back to shared["thinking_level"] when no plan exists).

NODE key Call site Workload filter_files DeterministicFileMapper Mechanical classification (api-reference) extract_facts ExtractFacts (per file) Extraction with verbatim quotes (api-reference) map_abstractions MapAbstractions (per batch) Extraction reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships Reasoning-heavy synthesis order_chapters OrderChapters Planning write_chapters WriteChapters (per chapter) Long-form generation chapter_summary WriteChapters (per chapter, summary_thinking_level) Mechanical summary group_modules CombineTutorial → write_mkdocs_output nav grouping Light structuring translate_strings utils/i18n.auto_translate (via init_output) Mechanical translation

Profiles (auto = balanced on ANTHROPIC, GEMINI and OPENROUTER (thinking.PROFILED_PROVIDERS), off elsewhere; off = every node None → model default):

NODE economy balanced quality max filter_files low low medium medium extract_facts low low medium medium map_abstractions low medium high xhigh reduce_abstractions medium high high max identify_abstractions medium high high max analyze_relationships low medium high xhigh order_chapters low medium high high write_chapters low medium high xhigh chapter_summary low low medium medium group_modules low medium high high translate_strings low low medium medium

Rationale: reasoning-heavy synthesis (identify/reduce) gets the most effort; relationship analysis only feeds the summary, diagram and ordering; chapter writing runs N times (hundreds in api-reference), so shipped profiles stop at high — current Claude 5 models already do strong work at medium (Opus 5.5 at medium beats Opus 5 at high on knowledge work). xhigh/max only in the explicit max profile (use when a gain has been measured).

Per-mode adjustments: economy → write_chapters=medium for advanced (design-rationale chapters, at most max_abstraction_num calls). MODE_NODES lists which nodes can run per mode (api-reference: filter_files, extract_facts, write_chapters, chapter_summary, group_modules, translate_strings; other modes: the analysis nodes + write_chapters, chapter_summary, translate_strings) — used for the config display and WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED.

Provider mapping of a level: ANTHROPIC → output_config.effort (xhigh → high on the 4.6 family; pre-4.6 models such as Haiku 4.5 → budget_tokens 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000); GEMINI 3.x → thinking_level (per-model set, llm_config.GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS), Gemini 2.5 → thinking_budget (GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS clamped to GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES); OPENROUTER → reasoning.effort clamped to the catalog's supported_efforts, or reasoning.max_tokens for budget-only models; OLLAMA → low/medium/high. The startup display shows it as CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT (llm_config.describe_thinking_support).

docs.title: call_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_anthropic.py)
docs.text:
• Model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL, default claude-sonnet-5 (1M context, 128K output; claude-opus-5-5 for Opus 5.5). Limits from the Models API (client.models.retrieve(model) → max_input_tokens, max_tokens), cached per process; offline fallback 1M/128K (Haiku 4.5: 200K/64K) with WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP.
  • Thinking: adaptive-thinking models (Opus 5.x, Sonnet 5, Fable/Mythos, Opus 4.6–4.8, Sonnet 4.6) get thinking={"type": "adaptive"} and, when a level is set, output_config={"effort": level} (minimal → low). With no level (model default), thinking is omitted on Opus/Sonnet 4.6–4.8, where omission means no thinking; Opus/Sonnet 5.x, Fable and Mythos think adaptively either way. Sonnet 5 (the default) thinks adaptively unless told otherwise and defaults to effort high; Opus 5.5 cannot disable thinking and defaults to medium — so the plan sets effort explicitly. With --debug, display="summarized" and the summaries are written to the log file only.
  • Never sent: temperature/top_p/top_k, assistant prefill, budget_tokens on adaptive models (all 400 on Opus 5.5; Sonnet 5 rejects enabled budget thinking and non-default sampling values).
  • max_tokens (thinking counts toward it): llm_config.anthropic_planned_output(model, level) — adaptive models: ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT (minimal/low 32K, medium/high/None 64K, xhigh 96K, max 128K); Haiku 4.5 and older: ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL + 16K for the reply. input_token_budget reserves the same value. Level → effort normalization (llm_config.anthropic_effort) is shared too. ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is a hard cap: planned max_tokens = min(table, cap), and the truncation retry never exceeds it. Ceiling = min(model output cap, context − count_tokens(prompt) − ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN (2,000), cap), min 4,096; WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED only when the ceiling is < 90% of the plan. The prompt is tokenized once per call.
  • Streaming: every request uses messages.stream(...) + get_final_message() (large max_tokens never hit HTTP timeouts).
  • Refusal fallbacks: ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS=default (Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x only) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 + extra_body={"fallbacks": "default"} on client.beta.messages.stream; a comma-separated model list (any model, e.g. Mythos 5.1) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 + [{"model": ...}]; off disables. A fallback-served answer emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED. Cost with fallbacks sums usage.iterations, each at its own model's price; an attempt with 0 output tokens (declined before output) is unbilled.
  • Prompt caching: ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE=on adds top-level cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}. Off by default: templates start with per-call content (chapter name, batch files), so only exact retries share a prefix — the 1.25× write cost is not repaid on single-shot calls.
  • Response: text = concatenated text blocks (thinking/fallback blocks ignored). A reply that ends with max_tokens / model_context_window_exceeded is returned as TruncatedResponse (a str subclass with truncated = True), which call_llm never caches. Refusal / truncation handling: Section 13.
  • Usage: one ledger request per billed attempt (_billed_entries: every usage.iterations entry with output under server-side fallbacks, each priced and listed under its own model; otherwise the top-level usage), recording total input (input + cache read + cache write), output, cache read/write and thinking (usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens). A refusal with no output tokens is an unbilled decline (_declined_before_output, same rule for tokens and _message_cost): recorded as one unmeasured $0 request. _billed_tokens sums the billed attempts for the debug line. The attempt that produced the message (top-level usage) feeds token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens unless a fallback model served it; the truncation retry observes once. Per request, ANTHROPIC USAGE | ... (DEBUG, dest BOTH: console with --debug) shows tokens, thinking, cache, est. cost and observed_token_ratio (billed input ÷ tiktoken count); call_llm prints the per-call LLM_CALL_USAGE line and the totals are emitted after the flow as LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY. Prices (USD/MTok in/out/cache-read) live in _PRICING; 5-minute cache writes = 1.25× input.

docs.title: Credentials & preflight (utils/llm_config.check_anthropic_auth)
docs.text:
The anthropic SDK (zero-arg anthropic.Anthropic()) resolves credentials itself: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN → the ant auth login profile (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE or the active one, stored under ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR, default %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows / ~/.config/anthropic elsewhere) → Workload Identity Federation. Empty variables count as unset. For OAuth profiles the SDK merges its oauth-2025-04-20 beta header with ours (fallback beta), so betas=[...] is safe.

check_anthropic_auth() -> bool (SDK-free; returns True for every other provider) runs before any LLM call in both entry points — main() (after argument validation, before translate_missing_strings() and the flow) and the utils/call_llm.py self-test (after init_output):

Step Condition Result 1 anthropic package not importable ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING (pip install -r requirements.txt) → False 2 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN non-empty (both → WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 3 Federation vars (ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, _ORGANIZATION_ID, _SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID + _IDENTITY_TOKEN[_FILE]) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 4 ant on PATH run ant auth status (30 s timeout, empty key vars removed from its env). Its exit code is not a health signal, so parse_ant_auth_status() reads the (active) rows of the Credentials / Workspace sections (token prefixes redacted). Active credential → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK (source + workspace) → True; none → ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN + the (redacted) status output + help → False; subprocess error/timeout → WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED → True 5 ant not on PATH stored credentials/*.json in the config dir → WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND → True; otherwise ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS + help (incl. OS-specific ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_INSTALL_ANT_{WIN,MAC,LINUX}: winget install Anthropic.Ant / brew install anthropics/tap/ant / release packages, each with a go install or zip fallback) → False

Help lines: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_HEADER, _KEY (API key from platform.claude.com/settings/keys), _INSTALL_ANT_* (only when ant is missing), _LOGIN (ant auth login / ant auth status), _NOTE (leave the key unset; billed to the API org, not a Claude.ai plan). Interactive login is for your own machine; CI uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or federation.

utils/call_llm.py adds the repo root to sys.path when run as a script, so the self-test works as both python utils/call_llm.py and python -m utils.call_llm.

docs.title: call_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_gemini.py)
docs.text:
The only module that imports google-genai (>= 1.56: thinking_level MINIMAL/MEDIUM; 1.51 had LOW/HIGH only; older SDKs reject the field).

Model (prefix, longest wins) Thinking control Levels Default when omitted gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.7-flash thinking_level low, medium, high (MINIMAL errors) medium gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash(-lite) thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high medium (Flash-Lite: minimal) gemini-3.1-pro(-preview) thinking_level low, medium, high (cannot turn off) high gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high minimal / high other gemini-3.x, gemini-flash-latest / gemini-pro-latest, newer families thinking_level low, medium, high — gemini-2.5-pro / -flash / -flash-lite thinking_budget 128-32,768 / 1-24,576 / 512-24,576 dynamic gemini-1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants, non-Gemini ids none (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED) — —

Model ids are normalized first (llm_config.gemini_model_id: models/… and publishers/google/models/… prefixes stripped, lower-cased).

  • thinking_level and thinking_budget are never sent together (400). Levels outside the set clamp (WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED, once per model+level); xhigh/max → high. No level → no thinking_config (model default). include_thoughts=True only with --debug (summaries go to the log).
  • max_output_tokens = llm_config.gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit): minimal/low 32,768, else 65,536 (the 3.x / 2.5 output limit, thinking included), capped by GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Gemini's input and output limits are separate, so output is not reduced for large prompts and input_token_budget reserves only CONTEXT_MARGIN.
  • Limits: models.get (input_token_limit, output_token_limit) on AI Studio, cached; Vertex AI (SDK maps no limits) and failures → GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS (1,048,576 / 65,536; WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP).
  • One client per process: HttpOptions(timeout=GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS×1000 ms (default 1800 s, total deadline), retry_options=HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, 408/429/5xx)); Vertex via vertexai=True, project, location=GEMINI_LOCATION (default global — Gemini 3.x is not served from us-central1); AI Studio via vertexai=False, api_key.
  • Requests stream (generate_content_stream): text = non-thought parts; prompt_feedback from the first chunk; the last usage_metadata and finish_reason win. Never sends temperature/top_p/top_k (deprecated on 3.x).
  • Usage: input = prompt_token_count (incl. cached), output = candidates + thoughts (thinking is billed as output), cost from _PRICING (standard prices, AI Studio = Vertex global; >200K-prompt tier for Pro; 3.6–3.8 Flash at the introductory _INTRO_PRICING through 2026-12-31; Vertex regional endpoints +10%; unknown models → cost n/a).
  • Retired ids (GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS: id → (replacement, still aliased on AI Studio)): gemini-3-pro-preview on AI Studio → WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (served by 3.1 Pro Preview); on Vertex, and gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview anywhere → ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (preflight fails).
  • Vertex locations per model (GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS, longest prefix): 3.1 Pro / 3 Flash / 3 Pro → global; 3.8 Flash Cyber → global, us; 3.5 Flash → any (also single regions); other 3.x → global, us, eu. us / eu use the aiplatform.{us|eu}.rep.googleapis.com endpoints.

docs.title: call_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_openrouter.py)
docs.text:
Catalog-driven (llm_config.openrouter_model_info: exact id, canonical_slug, a dated canonical slug only (anthropic/claude-4.6-opus → …-20260205; looser prefixes are not matched), routing suffixes :nitro/:floor/:online/…, ~…-latest aliases via alias_target). The catalog is fetched from {OPENROUTER_BASE_URL}/v1/models and cached on success; after a failure callers get None and the fetch is retried after a 60 s cooldown (WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE once). Family checks (rejects_sampling_params, get_token_ratio) resolve aliases through the catalog, and _normalize_claude_id maps version-first ids (claude-4.7-opus → claude-opus-4-7).

Catalog reasoning Request supported_efforts list reasoning.effort = level clamped to the list (never none; WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED once) supported_efforts key missing + supports_max_tokens (e.g. Qwen 3.8 Flash) reasoning.max_tokens = 1,024 / 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000 for minimal…max (kept below max_tokens) supported_efforts null / key missing otherwise (e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5) reasoning.effort = level (OpenRouter converts to a budget) no reasoning and not in supported_parameters no reasoning (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED once) model not in catalog / catalog unavailable reasoning.effort = level (unverified)
  • reasoning.exclude = not --debug (reasoning is billed either way; with --debug it is logged).
  • max_tokens: openrouter_output_budget(model, level) (shared per-effort table capped by top_provider.max_completion_tokens, 32K when that is unknown, and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), clamped to context − prompt − CONTEXT_MARGIN (min 4,096). Omitted for a model missing from the catalog unless OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is set.
  • temperature (OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE, default 0.7) only when: no reasoning requested, not rejects_sampling_params(model) (Claude 4.7+/5.x, Gemini 3.x), temperature in supported_parameters, and the model is neither mandatory nor default_enabled reasoning.
  • SSE streaming (stream: true; lines split as bytes and decoded per line — str.splitlines() would break JSON containing U+2028; :-prefixed keep-alive lines skipped; read timeout OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS between events). A proxy that answers with one application/json body is parsed as a single chunk. Headers Authorization: Bearer (when a key is set). App attribution is opt-in (llm_openrouter._attribution_headers()): only when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set are HTTP-Referer (that URL), X-OpenRouter-Title and legacy X-Title ("Codebase Knowledge Builder") sent; unset → no attribution headers.
  • Usage from the final chunk: prompt / completion (incl. reasoning) / completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens / prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens/cache_write_tokens / cost (USD, authoritative; with BYOK, cost_details.upstream_inference_cost is added).
  • Claude 4.6+ through OpenRouter: effort → Anthropic output_config.effort (xhigh → high on 4.6, minimal → low); Gemini 3.x: effort → thinkingLevel.

docs.title: Shared helpers (utils/llm_common.py, SDK-free)
docs.text: TruncatedResponse(str) (truncated = True), LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider, retryable=False), the refusal memo (request_key, remember_refusal, previous_refusal), the usage ledger (record_usage(provider, model, *, input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cache_read, cache_write, cost) — input_tokens is the TOTAL prompt tokens incl. cached for every provider, cache fields are breakdowns, cost=None counts an unpriced call; measured=False (no usage reported, or an unbilled decline) counts the request in unmeasured_calls and keeps it out of estimate-vs-billed comparisons; totals are kept per provider and per step (usage_step(step) context set by call_llm); count_event(provider, "refusals"|"fallbacks"|"truncations"), record_estimate(step, estimate, cache_hit=False), usage_snapshot(provider) / usage_delta, get_usage_summary(), get_step_summary() — entries expose unpriced_calls and cost_known), and warn_once(key, *parts). llm_anthropic re-exports TruncatedResponse / LLMRefusalError.

docs.title: Preflight for every provider (utils/llm_config.check_llm_auth)
docs.text: Called by main() and the utils/call_llm.py self-test before any LLM call; returns False (after printing instructions) when the run cannot work: - ANTHROPIC → check_anthropic_auth() (above). - GEMINI → check_gemini_config(): google-genai installed (ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING) and >= 1.56 (ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED); retired model → WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (AI Studio alias) or ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED → False; Vertex: location not in gemini_vertex_locations(model) → WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION (lists the allowed locations), google.auth.default() must succeed (ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS: gcloud auth application-default login); else GEMINI_API_KEY required (ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS). Success → LLM_AUTH_OK. - OPENROUTER → check_openrouter_config(): OPENROUTER_API_KEY when the base URL is an openrouter.ai host (ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_KEY), OPENROUTER_MODEL (ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_MODEL); a catalog that cannot load → WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE (with the URL and error, e.g. a 404 from a proxy without /v1/models); a model missing from a loaded catalog → WARN_OPENROUTER_MODEL_UNKNOWN (continues). Success → LLM_AUTH_OK. - Other providers → True.

docs.title: Application Setup
docs.text: Chapter Description main.py Serves as the primary CLI entry point that parses runtime arguments, verifies LLM credentials, and initializes the execution state. It builds the SharedStore and triggers the PocketFlow DAG within a protected telemetry lifecycle.

docs.title: Pipeline Orchestration
docs.text: Chapter Description nodes.py Implements the discrete computation graph nodes that execute ingestion, context window budgeting, abstraction discovery, fact extraction, and chapter drafting. Each node follows PocketFlow's three-phase prep, exec, and post lifecycle. flow.py Constructs the declarative execution Directed Acyclic Graph using pocketflow.Flow via create_tutorial_flow(). It wires nodes with sequential and conditional transitions across single-pass, MapReduce, and deterministic topologies.

docs.title: LLM Gateway & Providers
docs.text: Chapter Description call_llm.py Acts as the centralized LLM dispatch gateway routing prompts to Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or OpenAI-compatible backends via call_llm(). It implements SHA-256 content-addressable response caching, refusal short-circuiting, and token usage accounting. llm_config.py Centralizes configuration, credential preflight checks, and context window limits across supported model providers via resolve_llm_settings(). It acts as the single source of truth for reasoning capabilities, endpoint targets, and output token reserves. thinking.py Defines standardized reasoning effort levels and resolves per-node thinking plans across LLM providers via build_thinking_plan(). It normalizes profiles and maps abstract effort tiers to provider-specific parameters using clamp_level(). token_utils.py Calculates token counts, safe input budgets, and dynamic tokenizer calibration ratios using BPE tokenization and provider feedback. It exposes count_tokens() and input_token_budget() while caching token operations in an LRU memory buffer. llm_common.py Provides provider-neutral accounting primitives, refusal memoization, and custom signals like TruncatedResponse and LLMRefusalError. It tracks workflow step metrics using Python's contextvars to ensure asynchronous and thread-safe usage aggregation. llm_anthropic.py Executes Claude model invocations using client-side streaming through call_anthropic() and manages Anthropic-specific reasoning effort parameters. It handles transient truncation recovery through ceiling escalation and models generation costs. llm_gemini.py Adapts Google Gemini models across AI Studio and Vertex AI backends through call_gemini(). It manages streaming communication, translates thinking configurations, calculates generation costs, and converts truncated completions into TruncatedResponse instances. llm_openrouter.py Dispatches completions to OpenRouter endpoints via SSE streaming in call_openrouter(). It dynamically adapts reasoning budgets, performs bounded HTTP retries for transient errors, and updates shared token ledger metrics.

docs.title: Repository Ingestion
docs.text: Chapter Description crawl_local_files.py Traverses local directory hierarchies using os.walk to extract source code into in-memory string buffers via crawl_local_files(). It evaluates hierarchical .gitignore rules and excludes unwanted paths to maintain parity with remote crawls. crawl_github_files.py Retrieves remote repository source trees using Git-over-SSH cloning or GitHub REST API traversals via crawl_github_files(). It applies size thresholds, .gitignore matching, and rate-limit backoffs to yield normalized file buffers. files.py Generates indexed directory tree representations from file collections and retrieves selective file slices by index. It provides deterministic formatting via build_directory_tree() and bounds retrieval via get_content_for_indices() for token-efficient prompts. exclude_patterns.py Defines the centralized glob exclusion catalog in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS to filter non-essential files, compilation artifacts, and sensitive credentials. It prevents context overflow and secret leakage across remote and local file crawlers.

docs.title: Fact Verification & Publishing
docs.text: Chapter Description facts.py Provides an AST-independent verification engine auditing LLM-extracted code assertions against verbatim source code via SourceIndex and ModuleTable. It verifies entity citations, manifest boundaries, and cross-module dependencies to prevent hallucinations. prompts.py Loads Markdown prompt templates and parses model responses containing YAML, facts, and file index ranges into structured dictionaries. It employs progressive degradation and safe loading to salvage malformed or truncated LLM completions. mkdocs.py Compiles Markdown chapters, verified source facts, and Mermaid dependency diagrams into standalone documentation or complete MkDocs Material sites. Entry points write_mkdocs_output() and write_standalone_output() handle navigation pruning, link normalization, and stale page deletion.

docs.title: Operational Infrastructure
docs.text: Chapter Description output.py Manages console output, ANSI styling, and timestamped file logging through emit(), emit_raw(), and configure_logging(). It routes messages through localized string catalogs and ensures UTF-8 stream compatibility across operating systems. i18n.py Manages user interface localization by detecting missing translations in strings.csv and auto-generating them with LLMs via auto_translate(). It safely persists localized catalogs using UTF-8-SIG encoding.

docs.title: flow.py
docs.text:
Source: flow.py

Following the token estimation, budgeting, and ratio calibration mechanics established in utils/token_utils.py, flow.py provides the declarative orchestration layer for the entire documentation pipeline. It compiles the discrete operational stages of codebase analysis, semantic abstraction, fact extraction, and chapter compilation into an executable Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) using the pocketflow workflow engine.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
flow.py defines the macro-level execution graph for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. The module exposes a single factory function, create_tutorial_flow(), which instantiates workflow nodes declared in nodes.py and wires them together using PocketFlow's domain-specific operator syntax. Through operator overloading (>> for sequential transitions and - "action" >> for dynamic conditional dispatch), flow.py establishes deterministic routing paths that adapt dynamically based on repository volume, token capacity, and operational generation mode.

The graph architecture accommodates three distinct execution topologies anchored at the ContextRouter node: 1. Direct Path ("direct"): Activated for small codebases that fit entirely within the target model's context window. It bypasses chunking and dispatches directly to IdentifyAbstractions to extract high-level architectural concepts in a single unified prompt. 2. Batch Path ("batch"): Activated when a repository exceeds direct context budgets. It engages a MapReduce topology, routing source files through MapAbstractions to extract modular domain concepts across clustered file subsets, which are then consolidated by ReduceAbstractions. 3. Deterministic Path ("deterministic"): Activated for structured generation modes (such as api-reference or deterministic layouts). It bypasses heuristic abstraction discovery to map files systematically via DeterministicFileMapper and extracts ground-truth symbols and dependencies via ExtractFacts.

These divergent pathways converge at key downstream integration nodes. The abstraction branches (IdentifyAbstractions and ReduceAbstractions) feed into AnalyzeRelationships to construct a unified dependency graph, which OrderChapters uses to sequence a didactic curriculum. In parallel, the deterministic branch streams ground-truth code citations from ExtractFacts directly into WriteChapters. WriteChapters reconciles the structural curriculum with verified source facts, drafting the individual documentation chapters before CombineTutorial serializes the final documentation site to disk.

flowchart TD subgraph Ingestion_and_Routing ["Ingestion and Routing"] fetchRepo["FetchRepo"] contextRouter{"ContextRouter"} end subgraph Abstraction_Pipeline ["Abstraction Analysis Pipeline"] identifyAbstractions["IdentifyAbstractions"] mapAbstractions["MapAbstractions"] reduceAbstractions["ReduceAbstractions"] analyzeRelationships["AnalyzeRelationships"] orderChapters["OrderChapters"] end subgraph Fact_Extraction_Pipeline ["Ground-Truth Verification Pipeline"] deterministicMapper["DeterministicFileMapper"] extractFacts["ExtractFacts"] end subgraph Synthesis_and_Export ["Synthesis and Export Pipeline"] writeChapters["WriteChapters"] combineTutorial["CombineTutorial"] end fetchRepo >> contextRouter contextRouter -- "direct" --> identifyAbstractions contextRouter -- "batch" --> mapAbstractions contextRouter -- "deterministic" --> deterministicMapper mapAbstractions >> reduceAbstractions identifyAbstractions >> analyzeRelationships reduceAbstractions >> analyzeRelationships analyzeRelationships >> orderChapters orderChapters >> writeChapters deterministicMapper >> extractFacts >> writeChapters writeChapters >> combineTutorial classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class fetchRepo entryNode class identifyAbstractions entryNode class deterministicMapper entryNode class writeChapters entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Constructs, configures, and returns the complete PocketFlow execution graph for the codebase analysis and documentation generation pipeline. It initializes all constituent nodes with operational retry and backoff thresholds, links them into sequential and conditional transitions, logs graph creation to the diagnostic log stream, and binds the flow execution root to FetchRepo.

The method is structured into four distinct execution phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Node Instantiation and Resilience Configuration
docs.text:
def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    extract_facts = ExtractFacts(max_retries=3, wait=10)  # one small call per file; the last attempt keeps what verifies
    # ...

In this phase, all node instances participating in the pipeline lifecycle are instantiated with specific retry parameters. Network-bound and LLM-dependent operations—such as MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper—are initialized with max_retries=5 and an exponential backoff interval of wait=20 seconds to handle rate-limiting (HTTP 429), gateway timeouts (HTTP 504), and temporary provider capacity exhaustion. In contrast, ExtractFacts receives a tailored resilience profile (max_retries=3, wait=10), reflecting its per-file execution scope where each attempt audits verifiable facts against the source code, retaining verified citations across transient failures. Local I/O and routing nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) require no remote inference retries and operate under default execution constraints.

docs.title: Phase 2: Ingestion and Context-Aware Fan-Out Routing
docs.text:
# ...
    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper
    # ...

This phase wires the entry point and establishes conditional branching. The sequence begins with fetch_repo >> context_router, passing the raw repository ingestion payload (cloned Git directory or crawled local tree) directly into the routing engine. ContextRouter evaluates the overall codebase volume against active model context windows and inspects the execution mode. Using PocketFlow's conditional syntax (node - action >> target), the router branches execution into one of three isolated processing tracks: emitting "direct" routes execution to identify_abstractions for small single-context analysis; emitting "batch" routes execution to map_abstractions for MapReduce chunking; and emitting "deterministic" routes execution to deterministic_mapper for structured file-to-chapter layouts.

docs.title: Phase 3: Abstraction Analysis and Curriculum Sequencing
docs.text:
# ...
    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters
    # ...

This phase manages the reduction and semantic synthesis of architectural concepts. If the batch path is chosen, map_abstractions streams chunked concept summaries into reduce_abstractions, which deduplicates and condenses entity models. Both identify_abstractions (from the direct path) and reduce_abstractions (from the batch path) converge on analyze_relationships. AnalyzeRelationships inspects the unified abstractions, resolves cross-cutting interfaces, and models architectural dependencies. Once the relationship graph is established, order_chapters digests the dependency topology to construct an incremental pedagogical curriculum. The ordered chapter list is then forwarded to the compilation engine, write_chapters.

docs.title: Phase 4: Fact Extraction Convergence, Assembly, and Graph Finalization
docs.text:
# ...
    deterministic_mapper >> extract_facts >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    emit_raw("DEBUG", "create_tutorial_flow | constructed PocketFlow execution graph", dest="LOG")
    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

This phase converges factual ground-truth with curriculum drafting and exports the graph. In parallel with the abstraction pipeline, the deterministic branch links deterministic_mapper sequentially to extract_facts, which audits source files line-by-line to extract verified assertions, symbols, and dependencies. Both the chapter sequence from order_chapters and the verified source facts from extract_facts converge at write_chapters, ensuring that LLM chapter drafting is anchored by concrete ground-truth citations. Once chapters are drafted, execution transitions to combine_tutorial to write static assets, normalize links, generate MkDocs configurations, and output Markdown documents. Finally, emit_raw() logs graph construction to the debug log file, and a new Flow object initialized with start=fetch_repo is returned to the caller.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * pocketflow.Flow: A fully wired, non-executed PocketFlow graph instance configured with FetchRepo as the root entry point.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions internally. Node instantiation and edge connection are validated syntactically at runtime by the pocketflow engine.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py:
from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# Initialize the workflow graph
flow = create_tutorial_flow()

# Execute the flow passing the shared runtime state dictionary
flow.run(shared_context)

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: flow.py orchestrates nodes that read from and write to a shared context dictionary passed through the pocketflow.Flow engine. The primary data structures and configuration parameters governing this module are documented below.

docs.title: Node Resilience and Retry Policies
docs.text:
The following table details the operational retry configurations defined in flow.py:

Node Variable Target Node Class max_retries wait (seconds) Primary Operational Rationale fetch_repo FetchRepo 0 (default) 0 (default) Local disk crawling or Git cloning; failures are deterministic and terminal. context_router ContextRouter 0 (default) 0 (default) In-memory token counting and mode inspection; no external network I/O. map_abstractions MapAbstractions 5 20 High-volume batch LLM prompts; guards against transient 429 and 5xx errors. reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions 5 20 Heavy multi-abstraction synthesis; protects against token context timeouts. identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions 5 20 Monolithic repository analysis; prone to extended chain-of-thought latency. analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships 5 20 Global graph modeling; retries on schema or JSON parsing failures. order_chapters OrderChapters 5 20 Pedagogical curriculum sorting; guards against malformed YAML index responses. write_chapters WriteChapters 5 20 Extended multi-page chapter generation; vulnerable to network read timeouts. combine_tutorial CombineTutorial 0 (default) 0 (default) Local file writing, link normalization, and MkDocs YAML synthesis. deterministic_mapper DeterministicFileMapper 5 20 LLM-assisted or rule-based module clustering in api-reference mode. extract_facts ExtractFacts 3 10 Granular per-file fact verification; lower retry count because verification persists.

docs.title: Routing Actions Schema
docs.text:
The conditional transitions originating from context_router evaluate string action markers emitted by ContextRouter.run(). The table below outlines these routing contracts:

Routing Action Key Target Node Activation Criteria Architectural Purpose "direct" IdentifyAbstractions Total repository tokens $\le$ model input token budget, and mode is heuristic (tutorial, etc.). Single-pass global abstraction discovery without file chunking. "batch" MapAbstractions Total repository tokens $>$ model input token budget, and mode is heuristic. MapReduce abstraction extraction across modular file slices. "deterministic" DeterministicFileMapper Execution mode is api-reference or deterministic layouts are requested. Strict 1:1 or 1:N file-to-chapter structural mapping.

docs.title: Shared State Context (PrepResult)
docs.text:

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Error handling within flow.py is configured declaratively rather than imperatively:

  • Stochastic Failure Recovery: By injecting max_retries and wait into node constructors, flow.py delegates transient error recovery to PocketFlow. When a node encounters rate limits, network disconnects, or malformed LLM responses, PocketFlow pauses execution for the configured wait interval and retries the node execution up to the designated retry limit.
  • Partial Fact Verification Resilience: The configuration for extract_facts = ExtractFacts(max_retries=3, wait=10) contains inline defense logic: # one small call per file; the last attempt keeps what verifies. In ExtractFacts, each file is audited independently. If repeated retries fail on a subset of files, the node does not abort the entire pipeline; instead, it retains all citations verified during prior passes and marks unparseable items as unparsed, allowing WriteChapters to proceed with verified data.
  • Fail-Fast Graph Termination: If any node completely exhausts its retry budget (e.g., persistent HTTP 401 authentication rejections, terminal provider refusals via LLMRefusalError, or unrecoverable syntax errors), PocketFlow halts graph traversal immediately and propagates the unhandled exception up to the root caller in main.py. This prevents empty, corrupt, or partially hallucinated documentation from being written to disk.

docs.text:

  • main.py — Application entry point that calls create_tutorial_flow(), initializes shared runtime parameters, and triggers flow.run().
  • utils/output.py — Emits telemetry and diagnostic traces during graph assembly via emit_raw().
  • utils/facts.py — Ground-truth auditing engine executed within the extract_facts pipeline branch.
  • utils/token_utils.py — Provides token measurement and context window calculations consumed by ContextRouter during graph routing decisions.
  • utils/thinking.py — Manages cognitive reasoning effort budgets assigned to the LLM nodes instantiated across the flow.

docs.title: main.py
docs.text:
Source: main.py

Following the orchestration framework detailed in flow.py—which compiles repository ingestion, abstraction modeling, fact auditing, and chapter composition into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)—the main.py module serves as the command-line interface (CLI) entry point and system bootstrapper for the entire Codebase-Knowledge-Builder application. It translates raw shell arguments, environment variables, and provider settings into the runtime state required by the downstream graph pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
main.py provides the operational boundary between external execution environments (such as terminal shells, automation scripts, and CI/CD containers) and internal graph-processing pipelines. It orchestrates preflight validation, runtime configuration detection, subsystem initialization, credential verification, and graceful shutdown handling. By decoupling CLI option parsing from pipeline execution, main.py ensures that all external options—ranging from repository targets and include/exclude globs to reasoning token budgets and incremental cache policies—are fully validated and normalized before any compute-intensive or billable model inference tasks execute.

The module manages critical pre-flight operations that prevent silent failures and resource waste. It inspects CLI input strings for accidental shell quoting issues that could inadvertently swallow options, resolves documentation generation modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), detects and binds LLM provider credentials via utils/llm_config.py, and builds the per-node reasoning plan via utils/thinking.py. Furthermore, it configures centralized logging and terminal telemetry via utils/output.py, synchronizes localization catalogs via utils/i18n.py, and manages incremental cache invalidations alongside ground-truth fact stores via utils/facts.py.

At runtime, main.py packages all validated parameters, target specifications, pattern sets, and empty workflow accumulator slots into a single shared dictionary (shared). It then initializes the PocketFlow graph using create_tutorial_flow() from flow.py and triggers execution. Regardless of whether the execution succeeds, fails, or is interrupted, a robust try...finally block guarantees that full token usage ledgers, cost approximations, and diagnostic logs are emitted before resources are released via shutdown().

docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments() -> tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]:

Description: Configures and executes the command-line argument parser for the application. It establishes mutually exclusive ingestion source groups (--repo vs. --dir), configures target output directories, sets path inclusion and exclusion globs, specifies file size thresholds, and sets localized generation languages. Additionally, it binds complex LLM execution flags such as thinking effort levels, reasoning profiles, per-node overrides, context token ceilings, batching thresholds, and documentation generation modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk).

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A 2-tuple containing the configured argparse.ArgumentParser instance and the parsed argparse.Namespace populated with options.

Example: 

parser, args = parse_arguments()
# Access parsed CLI options
print(f"Target repository: {args.repo}, Output mode: {args.mode}")


def parse_arguments():
    """Parse and return command-line arguments."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Source: --repo or --dir (mutually exclusive but not required if --cleanup is used)
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache files. Can be used standalone or after a run.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
    # Add language parameter for multi-language support
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="english", help="Language for the generated tutorial (default: english).")
    # Add use_cache parameter to control LLM caching
    parser.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled).")
    # Add max_abstraction_num parameter to control the number of abstractions
    parser.add_argument("--max-abstractions", type=int, default=10, help="Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10).")
    # Add thinking_level parameter for LLM reasoning capabilities
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-level",
        default=None,
        type=_thinking_level_arg,
        metavar="{" + ",".join(THINKING_LEVELS) + "}",
        help="Global thinking effort for EVERY LLM call. Overrides --thinking-profile. 'default' (or empty) = model default. "
        "Mapped per provider: Anthropic effort (thinking budget on Haiku 4.5), Gemini thinking_level (3.x) / thinking budget (2.5), "
        "OpenRouter reasoning effort or budget, Ollama reasoning effort (clamped to what the model supports).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-profile",
        default="auto",
        type=str.lower,
        choices=THINKING_PROFILES,
        help="Per-node thinking effort profile (default: auto = balanced on ANTHROPIC, GEMINI and OPENROUTER, off elsewhere). "
        "economy/balanced/quality/max give reasoning-heavy nodes (abstractions, relationships) more effort than "
        "mechanical ones (summaries, translation), adjusted per --mode. off = model defaults.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-override",
        nargs="+",
        metavar="NODE=LEVEL",
        help=f"Per-node thinking level overrides, highest precedence (e.g., write_chapters=high identify_abstractions=xhigh). NODE: {', '.join(NODE_KEYS)}.",
    )
    # Add max_tokens parameter
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically)."
    )

    # --- Documentation Mode & Generation Styles ---
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"],
        default="tutorial",
        help="Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--advanced", action="store_true", help="Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced.")
    parser.add_argument("--mkdocs", action="store_true", help="Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--incremental",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force-rebuild", action="store_true", help="Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)."
    )

    # Add batching parameters
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size.")
    # Debug mode
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output.")

    return parser, parser.parse_args()

The argument parser establishes the complete operational parameters of the system. Mutually exclusive groups guarantee that a run targets either a remote GitHub URL or a local directory path, while permitting standalone invocations of --cleanup. Advanced flags like --thinking-level, --thinking-profile, and --thinking-override delegate parsing and type coercion to helper utilities like _thinking_level_arg and utils/thinking.py. The parser also handles backwards compatibility via --advanced (which maps to --mode advanced) and enforces constraints around API reference generation features, including --incremental and --force-rebuild.

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Resolves conflicts between legacy flags and explicit generation modes, and deterministically derives the project name from repository URLs or local filesystem paths when omitted by the user.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments containing options such as advanced, mode, name, dir, and repo.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple containing the normalized generation mode string (mode) and the resolved project identifier (project_name).

Example: 

mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)
# mode -> "advanced", project_name -> "my-repo"


def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name

This function resolves the documentation generation style. If the user passes the legacy --advanced flag while simultaneously specifying a non-default --mode (e.g., api-reference), it warns the user via emit() and overrides the mode to advanced. If the project name is not explicitly passed via -n/--name, it safely parses local absolute paths via os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir)) or extracts the trailing URL component from git targets, stripping trailing slashes and the .git suffix. If no source target is supplied, it falls back to "project".

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None], project_name: str) -> dict[str, any]:

Description: Constructs the primary shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow graph nodes during execution. It populates all initial configuration options, sets up file inclusion and exclusion sets, injects model reasoning plans, and initializes mutable accumulator keys for downstream pipeline stages.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI argument values. * github_token (str | None): Authenticated GitHub personal access token, if resolved. * mode (str): Resolved documentation generation mode. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of workflow node keys to reasoning effort tiers. * project_name (str): Resolved project identifier.

Returns: * dict[str, any]: The initialized state dictionary conformant to the PocketFlow shared state contract.

Example: 

shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
# Passed to pocketflow graph execution
tutorial_flow.run(shared)


def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": project_name,  # Resolved once in main so logs, --force-rebuild and output agree
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities: global level (legacy) + per-node plan (utils/thinking.py)
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "thinking_plan": thinking_plan,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The shared store functions as the central communication bus across the Directed Acyclic Graph instantiated by create_tutorial_flow(). File exclusion patterns are computed by taking the union of the built-in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS from utils/exclude_patterns.py and any user-provided exclusion globs passed via CLI flags. Empty output slots (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters, and final_output_dir) are initialized as mutable data structures, allowing nodes in nodes.py to inspect and populate results as execution moves through the graph.

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Inspects runtime environment variables and settings to determine the active LLM provider, target model identifier, endpoint URL, API credentials, and maximum token context window length.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments, used specifically to evaluate --max-tokens overrides.

Returns: * tuple: A 5-tuple structured as (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length).

Example: 

provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
print(f"Provider: {provider}, Context Window: {context_length}")


def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length

This helper wraps resolve_llm_settings() from utils/llm_config.py. If the user explicitly provided --max-tokens on the command line, that integer takes precedence. Otherwise, it delegates context resolution to get_model_context_length(), which queries provider endpoints or applies static fallback defaults. This ensures that downstream batching decisions in ContextRouter have an accurate token budget to evaluate against repository size.

docs.title: resolve_thinking_plan()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_thinking_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]:

Description: Compiles the per-node thinking/reasoning plan from user CLI options prior to terminal subsystem initialization. It guarantees side-effect-free execution so that early string translations can use the resolved reasoning levels.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments containing options such as thinking_override, thinking_level, thinking_profile, and mode flags.

Returns: * tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]: A 3-tuple containing: 1. The resolved profile name (str). 2. The thinking plan mapping node names to reasoning tiers (dict[str, str | None]). 3. A list of any invalid override tokens detected (list[str]).

Example: 

thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
# thinking_plan -> {"translate_strings": "minimal", "write_chapters": "high", ...}


def resolve_thinking_plan(args):
    """Build the per-node thinking plan from --thinking-override / --thinking-level / --thinking-profile.

    Pure (no emit): runs before init_output(). Validation messages come from _validate_thinking_args().

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict, list[str]]: (resolved profile name, {node_key: level | None}, invalid override strings)
    """
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, invalid = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    profile = "global" if args.thinking_level else resolve_profile_name(args.thinking_profile, resolve_llm_settings()[0])
    return profile, build_thinking_plan(profile, mode, args.thinking_level, overrides), invalid

This function computes the reasoning configuration before logging is initialized. It isolates parsing logic from the terminal emission system to avoid circular dependencies during startup. By obtaining the resolved level for translate_strings early, the application can initialize the output subsystem using the correct reasoning tier for automated translation calls in utils/i18n.py.

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str, thinking_profile: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None]) -> None:

Description: Emits an operational configuration summary banner to the console and log files, detailing active targets, LLM settings, token ratio calibrations, batching thresholds, and caching options.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode. * provider (str): Active LLM provider name. * model_name (str): Active model identifier. * endpoint_url (str): Target provider API endpoint. * context_length (int): Token limit for the context window. * log_file (str): Path to the generated persistent run log file. * thinking_profile (str): Resolved reasoning profile name. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Full per-node thinking configuration.

Returns: * None

Example: 

display_config(
    args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url,
    context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan
)


def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_PROFILE", value=thinking_profile)
    if any(thinking_plan.values()):
        emit("CFG_THINKING_PLAN", value=describe_plan(thinking_plan, mode))
    emit("CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT", value=describe_thinking_support(provider, model_name))
    emit("CFG_TOKEN_RATIO", value=describe_token_ratio())
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block

The configuration banner outputs localized diagnostic information via emit() and get() from utils/output.py. It displays runtime provider characteristics, formatted context lengths, thinking profile settings, and dynamic token ratio estimates calculated by utils/token_utils.py. It also dynamically formats parameter values based on the active mode (for example, showing CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX when --mode api-reference is set, since abstraction limits are bypassed during deterministic module mapping).

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: The primary entry point and orchestrator for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder runtime. It coordinates argument parsing, shell quoting validation, output subsystem initialization, provider credential checks, cache and fact pruning, shared store setup, graph execution, and final telemetry reporting.

docs.title: Phase 1: Argument Parsing and Preflight Reasoning Setup
docs.text:
parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # Translation of missing strings is an LLM call: deferred until arguments and credentials are checked.
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=thinking_plan["translate_strings"],
        debug=args.debug,
        auto_translate=False,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
    _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)
The application first parses command-line arguments and constructs the thinking plan. It initializes the output subsystem with auto_translate=False to defer model inference until authentication credentials have been verified. Next, it evaluates user inputs using _check_quoting_errors() to prevent shell quoting bugs from swallowing flags, and validates thinking arguments using _validate_thinking_args().

docs.title: Phase 2: Standalone Cleanup and Ingestion Target Validation
docs.text:
# Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    # Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if the configured provider cannot authenticate
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    translate_missing_strings()
    notice_legacy_cache()
The orchestrator checks if --cleanup was invoked without a target repository or directory; if so, it triggers cache and log removal via _run_cleanup() and terminates immediately. For documentation runs, it verifies that either --dir or --repo was supplied. Before initiating repository crawling, it calls check_llm_auth() to verify provider credentials and fails fast if authentication is invalid. Once verified, it translates missing UI strings via translate_missing_strings() and warns about any deprecated cache files via notice_legacy_cache().

docs.title: Phase 3: Token Resolution and Mode Normalization
docs.text:
# Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)
This phase extracts the GitHub Personal Access Token from CLI arguments or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, emitting warnings if a remote repository is targeted without authentication (which risks rate-limiting). It then derives the project name and generation mode. It enforces mode constraints: incremental generation (--incremental) is restricted to --mode api-reference, and --force-rebuild is rejected unless --incremental is active.

docs.title: Phase 4: Cache Pruning and Incremental State Invalidation
docs.text:
# Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)
        # The verified-facts cache (ExtractFacts) lives in facts.json: docs/api/ under --mkdocs, else next to the pages
        for facts_file in (facts_path(output_base, project_name, True), facts_path(output_base, project_name, False)):
            if os.path.exists(facts_file):
                os.remove(facts_file)
                emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED_FACTS", path=facts_file)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False
If --force-rebuild is active, the orchestrator invalidates caches by removing .doc_cache_manifest.json and purging any verified facts JSON files located via facts_path(). It also suppresses flags that are incompatible with the selected mode, such as unsetting --force-batch in API reference mode (which processes files deterministically rather than via batching).

shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
