docs.title: _thinking_level_arg()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_level_arg(value: str) -> str | None:

Description: Type-converter and validator function designed for argparse integration with the --thinking-level option. It normalizes input strings and maps sentinel empty values to None.

Parameters: * value (str): Raw CLI string value passed to --thinking-level.

Returns: * str | None: Validated thinking level string from THINKING_LEVELS, or None if "" or "default" was supplied.

Raises: * argparse.ArgumentTypeError: Raised if the argument string does not match any recognized level in THINKING_LEVELS.

Example: 

# Internal invocation by argparse
parser.add_argument("--thinking-level", type=_thinking_level_arg)


def _thinking_level_arg(value):
    """argparse type for --thinking-level: a level from THINKING_LEVELS; '' or 'default' → None (model default)."""
    level = value.strip().lower()
    if level in ("", "default"):
        return None
    if level not in THINKING_LEVELS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid choice: {value!r} (choose from {', '.join(THINKING_LEVELS)}, default)")
    return level

This helper sanitizes input values passed to the --thinking-level CLI argument. By trimming surrounding whitespace and converting to lowercase, it normalizes user inputs before validation. Passing "default" or an empty string returns None, allowing the model's native default reasoning behavior to take effect. If an unrecognized string is passed, it raises an argparse.ArgumentTypeError containing the list of allowed options from THINKING_LEVELS (imported from utils/thinking.py), causing argparse to halt parsing and display a usage error.

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

Description: Scans pattern arguments (--exclude and --include) to detect shell quoting mistakes where whitespace or quote issues caused subsequent CLI options to be merged into pattern strings.

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The parser instance, used to dynamically introspect registered flag strings. * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments containing include and exclude pattern lists.

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Exits with status code 1 via sys.exit(1) if a quoting error is detected.

Example: 

_check_quoting_errors(parser, args)


def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)

Shell misquoting is a common source of user error in CLI tools that accept multiple arguments. For instance, inputting --exclude "target/* "src/*" --language Vietnamese can cause the shell to treat --language and Vietnamese as part of the --exclude pattern rather than distinct options. To prevent the application from silently ignoring flags, this function extracts all valid option strings from the ArgumentParser instance and checks if any pattern contains an embedded flag surrounded by spaces or at the end of the string. If a match is found, it emits ERROR_QUOTING with the offending pattern snippet and terminates execution.

docs.title: _validate_thinking_args()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _validate_thinking_args(args: argparse.Namespace, invalid_overrides: list[str]) -> None:

Description: Validates thinking effort configurations by catching malformed node overrides, identifying unused overrides for inactive workflow modes, and warning about precedence conflicts between global and per-profile settings.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments. * invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of invalid override tokens returned by resolve_thinking_plan().

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Exits with status code 1 via sys.exit(1) if invalid_overrides contains any values.

Example: 

_validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)


def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):
    """Report malformed --thinking-override values (fatal), overrides for nodes the mode never runs,
    and --thinking-level/--thinking-profile conflicts."""
    if invalid_overrides:
        emit("ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE", value=", ".join(invalid_overrides), nodes=", ".join(NODE_KEYS), levels=", ".join(THINKING_LEVELS))
        sys.exit(1)
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, _ = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    unused = [node for node in overrides if node not in MODE_NODES[mode]]
    if unused:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED", nodes=", ".join(unused), mode=mode, active=", ".join(MODE_NODES[mode]))
    if args.thinking_level and args.thinking_profile != "auto":
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE", level=args.thinking_level, profile=args.thinking_profile)

This helper ensures consistency across thinking effort configurations. If any malformed override strings were detected during parsing (such as missing = delimiters, unknown node names, or invalid level values), it emits an ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE diagnostic and halts execution. It also cross-references parsed overrides with MODE_NODES from utils/thinking.py; if a user specifies an override for a node that is never executed by the selected --mode, it logs a warning. Finally, it warns the user if a global --thinking-level is set alongside a non-default --thinking-profile, noting that the global setting overrides profile configurations.

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Deletes persistent cache files and removes the runtime log directory.

Returns: * None

Example: 

# Standalone execution
if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
    _run_cleanup()
    return


def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in [cache_file, f"{cache_file}.tmp", LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE, f"{TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE}.tmp"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

This function cleans up local runtime artifacts. It iterates through primary cache paths—including llm_cache_v2.json (cache_file), temporary atomic write files (.tmp), deprecated v1 cache files (LEGACY_CACHE_FILE), and token ratio calibration files (TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE). For each existing file, it attempts deletion via os.remove(), logging successes or failures. It then resolves the logging directory from the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs") and removes it using shutil.rmtree().

docs.title: _emit_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _emit_usage_summary() -> None:

Description: Queries the token accounting subsystem in utils/llm_common.py and displays a structured summary table covering total API calls, token volumes, cache hits, estimated dollar costs, refusals, and per-step breakdowns.

Returns: * None

Example: 

try:
    _emit_usage_summary()
except Exception as e:
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")


def _emit_usage_summary():
    """Emit accumulated token usage and estimated cost per provider, then the per-step breakdown."""
    from utils.llm_common import get_step_summary, get_usage_summary
    from utils.token_utils import emit_step_usage, format_cost

    for name, usage in get_usage_summary().items():
        emit(
            "LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY",
            provider=name,
            models=", ".join(usage["models"]) or "-",
            calls=f"{usage['calls']:,}",
            input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
            output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
            thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
            cache_read=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
            cache_write=f"{usage['cache_write']:,}",
            cost=format_cost(usage),
            refusals=usage["refusals"],
            fallbacks=usage["fallbacks"],
            truncations=usage["truncations"],
        )
    steps = get_step_summary()
    if steps:
        emit("LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER")
        for step, usage in steps.items():
            emit_step_usage("LLM_USAGE_STEP", step, usage)

This function reports LLM consumption metrics collected during the run. It imports tracking helpers lazily to avoid circular imports during startup, iterating over the usage metrics returned by get_usage_summary(). For each provider, it emits metrics detailing total API requests, prompt tokens, generation tokens, thinking/reasoning tokens, prompt cache reads/writes, estimated costs computed via format_cost(), and exception counters (such as refusals, fallbacks, and truncations). If step-level usage was tracked, it prints a breakdown via emit_step_usage(), giving visibility into which pipeline nodes consumed the most resources.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
main.py applies defensive validation patterns at startup to intercept misconfigurations before expensive model calls or disk operations occur:

  • Quoting Error Interception (_check_quoting_errors): Catches shell quoting mistakes in pattern lists (such as --exclude "dir/* "other/*"). It inspects pattern values for registered CLI option strings and terminates execution with an ERROR_QUOTING message, preventing subsequent flags from being silently ignored.
  • Fail-Fast Authentication (check_llm_auth): Calls check_llm_auth() to verify provider credentials and reachability before crawling files. If authentication fails, the process terminates immediately with exit code 1 rather than failing mid-pipeline during chapter generation.
  • Thinking Validation and Sanitization (_validate_thinking_args): Rejects malformed per-node override strings via _validate_thinking_args(), displaying supported nodes (NODE_KEYS) and reasoning tiers (THINKING_LEVELS). It also warns if overrides target nodes that are not used by the selected --mode, or if a global --thinking-level conflicts with a --thinking-profile.
  • Incremental Cache Consistency: Restricts --incremental caching to --mode api-reference. If passed with other modes, it logs a warning (WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY) and disables the flag. It also verifies that --force-rebuild is only used alongside --incremental, exiting with an error if used independently.
  • Safe Cleanup Exception Handling (_run_cleanup): Catches and logs filesystem errors using CLEANUP_FAILED when removing cache files or log folders, allowing cleanup to proceed through remaining files rather than failing on the first error.
  • Guaranteed Teardown Telemetry (main try...finally): Wraps flow execution in a try...finally block. Regardless of whether the pipeline completes successfully, fails with an unhandled exception, or is canceled via keyboard interrupt, _emit_usage_summary() outputs token consumption metrics and costs before shutdown() releases log file handles.

docs.title: nodes.py
docs.text:
Source: nodes.py

Following the orchestration graph definitions established in flow.py and the operational bootstrapping managed by main.py, nodes.py houses the executable node implementations for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It defines the discrete steps within the PocketFlow pipeline that ingest source repositories, evaluate token budgets, discover domain abstractions, verify code facts, draft instructional chapters, and package final documentation artifacts.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
nodes.py implements the core computation graph nodes inheriting from PocketFlow's Node and BatchNode base classes. Each node follows a strict lifecycle lifecycle: prep() extracts and formats state parameters from the shared execution dictionary (shared), exec() runs the primary transformation or LLM invocation (often shielded by retry logic via the safe_exec decorator), and post() mutates the shared pipeline state with downstream data structures. The module bridges high-level pipeline control with underlying utility subsystems, interfacing directly with remote/local repository crawlers, prompt templating, token counting, fact verification engines, and documentation compilers.

The execution topology divides into three primary pathways managed dynamically at runtime: 1. Direct Path: Used when the cumulative codebase token count comfortably fits inside the LLM input token budget, extracting abstractions directly from the full concatenated source files. 2. Batch Path: Applied when repository token volume exceeds single-prompt safety thresholds, partitioning files into directory-aligned batches, mapping partial abstractions across batches, and reducing them into a consolidated domain model. 3. Deterministic Path: Triggered under api-reference mode, skipping fuzzy abstraction discovery in favor of a 1:1 file-to-chapter mapping with rigorous AST-independent fact auditing.

The diagram below illustrates the node lifecycle, execution topologies, and inter-node data dependencies across the system:

docs.title: FetchRepo
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class FetchRepo(Node):

Description: The primary entry-point node for the pipeline. It derives project identification names and executes source code ingestion against either a remote GitHub URL or a local filesystem directory, filtering targets based on configured inclusion and exclusion wildcards.

docs.title: FetchRepo.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Normalizes configuration properties from the shared store, derives the default project name from Git URLs or folder basenames if omitted, and packages crawling parameters into an execution configuration dictionary.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow state dictionary containing CLI options and configuration flags.

Returns: * dict: Parameter dictionary containing repo_url, local_dir, token, include_patterns, exclude_patterns, max_file_size, and use_relative_paths.

Example: 

class FetchRepo(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
        local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
        project_name = shared.get("project_name")

        if not project_name:
            # Basic name derivation from URL or directory
            if repo_url:
                project_name = repo_url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
            else:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(local_dir))
            shared["project_name"] = project_name

        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG", f"FetchRepo prep | project_name='{project_name}' | source='{shared.get('repo_url') or shared.get('local_dir', '.')}'", dest="LOG"
        )

        # Get file patterns directly from shared
        include_patterns = shared["include_patterns"]
        exclude_patterns = shared["exclude_patterns"]
        max_file_size = shared["max_file_size"]

        return {
            "repo_url": repo_url,
            "local_dir": local_dir,
            "token": shared.get("github_token"),
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "max_file_size": max_file_size,
            "use_relative_paths": True,
        }

The method inspects repo_url and local_dir to populate missing project identifiers before extraction occurs. It logs debug telemetry indicating the ingestion source and packages inclusion and exclusion globs alongside size constraints into a dictionary. This prepared dictionary ensures that subsequent network or disk crawling functions operate over sanitized parameters without altering the shared store directly during preparation.

docs.title: FetchRepo.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Dispatches ingestion to crawl_github_files.py or crawl_local_files.py depending on whether repo_url is provided, transforming the decoded file mapping into an indexed list of path and content tuples.

Parameters: * prep_res (dict): The crawling parameters returned by FetchRepo.prep().

Returns: * list[tuple[str, str]]: A list of 2-tuples containing relative file paths and UTF-8 decoded source content strings.

Raises: * ValueError: If no matching source files are identified after applying inclusion/exclusion filters.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}", dest="LOG")

        if prep_res["repo_url"]:
            emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
            result = crawl_github_files(
                repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
                token=prep_res["token"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )
        else:
            emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])

            result = crawl_local_files(
                directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )

        # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
        files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
        if len(files_list) == 0:
            raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")

        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE COMPLETE | node=FetchRepo | files_found={len(files_list)}", dest="LOG")
        return files_list

The method branches on the presence of a repository URL, dispatching to crawl_github_files for remote repository retrieval or crawl_local_files for local filesystem crawls. Once retrieval finishes, it converts the underlying dictionary structure into an ordered list of (path, content) tuples. An explicit emptiness check enforces fail-fast error handling by raising a ValueError if all candidate files were excluded or missing, preventing subsequent nodes from attempting inference on an empty payload.

docs.title: FetchRepo.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: dict, exec_res: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:

Description: Persists the extracted list of file tuples directly to the shared store under the "files" key.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (dict): The output produced during prep(). * exec_res (list[tuple[str, str]]): The list of parsed (file_path, content) tuples from exec().

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["files"] = exec_res  # List of (path, content) tuples

This method commits the harvested source code array into shared memory. By storing the source code as indexed tuples, downstream nodes can reference files using zero-based integer identifiers, reducing prompt token footprints across analysis operations.

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ContextRouter(Node):

Description: Evaluates cumulative token capacity against model context constraints, prompt template footprints, and safety reserves. Dynamically selects between direct analysis, batch-mode MapReduce, or deterministic 1:1 API mappings.

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

The preparation phase measures prompt overhead and content token volumes across multiple sub-phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Mode Check & Directory Tree Construction
docs.text:
def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            # One chapter per file, one page call each: no routing budget is needed.
            emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
            return ("deterministic", files_data, 0, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)
The method resolves the model context window ceiling using resolve_max_tokens and generates an indexed directory tree string via build_directory_tree. If execution is configured for api-reference mode, token capacity checks are bypassed entirely, immediately routing to the "deterministic" topology since documentation is compiled per individual file without needing full repository context consolidation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Prompt Overhead Calculation
docs.text:
# --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
        # 1. Prompt templates: check both IA/MA (for batching) and WC (for chapter writing)
        #    Use the largest template across all modes as worst-case estimate
        prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
        max_template_tokens = 0
        for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"]:
            for template_name in ["map_abstractions.md", "identify_abstractions.md", "draft_chapters.md"]:
                template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, template_name)
                if os.path.exists(template_path):
                    with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        t = count_tokens(f.read())
                    max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)

        # 2. Directory tree (shared across IA, MA, and WC prompts)
        tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)

        # 3. Chapter listing estimate (used in WC draft_chapters prompts)
        #    Format: "N. basename (doc: path.md)" per file
        chapter_listing_estimate = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {os.path.basename(path)} (doc: {path}.md)" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data))
        listing_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_listing_estimate)

        prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens
        emit(
            "CAPACITY_PROMPT_OVERHEAD",
            total=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            template=f"{max_template_tokens:,}",
            tree=f"{tree_tokens:,}",
            listing=f"{listing_tokens:,}",
        )
The method computes the worst-case structural prompt overhead by surveying all Markdown prompt templates across available modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk) and identifying the maximum template token count. It measures the token cost of the generated directory tree and synthesizes a simulated chapter listing string to estimate final drafting overhead. The sum of these values establishes prompt_overhead, which is broadcast via UI telemetry.

docs.title: Phase 3: Token Capacity Comparison & Route Selection
docs.text:
# --- Count file content tokens (batch-encoded; memoized for the nodes that re-count entries) ---
        file_token_map = count_tokens_many([f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data)])
        total_tokens = sum(file_token_map)

        # --- Effective limit = context minus output reserve minus overhead ---
        # Reserve output for whichever consumer of this budget thinks more: IdentifyAbstractions
        # (direct route) or MapAbstractions (each batch is packed to effective_limit).
        safety_limit = min(
            input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")),
            input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "map_abstractions")),
        )
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

        if total_tokens > effective_limit and force_batch:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_EXCEEDS_FORCE",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        elif total_tokens > effective_limit:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_EXCEEDS",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        elif force_batch:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_FITS_FORCE",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        else:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_FITS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}"
            )
            return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

        return (
            "batch",
            files_data,
            effective_limit,
            shared.get("batch_size", 50),
            file_token_map,
            count_tokens,
            directory_tree,
        )
The method batch-encodes file contents using count_tokens_many and aggregates total tokens. It resolves reasoning reserves via input_token_budget for both direct and batch abstractions, choosing the tighter bound and subtracting prompt overhead to compute effective_limit. If the codebase exceeds this limit or --force-batch is active, it returns a 7-tuple selecting the "batch" route; otherwise, it returns a 7-tuple selecting "direct".

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]:

Description: Passes through scalar route decisions ("direct" or "deterministic"), or executes directory-grouped token-bounded bin-packing when operating in "batch" mode to produce balanced file batches.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The routing payload returned by ContextRouter.prep().

Returns: * str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]: Either the literal strings "direct" / "deterministic", or a list of batches where each batch contains tuples of (original_index, path, content).

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, _directory_tree = prep_res
        # ...
        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            # Flush remaining files in this directory
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)
        # ...
        return batches

When batching, files are segregated by parent directory using defaultdict(list). Traversal iterates through sorted directory groups, accumulating files until adding another entry would exceed either effective_limit tokens or batch_size file entries. Directories are kept isolated across batches to maintain contextual semantic coherence for downstream LLM prompts.

docs.title: ContextRouter.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: str | list) -> str:

Description: Persists the directory tree to the shared store and assigns file_batches if batching was selected, returning the route key to dictate DAG routing transitions in flow.py.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state. * prep_res (tuple): The preparation tuple containing the computed directory tree. * exec_res (str | list): The route name string or the packed file batches.

Returns: * str: The dynamic route action name ("direct", "deterministic", or "batch").

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ContextRouter post | route={'batch' if isinstance(exec_res, list) else exec_res}", dest="LOG")
        # Store the directory tree built during prep() for EVERY route: draft_chapters and
        # group_modules prompts read shared["directory_tree"] on direct/deterministic routes too.
        shared["directory_tree"] = prep_res[-1]
        if exec_res == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if exec_res == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"
        shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
        return "batch"

The method sets shared["directory_tree"] unconditionally so downstream prompts across all routes can access layout metadata. It then acts as a PocketFlow action router, returning string literals that direct flow transitions.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):

Description: Designed for api-reference generation. Filters out non-source files, identifies configuration manifests, builds a 1:1 module abstraction mapping for all valid source files, and sorts chapters by directory depth.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple[str, bool, str | None, int]:

Description: Formats an indexed code file inventory, excluding empty or whitespace-only files, and constructs a classification prompt for LLM evaluation.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow dictionary.

Returns: * tuple[str, bool, str | None, int]: A tuple containing (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Example: 

class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        # Empty/whitespace-only files (e.g. bare __init__.py) are left out: post() skips unlisted indices,
        # so they are never documented instead of flipping in and out with the LLM's answer.
        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data) if content.strip()])

        prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")
        return prompt, shared.get("use_cache", True), resolve_thinking_level(shared, "filter_files"), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)

The method filters candidate files by verifying that content.strip() evaluates to a truthy value, omitting empty files like blank __init__.py markers. It uses build_code_file_filter_prompt from prompts.py to instruct the LLM to separate genuine code files from manifests and auxiliary assets.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:

Description: Invokes the LLM to categorize files, parses YAML response arrays, and resolves file index boundaries for both executable source code and package manifests.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The parameters compiled by DeterministicFileMapper.prep().

Returns: * tuple[list[int], list[int]]: A 2-tuple containing (code_indices, manifest_indices).

Example: 

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
        emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="filter_files")
        parsed = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # {code: [...], manifests: [...]}; a bare list (older reply shape) is the code list
        code = parsed.get("code") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
        manifests = parsed.get("manifests") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else []
        indices = [idx for entry in (code if isinstance(code, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
        manifest_indices = [idx for entry in (manifests if isinstance(manifests, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
        return indices, manifest_indices

The method passes the generated prompt to call_llm under the "filter_files" execution step. It processes the YAML response using parse_yaml_response and expands potential index ranges or scalar integers using parse_file_indices. If the model returns an older flat list structure instead of a mapping containing code and manifests keys, it degrades gracefully by assigning the flat list to code.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: tuple) -> str:

Description: Constructs deterministic module abstractions for each included source file, separates manifest file indices for factual dependency auditing, and sorts chapters by directory nesting depth (deepest first).

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): The prepared prompt payload. * exec_res (tuple): The 2-tuple of (code_indices, manifest_indices).

Returns: * str: Returns the string literal "default".

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        files = shared.get("files", [])
        code_indices, manifest_indices = exec_res
        valid_indices = set(code_indices)
        # Manifests are read by ExtractFacts (declared package names and path aliases), never documented as pages
        shared["manifest_files"] = sorted(
            {idx for idx in manifest_indices if 0 <= idx < len(files) and idx not in valid_indices and files[idx][1].strip()}
        )
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, content) in enumerate(files):
            # Re-check emptiness: the LLM can return an index it was not shown (e.g. a contiguous range)
            if idx not in valid_indices or not content.strip():
                emit("SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE", path=file_path)
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.basename(file_path)
            # Forward slashes everywhere original_path is shown (nav dir labels, index) — the crawler keeps os.sep
            doc_path = file_path.replace(os.sep, "/")

            modules.append({"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{doc_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": doc_path})
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        # Sort chapter order by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical).
        shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
            chapter_order,
            key=lambda idx: (
                -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
                modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
            ),
        )
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        emit("DONE_DETERMINISTIC_MAPPER", count=len(modules))
        return "default"

The method populates shared["manifest_files"] with indices of project manifests (e.g., package.json, Cargo.toml), excluding them from standalone documentation. Each valid code file is assigned a single-item abstraction dictionary. The generated chapter_order list is sorted based on descending path separator count, ensuring leaf and utility modules are documented prior to higher-level orchestrator files.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class IdentifyAbstractions(Node):

Description: The direct abstraction discovery engine. Used when the full repository source fits within input token boundaries, prompting the model to identify major software architecture components in a single pass.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Measures token budgets, concatenates source files up to the model safety ceiling using an internal helper, builds a directory tree, and compiles execution parameters into a 12-element tuple.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * tuple: A 12-element tuple containing context string, directory tree, total files count, project name, language, cache flag, max abstractions, thinking level, advanced mode, max tokens, mode, and context token count.

Example: 

class IdentifyAbstractions(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")

        # ... calls nested create_llm_context(files_data) ...
        context, context_tokens = create_llm_context(files_data)
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"IdentifyAbstractions prep | context_tokens={context_tokens:,} | files={len(files_data)}", dest="LOG")
        return (
            context,
            directory_tree,
            len(files_data),
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            max_abstraction_num,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
            context_tokens,
        )

The method resolves the thinking level and max token boundaries, using the nested helper create_llm_context to safely concatenate source text without overflowing the reasoning-adjusted token ceiling. It returns a parameter tuple that isolates execution logic from direct mutations of the shared dictionary.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[dict]:

Description: Formats the abstraction identification prompt with localized instructions, invokes the LLM, parses the resulting YAML response, and validates that abstraction names, descriptions, and file index bindings conform to internal schema specifications.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The 12-element tuple generated by prep().

Returns: * list[dict]: A list of validated abstraction dictionaries, each containing "name", "description", and "files".

Raises: * ValueError: If the response does not parse into a list or contains items missing required schema keys.

Example: 

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        (
            context, directory_tree, total_files_count, project_name, language,
            use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode,
            max_tokens, mode, context_tokens,
        ) = prep_res

        # ... format prompt using load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions") ...
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="identify_abstractions"
        )

        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        if not isinstance(abstractions, list):
            raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

        validated_abstractions = []
        for item in abstractions:
            if not isinstance(item, dict) or not all(k in item for k in ["name", "description", "file_indices"]):
                raise ValueError(f"Missing keys in abstraction item: {item}")
            # ... validate indices ...
            validated_abstractions.append(
                {"name": item["name"], "description": item["description"], "files": item["files"]}
            )
        return validated_abstractions

The method injects target language rules into the prompt template and tracks prompt token estimation via log_token_estimation. After invoking call_llm, it evaluates the YAML array structure, sanitizes file index bounds, expands hyphenated ranges ("0-3"), and eliminates duplicate or invalid file references.

Description: Stores the validated list of domain abstraction dictionaries into shared["abstractions"].

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

The method commits the abstraction definitions to shared["abstractions"], where downstream relationship analyzers and chapter ordering components consume them.

docs.title: MapAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class MapAbstractions(BatchNode):

Description: The mapping phase of the MapReduce abstraction discovery pipeline. Operates over discrete directory-aligned file batches concurrently or sequentially, identifying candidate concepts localized to each batch.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Iterates through shared["file_batches"] and compiles an iterable batch configuration dictionary for each chunk.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global state containing file_batches, project name, and thinking configuration.

Returns: * list[dict]: A list of item dictionaries ready for BatchNode execution.

Example: 

class MapAbstractions(BatchNode):
    def prep(self, shared):
        return [
            {
                "batch_index": i,
                "files": batch,
                "project_name": shared["project_name"],
                "language": shared.get("language", "english"),
                "use_cache": shared.get("use_cache", True),
                "thinking_level": resolve_thinking_level(shared, "map_abstractions"),
                "advanced_mode": shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
                "max_tokens": shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
                "directory_tree": shared.get("directory_tree", ""),
                "mode": shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
            }
            for i, batch in enumerate(shared["file_batches"])
        ]

The method maps each pre-calculated batch in shared["file_batches"] to an independent payload containing file entries, language parameters, and directory tree structure. This isolates each batch execution context during processing.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Formats the batch file context, requests partial abstractions from the LLM via prompts/common/map_abstractions.md, and validates file indices returned in the YAML response.

Parameters: * item (dict): The item configuration for a single batch chunk.

Returns: * list[dict]: Validated partial abstractions discovered within the file batch.

Example: 

    def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        emit("LLM_CALL_MAP_ABSTRACTIONS", batch_index=batch_index, file_count=len(files))

        context = ""
        for i, path, content in files:
            context += f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))
        # ... prompt formatting and call_llm ...
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="map_abstractions"
        )
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # ... validation ...
        return validated_abstractions

The method formats all batch files into an indexed context string and applies language hints before invoking call_llm under the "map_abstractions" step. The resulting YAML response is parsed, ensuring that returned indices match actual source files present in the codebase.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[list[dict]]) -> None:

Description: Flattens the nested lists of partial abstractions returned by all batch jobs, commits the aggregated list to shared["mapped_abstractions"], and prints token subtotal telemetry.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (list[dict]): The batch preparation list. * exec_res_list (list[list[dict]]): Aggregated lists of partial abstraction dictionaries from each executed batch.

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        all_abstractions = []
        for batch_abs in exec_res_list:
            all_abstractions.extend(batch_abs)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"MapAbstractions post | collected {len(all_abstractions)} partial abstractions", dest="LOG")
        shared["mapped_abstractions"] = all_abstractions
        emit_step_subtotals("map_abstractions")

The method aggregates partial abstractions across all processed batches into a single flat list stored in shared["mapped_abstractions"]. It then calls emit_step_subtotals to log running token usage and cost metrics for the map step.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ReduceAbstractions(Node):

Description: The reduction phase of the MapReduce abstraction discovery pipeline. Consolidates redundant, overlapping, or fragmented partial abstractions discovered by MapAbstractions into a cohesive set capped at max_abstraction_num.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Extracts mapped_abstractions from the shared state along with threshold limits and thinking levels, returning an execution tuple.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * tuple: A 9-element tuple packing mapped abstractions, project name, language, cache settings, max abstraction count, thinking level, advanced mode flag, token ceiling, and mode.

Example: 

class ReduceAbstractions(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        return (
            shared["mapped_abstractions"],
            shared["project_name"],
            shared.get("language", "english"),
            shared.get("use_cache", True),

The method extracts the raw partial abstractions collected by MapAbstractions and prepares parameters for prompt synthesis. It retrieves max_abstraction_num (defaulting to 10) to cap the final architecture size.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[dict]:

Description: Compiles candidate partial abstractions into an evaluation listing, prompts the LLM to deduplicate and consolidate the abstractions, and validates file index arrays in the parsed YAML response.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The parameters output by ReduceAbstractions.prep().

Returns: * list[dict]: Consolidated list of abstraction dictionaries bounded by max_abstraction_num.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        mapped_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode = prep_res

        context = ""
        for i, abs_obj in enumerate(mapped_abstractions):
            context += f"- Partial Abstraction {i}: {abs_obj['name']}\n  Description: {abs_obj['description']}\n  Files: {abs_obj['files']}\n\n"

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("reduce_abstractions", mode=mode)
        # ... prompt assembly and call_llm ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="reduce_abstractions")

        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # ... schema verification ...
        return validated_abstractions

The method assembles partial abstractions into a formatted text catalog and merges them using the reduce_abstractions.md prompt template. The parsed output is validated to verify that file indices reference valid integers, returning a pruned set of primary abstractions.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Assigns the consolidated abstractions to shared["abstractions"].

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): The preparation inputs. * exec_res (list[dict]): The final reduced abstraction dictionaries.

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["abstractions"] = exec_res

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class AnalyzeRelationships(Node):

Description: Evaluates dependency and architectural connections between identified abstractions using an even, two-pass token redistribution algorithm over representative source code snippets.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

The preparation logic handles token allocation across multiple sub-phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Setup & Token Budget Resolution
docs.text:
def prep(self, shared):
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "analyze_relationships")

        num_abstractions = len(abstractions)
        context = "Identified Abstractions:\n"
        all_relevant_indices = set()
        abstraction_info_for_prompt = []
        for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
            file_indices_str = ", ".join(map(str, abstr["files"]))
            info_line = f"- Index {i}: {abstr['name']} (Relevant file indices: [{file_indices_str}])\n  Description: {abstr['description']}"
            context += info_line + "\n"
            abstraction_info_for_prompt.append(f"{i} # {abstr['name']}")
            all_relevant_indices.update(abstr["files"])

        context += "\nRelevant File Snippets (per abstraction, budget-aware):\n"
        max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
        safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
        prompt_overhead = 2000

        current_tokens = count_tokens(context)
        total_budget = safety_limit - current_tokens - prompt_overhead
The method lists all abstractions and their associated file indices. It calculates the remaining available token budget by subtracting the abstraction catalog tokens and an estimated prompt overhead (2,000 tokens) from the reasoning-adjusted safety_limit.

docs.title: Phase 2: Per-Abstraction Token Sizing & Two-Pass Allocation
docs.text:
# Pre-compute file token sizes for all abstractions
        abstr_file_data = []
        for abstr in abstractions:
            sized = []
            for idx in abstr["files"]:
                if 0 <= idx < len(files_data):
                    path, file_content = files_data[idx]
                    entry = f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
                    sized.append((idx, path, file_content, count_tokens(entry)))
            # Sort largest first (most architecturally significant)
            sized.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
            abstr_file_data.append(sized)

        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
The method sizes every file belonging to each abstraction, ordering files largest-first to prioritize significant source code modules. It divides the budget equally among abstractions (per_abstr_budget). In Pass 1, each abstraction packs files within its individual quota. In Pass 2, any remaining unused budget is pooled into total_unused and redistributed to abstractions that have remaining files, preventing smaller abstractions from stranding token capacity.

docs.title: Phase 3: Context Payload Assembly
docs.text:
# Build context output
        for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
            included_files, remaining_files, _ = abstr_results[i]
            if included_files or remaining_files:
                context += f"\n--- Abstraction {i}: {abstr['name']} ---\n"
                for idx, path, file_content, _tokens in included_files:
                    if file_content is not None:
                        context += f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
                    else:
                        context += f"  (File {idx} # {path} -- already shown above)\n"
                if remaining_files:
                    rest_list = ", ".join(f"{idx} # {p}" for idx, p, _c, _t in remaining_files)
                    context += f"  Other files (path only, budget exhausted): {rest_list}\n"

        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG",
            f"AnalyzeRelationships prep | total_budget={total_budget:,} | per_abstr_budget={per_abstr_budget:,} | abstractions={num_abstractions}",
            dest="LOG",
        )
        return (
            context, "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt), num_abstractions,
            project_name, language, use_cache, thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )
The method builds the final context payload from the two-pass allocation. For files included in full, the complete source is injected; files already added by an earlier abstraction are referenced with a pointer to prevent duplicate tokens. Any files omitted due to budget exhaustion are appended as path-only references.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> dict:

Description: Dispatches the relationship extraction prompt to call_llm, parses the summary and relationship edge definitions, validates directional abstraction indices, and constructs a relationship graph model.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The prepared parameter tuple from AnalyzeRelationships.prep().

Returns: * dict: Dictionary with keys "summary" (string overview) and "details" (list of relationship dictionaries with "from", "to", and "label").

Raises: * ValueError: If the model output is missing required root keys or relationship items lack valid indices.

Example: 

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        # ... unpack prep_res, format prompt with identify_relationships template ...
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="analyze_relationships"
        )

        relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)
        if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
            raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")

        validated_relationships = []
        for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
            # Validate indices and labels
            from_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["from_abstraction"]))[0])
            to_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["to_abstraction"]))[0])
            if not (0 <= from_idx < num_abstractions and 0 <= to_idx < num_abstractions):
                continue
            validated_relationships.append({"from": from_idx, "to": to_idx, "label": rel["label"]})

        emit("DONE_RELATIONSHIPS")
        return {"summary": relationships_data["summary"], "details": validated_relationships}

The method uses regular expressions to extract index numbers from model responses (e.g., parsing "0 # Database" into integer 0). It ensures extracted relationships stay within bounds (0 <= idx < num_abstractions), dropping invalid edges while warning via WARN_INVALID_RELATIONSHIP.

class OrderChapters(Node):

docs.title: OrderChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Prompts the LLM to order chapters, verifies that the response contains an exhaustive, non-duplicate permutation of all abstraction indices, and returns the ordered list.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The parameters output by OrderChapters.prep().

Returns: * list[int]: An ordered permutation of integer abstraction indices.

Raises: * ValueError: If the model response is not a valid list, contains out-of-bounds or duplicate indices, or omits abstractions.

Example: 

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        (
            abstraction_listing, context, num_abstractions, project_name,
            list_lang_note, use_cache, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode,
        ) = prep_res

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context
        )
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="order_chapters"
        )

        ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
        if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
            raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

        ordered_indices = []
        seen_indices = set()
        for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
            idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip()) if isinstance(entry, str) and "#" in entry else int(entry)
            if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions) or idx in seen_indices:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid or duplicate index {idx} in ordered list.")
            ordered_indices.append(idx)
            seen_indices.add(idx)

        if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
            raise ValueError("Ordered list length does not match number of abstractions.")
        return ordered_indices

The method validates the returned sequence against the total number of abstractions. It checks that every integer index from 0 to num_abstractions - 1 is present exactly once, raising a ValueError on malformed permutations to trigger PocketFlow retry logic.

docs.title: ExtractFacts
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ExtractFacts(BatchNode):

Description: The ground-truth fact extraction and verification engine for api-reference mode. Extracts declared symbols, dependencies, configuration, and errors from raw source files and manifests using facts.py, auditing each claim against verbatim code.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Computes facts signatures across models, prompt templates, and source content hashes. Identifies reusable entries from facts.json when running under incremental or cached execution, and schedules extraction items for both code modules and package manifests.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state.

Returns: * list[dict]: A collection of item parameter dictionaries for each module and manifest.

Example: 

class ExtractFacts(BatchNode):
    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        template = load_prompt_template("extract_facts", mode="common")
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "extract_facts")
        provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
        signature = f"{provider}|{model_name}|{thinking_level or 'default'}|{hashlib.md5(template.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}"
        self.facts_file = facts_path(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared["project_name"], shared.get("mkdocs", False))
        reuse = shared.get("incremental") or shared.get("use_cache", True)
        previous = load_facts(self.facts_file) if reuse else {}
        self.previous_manifests = load_facts(self.facts_file, section="manifests") if reuse else {}
        self.best = {}

        items = []
        for module in shared["abstractions"]:
            file_path, content = files_data[module["files"][0]]
            path = module.get("original_path") or file_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            item_hash = facts_hash(signature, path, content)
            cached = previous.get(path) if isinstance(previous.get(path), dict) else {}
            items.append({
                "path": path, "content": content, "facts_hash": item_hash,
                "cached_claims": cached.get("claims") if cached.get("facts_hash") == item_hash else None,
                "cached_followup": (cached.get("completeness") or {}).get("followup"),
                "template": template, "project_name": shared["project_name"],
                "use_cache": shared.get("use_cache", True), "thinking_level": thinking_level,
                "max_tokens": shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            })
        # ... prepares manifest items ...
        return items

The method derives an MD5 execution signature combining the active provider, model name, reasoning effort, and template hash. It loads previous runs from facts.json via load_facts when --incremental or cache reuse is enabled. If a module's content and signature match its stored facts_hash, the cached claims and follow-up states are reused directly.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> dict:

The fact extraction workflow operates across several distinct phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Manifest Branch & Fact Cache Resolution
docs.text:
@safe_exec
    def exec(self, item):
        if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
            return self._exec_manifest(item)
        if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
            emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
            followup = item["cached_followup"] if isinstance(item["cached_followup"], dict) else {"status": "none", "asked": []}
            if followup.get("status") != "failed":
                return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"], "followup": followup}
            claims, followup, calls = self._follow_up(item, item["cached_claims"], followup.get("asked") or [])
            return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": claims, "followup": followup, "followup_calls": calls}
If the item represents a manifest file, execution routes to _exec_manifest. For standard code modules with valid cached claims, the cache hit is logged. If a previous follow-up pass failed, it retries the completeness follow-up; otherwise, it returns the cached claims immediately without making an LLM call.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Invocation & Parsing
docs.text:
prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note="")
        emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_FACTS", name=item["path"])
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
        )
        claims = parse_facts_response(response)
On cache misses, the prompt is formatted with the source file contents and an empty focus note, then dispatched to call_llm under the "extract_facts" step. The raw model output is parsed via parse_facts_response into a dictionary containing symbols, dependencies, config, and errors.

docs.title: Phase 3: Claim Verification & Coverage Rejection Check
docs.text:
checked = verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"FACTS | {item['path']} | claimed={checked['claimed']} | found={checked['found']}", dest="LOG")
        if self.cur_retry == 0:
            self.best.pop(item["path"], None)
        best = self.best.get(item["path"])
        if best is None or checked["found"] > best[0]:
            self.best[item["path"]] = best = (checked["found"], claims)
        # Mostly unfindable quotes mean the model paraphrased: retry uncached, then keep the best attempt's
        # verified part rather than losing the module
        if checked["claimed"] >= 4 and checked["found"] * 2 < checked["claimed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
            emit("FACTS_LOW_COVERAGE", name=item["path"], found=checked["found"], claimed=checked["claimed"])
            raise ValueError(f"only {checked['found']}/{checked['claimed']} claims found in the source")
        claims, followup, calls = self._follow_up(item, best[1])
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": claims, "followup": followup, "followup_calls": calls}
The claims are audited against the verbatim source code using verify_file_claims. The node tracks the highest-yield attempt in self.best. If the model fabricated citations (finding less than 50% of 4+ claims), a ValueError is raised to trigger an uncached retry. Once verified, the claims are passed to _follow_up to capture any missed declarations.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item: dict, exc: Exception) -> dict:

Description: Fallback handler invoked when all retries are exhausted. Retains the best partial claims extracted from earlier attempts (with facts_hash intact), or returns an empty placeholder to allow the DAG to continue without halting execution.

Parameters: * item (dict): The batch item payload. * exc (Exception): The exception raised during the final failed execution.

Returns: * dict: Fallback claims dictionary containing path, hash status, and parsed claims.

Example: 

    def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
        emit("WARN_FACTS_FALLBACK", name=item["path"], error=exc)
        if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
            return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}
        best = self.best.get(item["path"])
        if best is not None:  # no follow-up ran: the next run asks it
            return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": best[1], "followup": {"status": "failed", "asked": []}}
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}

The method ensures pipeline resilience against transient LLM parsing failures. If an earlier attempt produced readable claims (stored in self.best), it preserves those claims and marks the follow-up status as "failed". If no attempt succeeded, it returns facts_hash: None, ensuring the file will be re-analyzed on subsequent incremental runs.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[dict]) -> str:

The post-processing phase consolidates repository-wide facts and verifies cross-file links:

docs.title: Phase 1: Manifest Verification & Table Construction
docs.text:
def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        manifest_results = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") == "manifest"]
        exec_res_list = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") != "manifest"]
        manifest_texts = {item["path"]: item["content"] for item in prep_res if item.get("kind") == "manifest"}
        manifests = {
            res["path"]: {
                **verify_manifest_claims(res["claims"], manifest_texts[res["path"]], res["path"]),
                "facts_hash": res["facts_hash"],
                "claims": res["claims"],
            }
            for res in manifest_results
            if res["claims"] is not None
        }
        contents = {item["path"]: item["content"] for item in prep_res if item.get("kind") != "manifest"}
        checked = {res["path"]: verify_file_claims(res["claims"], contents[res["path"]]) for res in exec_res_list if res["claims"] is not None}
        table = ModuleTable(list(contents), {path: result["symbols"] for path, result in checked.items()}, contents, manifests)
        resolved = verify_dependencies({path: result["dependencies"] for path, result in checked.items()}, contents, table)
The method partitions manifest and code module outputs. Manifest claims are audited via verify_manifest_claims. Using verified symbols and path definitions, it constructs a cross-module ModuleTable and runs verify_dependencies to resolve import links and package aliases across the entire repository.

docs.title: Phase 2: Completeness Metrics & Persistence
docs.text:
modules = {}
        for res in exec_res_list:
            path, content = res["path"], contents[res["path"]]
            result, deps = checked.get(path), resolved.get(path)
            rejected = (result["rejected"] if result else []) + (deps["rejected"] if deps else [])
            claimed = result["claimed"] if result else 0
            hints = completeness_hints(content, result, res["claims"]) if result else None
            followup = res.get("followup") or {"status": "none", "asked": []}
            asked = set(followup.get("asked", []))
            modules[path] = {
                "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
                "lines": len(split_lines(content)),
                "symbols": result["symbols"] if result else [],
                "depends_on": deps["depends_on"] if deps else [],
                "used_by": [],
                "external": deps["external"] if deps else [],
                "config": result["config"] if result else [],
                "errors": result["errors"] if result else [],
                "coverage": {"claimed": claimed, "verified": claimed - len(rejected)},
                "completeness": {
                    "import_lines": len(hints["import_lines"]),
                    "declaration_lines": len(hints["declaration_lines"]),
                    "unreported_lines": [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number not in asked],
                    "declined_lines": [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number in asked],
                    "followup": followup,
                }
                if hints else None,
                "rejected": rejected,
                "missed_imports": deps["missed"] if deps else [],
                "unexplained_names": unexplained_names(content, path, deps["depends_on"], table) if deps else [],
                "facts_hash": res["facts_hash"],
                "claims": res["claims"],
            }
        for path, entry in modules.items():
            for edge in entry["depends_on"]:
                modules[edge["module"]]["used_by"].append(path)

        save_facts(self.facts_file, build_facts_document(shared["project_name"], source_commit(shared.get("local_dir")), modules, manifests))
        shared["module_facts"] = modules
        # ... emits DONE_FACTS and FACTS_COMPLETENESS telemetry ...
        emit_step_subtotals("extract_facts")
        return "default"
The method computes reverse dependencies (used_by) and calculates coverage statistics comparing claimed facts against rejected citations. It evaluates completeness against raw line counts, tracking lines the model intentionally declined versus those left unanalyzed. The verified dataset is serialized to facts.json using save_facts, committed to shared["module_facts"], and summarized via telemetry events.

docs.title: WriteChapters
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class WriteChapters(BatchNode):

Description: The chapter drafting engine. Generates technical documentation chapters sequentially, tracking cross-chapter context summaries to maintain narrative continuity without token explosion.

docs.title: WriteChapters.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Computes an incremental cache signature, generates target file paths via build_chapter_filenames, and builds an execution dictionary for each chapter item.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * list[dict]: The batch execution items for all chapters.

Example: 

class WriteChapters(BatchNode):
    def prep(self, shared):
        chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "write_chapters")
        summary_thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "chapter_summary")

        mode = shared.get("mode", "tutorial")
        provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
        template_digest = hashlib.md5(load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=mode).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        generation_signature = f"{mode}|{language}|{provider}|{model_name}|{thinking_level or 'default'}|{template_digest}"

        self.chapters_written_so_far = []
        self.chapter_summaries = []
        filenames = build_chapter_filenames(chapter_order, abstractions, shared.get("mkdocs", False))
        # ... compiles all_chapters and items_to_process ...
        return items_to_process

The method generates a generation_signature hash combining the active documentation mode, target language, provider, model name, thinking effort, and chapter prompt template digest. It assigns destination filenames and constructs navigation references for previous and next chapters, packing them into an item payload.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> dict:

The chapter drafting lifecycle runs across four distinct phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Preparation & Incremental Manifest Cache Check
docs.text:
@safe_exec
    def exec(self, item):
        abstraction_name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
        chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]

        )

            hasher = hashlib.md5()
