            hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
            current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()

            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                # ... read manifest, check cached_hash == current_hash and file exists ...
                # On hit: reads clean_content, appends to self.chapter_summaries, returns cached dict
The method combines the generation_signature with the MD5 digest of the abstraction's source files. Under --incremental mode, it checks .doc_cache_manifest.json. On a cache hit, it loads the existing markdown file from disk, strips frontmatter if necessary, restores the chapter summary, and skips generation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Context Budget Windowing for Previous Chapter Summaries
docs.text:
# Capped at 50% of context window — drops oldest summaries first.
        prev_chapters_budget = int(item.get("max_tokens", 100000) * 0.50)
        prev_chapters_tokens = 0
        if self.chapter_summaries:
            selected_summaries = []
            running_tokens = 0

            for summary in reversed(self.chapter_summaries):
                summary_tokens = count_tokens(summary)
                if running_tokens + summary_tokens > prev_chapters_budget and selected_summaries:
                    break
                selected_summaries.append(summary)
                running_tokens += summary_tokens

            selected_summaries.reverse()
            # ... join selected summaries with windowing notification if trimmed ...
            previous_chapters_summary = "\n---\n".join(selected_summaries)
        else:
            previous_chapters_summary = ""
To avoid token bloat from injecting entire preceding chapters into the prompt, the method maintains concise LLM-generated chapter summaries. It allocates up to 50% of the active context window for cross-chapter continuity, selecting summaries from newest to oldest and omitting older summaries if the budget is reached.

docs.title: Phase 3: LLM Chapter Generation & Heading Normalization
docs.text:
prompt_template = load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            # ... injects project, abstraction, directory_tree, previous_chapters_summary, etc. ...
            previous_chapters_summary=previous_chapters_summary or "This is the first chapter.",
            file_context_str=file_context_str or "No specific code snippets provided for this abstraction.",
        )
        emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=abstraction_name.strip())
        chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item.get("thinking_level"), step="write_chapters")
        if not chapter_content.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"Empty chapter response for '{abstraction_name.strip()}'")
        if getattr(chapter_content, "truncated", False):
            current_hash = None

        if not chapter_content.strip().startswith(f"# {chapter_word} {chapter_num}") and item.get("mode") != "api-reference":
            lines = chapter_content.strip().split("\n")
            if lines and lines[0].strip().startswith("#"):
                lines[0] = actual_heading
                chapter_content = "\n".join(lines)
            else:
                chapter_content = f"{actual_heading}\n\n{chapter_content}"
        self.chapters_written_so_far.append(chapter_content)
The method formats the chapter draft prompt and invokes call_llm under the "write_chapters" step. If the response was truncated by provider limits, current_hash is cleared to prevent saving the incomplete output to the cache. In tutorial modes, it normalizes the top-level Markdown # heading to match the assigned chapter number.

docs.title: Phase 4: Technical Summary Generation
docs.text:
summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, item.get("language", "english"))
        emit("LLM_CALL_SUMMARIZE", chapter_num=chapter_num)

            summary_prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item.get("summary_thinking_level"), step="chapter_summary"
        )

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item: dict, exc: Exception) -> dict:

Description: Fallback handler that catches exhausted retries during chapter drafting, returning a placeholder page with a missing hash to ensure the chapter is regenerated on the next run without halting the pipeline.

Parameters: * item (dict): The chapter generation item payload. * exc (Exception): The exception raised during the final failed execution.

Returns: * dict: Placeholder dictionary containing notice text, hash: None, and a fallback summary.

Example: 

    def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
        name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
        chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
        emit("WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=name.strip(), error=exc)
        notice = get("UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE")
        summary = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {name.strip()}:\n{notice}"
        self.chapter_summaries.append(summary)
        return {"content": f"# {name.strip()}\n\n{notice}\n", "hash": None, "name": name, "summary": summary}

The method generates a placeholder Markdown page using UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE. Setting "hash": None ensures that .doc_cache_manifest.json will not cache the placeholder, forcing the chapter to regenerate on subsequent runs.

docs.title: WriteChapters.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Persists drafted chapter contents to shared["chapters"], stages incremental manifest entries in shared["pending_manifest"], and saves chapter summaries to the shared store.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (list[dict]): The batch preparation list. * exec_res_list (list[dict]): The list of drafted chapter result dictionaries.

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        if shared.get("incremental"):
            shared["pending_manifest"] = {
                res.get("cache_key") or res["name"]: {"hash": res["hash"], "summary": res.get("summary", ""), "filename": res.get("filename")}
                for res in exec_res_list
                if res.get("hash") and res.get("name")
            }

        shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)
        del self.chapters_written_so_far
        del self.chapter_summaries
        emit("DONE_ALL_CHAPTERS", count=len(exec_res_list))
        emit_step_subtotals("write_chapters", "chapter_summary")

The method commits all chapter content strings to shared["chapters"]. When running in --incremental mode, valid hashes and filenames are staged in pending_manifest for writing by CombineTutorial once files are safely on disk. Finally, it cleans up batch-scoped instance variables and prints step subtotals.

docs.title: CombineTutorial
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class CombineTutorial(Node):

Description: The final compilation node in the pipeline. Formats outputs, writes files to disk via mkdocs.py (as either a standalone Markdown collection or a full MkDocs Material documentation site), and updates the incremental cache manifest.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

The preparation phase handles diagram rendering and navigation layout across multiple steps:

docs.title: Phase 1: Mermaid Relationship Diagram Generation
docs.text:
class CombineTutorial(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        output_base_dir = shared.get("output_dir", "output")
        output_path = os.path.join(output_base_dir, project_name)
        repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
        relationships_data = shared["relationships"]
        chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        chapters_content = shared["chapters"]

        # --- Generate Mermaid Diagram ---
        mermaid_lines = ["flowchart TD"]
        for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
            sanitized_name = abstr["name"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
            mermaid_lines.append(f'    A{i}("{sanitized_name}")')
        for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
            edge_label = rel["label"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ")
            if len(edge_label) > 30:
                edge_label = edge_label[:27] + "..."
            mermaid_lines.append(f'    A{rel["from"]} -- "{edge_label}" --> A{rel["to"]}')

        incoming = {f"A{i}": 0 for i in range(len(abstractions))}
        for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
            incoming[f"A{rel['to']}"] += 1
        entry_nodes = [nid for nid, inc in incoming.items() if inc >= 2]
        if entry_nodes:
            mermaid_lines.append("    classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5")
            mermaid_lines.extend(f"    class {node_id} entryNode" for node_id in entry_nodes)

        mermaid_diagram = "\n".join(mermaid_lines)
The method builds a Mermaid flowchart TD diagram representing the abstraction relationships. Nodes with two or more incoming edges are styled as foundation hubs with the entryNode CSS class. In api-reference mode, where relationships are stubbed, the diagram generation completes with an empty edge list.

docs.text:
ui = {

        if repo_url:

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> str:

Description: Creates the destination directory and compiles documentation files to disk using either write_mkdocs_output or write_standalone_output.

Parameters: * prep_res (dict): The compilation payload assembled by CombineTutorial.prep().

Returns: * str: The absolute or normalized output directory path where documentation was written.

Example: 

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        output_path = prep_res["output_path"]
        is_mkdocs = prep_res["is_mkdocs"]
        chapter_files = prep_res["chapter_files"]
        ui = prep_res["ui"]

        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG",
            f"NODE EXEC | node=CombineTutorial | action=write_output | output={output_path} | chapters={len(chapter_files)} | mkdocs={is_mkdocs}",
            dest="LOG",
        )
        emit("COMBINE_WRITING_OUTPUT", path=output_path)

            write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files)

            write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui)

            "DEBUG",
            f"NODE COMPLETE | node=CombineTutorial | output={output_path} | files_written={len(chapter_files) + 1}",
            dest="LOG",
        )
        return output_path  # Return the final path

The method creates the target output path via os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True). It branches on is_mkdocs to delegate compilation to mkdocs.py, returning the output path on completion.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: dict, exec_res: str) -> None:

Description: Persists the final output directory path to shared["final_output_dir"] and atomically writes the incremental cache manifest (.doc_cache_manifest.json) using a temporary file to prevent cache corruption on interrupted runs.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global pipeline state. * prep_res (dict): The preparation inputs. * exec_res (str): The final output directory path from exec().

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["final_output_dir"] = exec_res  # Store the output path

        # Save the incremental manifest only now that the pages it describes are on disk: saved earlier,
        # an interrupted run left new hashes next to old pages, which later runs served as cache hits.
        manifest = shared.get("pending_manifest")
        if shared.get("incremental") and manifest is not None:
            manifest_path = os.path.join(exec_res, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            tmp_path = f"{manifest_path}.tmp"
            with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
            os.replace(tmp_path, manifest_path)

        emit("GEN_COMPLETE", path=exec_res)

The method writes .doc_cache_manifest.json only after all output files are committed to disk. Writing to a .tmp file and renaming it via os.replace guarantees atomic updates, preventing broken cache states if the process is terminated abruptly.

docs.title: safe_exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def safe_exec(func: callable) -> callable:

Description: Decorator that standardizes error handling across PocketFlow node exec() implementations. Emits a localized NODE_RETRY_ERROR event, writes the full traceback to the debug log, and re-raises the exception to trigger configured PocketFlow retry logic.

Parameters: * func (callable): The underlying exec(self, prep_res) method being decorated.

Returns: * callable: The wrapped execution function.

Raises: * Exception: Re-raises any exception thrown by the underlying method.

Example: 

def safe_exec(func):
    """Decorator that wraps Node.exec() with standardized error handling.

    On exception: emits NODE_RETRY_ERROR, logs traceback, and re-raises.
    Eliminates the identical try/except pattern duplicated across all nodes.
    """

    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return func(self, *args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("NODE_RETRY_ERROR", class_name=self.__class__.__name__, error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            raise

    return wrapper

This decorator wraps node execution, intercepting errors to emit telemetry through utils.output and record stack traces in log files. It re-raises exceptions cleanly so upstream orchestrators can manage retry backoffs.

Visibility: Private Signature: def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:

Description: Queries the token accounting ledger in llm_common.py and prints cumulative usage and cost subtotals for each specified step.

Parameters: * *steps (str): Variable number of step name strings (e.g., "write_chapters", "chapter_summary", "extract_facts").

Returns: * None

Example: 

def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:
    """Print the running usage subtotal of each step (batch nodes call this from post())."""
    summary = get_step_summary()
    for step in steps:
        if step in summary:

docs.title: ExtractFacts._exec_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _exec_manifest(self, item: dict) -> dict:

Description: Dedicated execution helper for package manifests. Prompts the model using extract_manifest.md to identify declared package exports and path aliases.

Parameters: * item (dict): The manifest item configuration dictionary.

Returns: * dict: Manifest claims dictionary containing kind: "manifest", path, hash, and claims.

Raises: * ValueError: If parsed manifest claims contain invalid YAML items and remaining retries are available.

Example: 

    def _exec_manifest(self, item):
        if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
            emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
            return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"]}
        prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"])
        emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_MANIFEST", name=item["path"])
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
        )
        claims = parse_facts_response(response, MANIFEST_KEYS)
        if claims["unparsed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{claims['unparsed']} manifest items are not valid YAML")
        facts_hash = None if claims["unparsed"] else item["facts_hash"]
        return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": facts_hash, "claims": claims}

The method bypasses LLM inference on cache hits. On cache misses, it prompts the model and parses the output against MANIFEST_KEYS. If YAML parsing fails and retries remain, it raises a ValueError to trigger an uncached retry; otherwise, it returns readable claims while clearing facts_hash to force re-evaluation on subsequent runs.

docs.title: ExtractFacts._follow_up()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _follow_up(self, item: dict, claims: dict, asked: tuple | list = ()) -> tuple[dict, dict, int]:

Description: Conducts multi-round completeness follow-up prompts (up to FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS = 3) focusing on declaration lines that were omitted from initial claims.

Parameters: * item (dict): The module item dictionary. * claims (dict): The current validated claims dictionary. * asked (tuple | list, optional): Collection of line numbers that have already been queried. Defaults to ().

Returns: * tuple[dict, dict, int]: A 3-tuple containing: 1. claims (dict): Merged and verified claims dictionary. 2. followup (dict): Follow-up status dictionary ("status", "asked"). 3. calls (int): Count of additional LLM queries executed.

Example: 

    FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS = 3  # follow-up calls per module at most, each on FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT lines not asked before

    def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):
        asked, calls, lines = list(asked), 0, split_lines(item["content"])
        for _round in range(self.FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS):
            hints = completeness_hints(item["content"], verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"]), claims)
            already = set(asked)
            pending = [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number not in already]
            if not pending:
                break
            note = build_facts_focus_note([(number, lines[number - 1]) for number in pending])
            prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note=note)
            emit("FACTS_FOLLOWUP", name=item["path"], count=len(pending))
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
            answer = None
            for attempt in range(2):
                calls += 1
                try:
                    response = call_llm(
                        prompt,
                        use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0 and attempt == 0),
                        thinking_level=item["thinking_level"],
                        step="extract_facts",
                    )
                    answer = parse_facts_response(response)
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    emit_raw("WARNING", f"FACTS FOLLOW-UP FAILED | {item['path']} | attempt {attempt + 1} | {e}", dest="LOG")
            if answer is None:
                return claims, {"status": "failed", "asked": asked}, calls
            claims = merge_claims(claims, answer)
            asked += pending[:FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT]
        return claims, {"status": "done" if asked else "none", "asked": asked}, calls

The method loops through candidate lines using completeness_hints. If declaration-like lines are missing from existing claims, it extracts up to FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT (60) unqueried lines and prompts the model to classify them. Responses are parsed, verified, and merged into the primary claim set via merge_claims. If a follow-up query fails, existing claims are preserved and the status is recorded as "failed".

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep.<locals>.create_llm_context()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def create_llm_context(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> tuple[str, int]:

Description: Nested helper inside IdentifyAbstractions.prep. Concatenates indexed source file blocks until adding another file would exceed the reasoning-adjusted token budget.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): The list of relative path and content tuples.

Returns: * tuple[str, int]: A 2-tuple containing the combined context string and its total token count.

Example: 

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)

            context = ""
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                    break

                context += entry
                current_tokens += entry_tokens

            return context, current_tokens

This helper protects prompt construction against context window overflow. It sizes each file block using count_tokens and stops concatenation if the total exceeds safety_limit, emitting WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED to signal that remaining files were omitted.

docs.text:
Detailed ground-truth data extracted by ExtractFacts and verified against source text.

Field Type Description source_sha256 str SHA-256 digest of the raw source file contents. lines int Total line count of the source file. symbols list[dict] Verified classes, functions, and methods defined in the file. depends_on list[dict] Outgoing dependencies mapped to other modules in the codebase. used_by list[str] Incoming dependencies from other modules that consume this file. external list[str] External third-party packages or standard library imports. config list[dict] Environment variables and configuration options read by the file. errors list[dict] Error classes, exceptions, and panic cases raised by the file. coverage dict[str, int] Coverage metrics tracking claimed versus verified facts (claimed, verified). completeness dict Line audit tracking import and declaration coverage. rejected list[dict] Citations rejected during verification due to missing source evidence. missed_imports list[str] Detected import statements that failed resolution. facts_hash str \| None MD5 signature hash, or None if the file requires re-analysis.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The nodes in nodes.py use defensive error-handling patterns to handle LLM variations and transient failures:

  • Decorator-Driven Retries (@safe_exec): Applied to all primary exec() methods. Catches unexpected exceptions, emits a NODE_RETRY_ERROR event to utils.output, logs the exception and full stack trace to the LOG destination, and re-raises the error to let PocketFlow's retry policies handle the failure.
  • Low Coverage Detection (ExtractFacts.exec): Verifies that LLM-claimed citations physically exist in the source code using verify_file_claims. If an LLM hallucinates quotes (finding fewer than 50% of claims across 4+ items), the node raises a ValueError to force an uncached retry rather than saving corrupt fact data.
  • Non-Blocking Follow-up Failures (ExtractFacts._follow_up): Wraps completeness queries in an internal retry loop. If follow-up calls fail or return unparseable YAML, the node logs a warning to LOG and preserves previously verified claims, marking the follow-up status as "failed" so subsequent runs can retry.
  • Graceful Chapter Fallbacks (WriteChapters.exec_fallback): If all retries fail when drafting a chapter, exec_fallback returns a placeholder page with UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE and sets hash: None. This keeps the pipeline running, adds a placeholder entry to chapter_summaries, and ensures the chapter will be regenerated on the next run.
  • Truncation Defense: Inspects LLM completions for truncation markers via getattr(chapter_content, "truncated", False). If a response was cut short by output token limits, its cache hash is cleared to prevent saving incomplete pages to .doc_cache_manifest.json.
  • Atomic Cache Persistence (CombineTutorial.post): Serializes .doc_cache_manifest.json to a .tmp file before renaming it with os.replace. This atomic write ensures that interrupted runs do not leave corrupted JSON caches on disk.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text: Source: utils/call_llm.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
As the primary invocation gateway for large language models within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture, utils/call_llm.py establishes a unified interface across diverse LLM backends. It abstracts provider-specific communication protocols, serialization quirks, and client libraries beneath a consistent, caching-aware dispatch pipeline. The module dispatches prompts to Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenRouter, or generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (such as local Ollama instances) according to system configuration resolved at runtime.

The module incorporates an atomic, content-addressable caching subsystem keyed on SHA-256 digests over the provider name, target model, reasoning effort, and the full prompt body. This design guarantees that identical calls avoid redundant API consumption and billing without risking disk corruption if interrupted mid-write. Surrounding each execution, call_llm.py integrates token tracking, ledger differential measurements via context managers, refusal memory caching to prevent repetitive failures during workflow node retries, and automated pruning of incompatible sampling parameters for advanced reasoning models.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, step: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single prompt string to the currently configured LLM provider and model. Manages the lifecycle of cache lookup, refusal short-circuiting, active API dispatch, ledger delta calculation, and cache persistence. If caching is enabled and an exact key match exists, the cached response is returned immediately. Otherwise, the call executes against the provider, records token usage against the specified workflow step, validates that the output is not truncated or empty, updates persistent storage, and returns the response string.

docs.title: Phase 1: Setup and Token Estimation
docs.text:
step = step or "other"
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")

The function normalizes the workflow step to "other" if not specified and resolves the runtime provider, model identifier, and credentials through resolve_llm_settings(). It counts the prompt tokens using count_tokens(prompt)—which is typically pre-computed and memoized in token utilities—and emits structured debug logs containing the invocation metadata and raw prompt content.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cache Lookup and Hit Resolution
docs.text:
# Check cache if enabled
    key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if key in cache:
            cached_response = cache[key]
            emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)
            emit("LLM_CALL_CACHED", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
            return cached_response
        emit("CACHE_MISS")

When caching is requested, _cache_key() hashes the provider, model, normalized thinking level, and prompt text. If a match is present within the singleton cache structure loaded by load_cache(), the system registers a cache hit event, attributes estimated prompt tokens to the current pipeline step without incurring monetary cost, logs the retrieved response, and exits early.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prior Refusal Verification
docs.text:
# A request the provider already declined this run is declined again: do not re-send it on
    # node retries (rate limits, billed partial output). The node retry still sees the error.
    refusal_key = request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt)
    refused = previous_refusal(refusal_key)
    if refused is not None:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=refused_before (not re-sent)", dest="LOG")
        raise refused

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

To prevent wasteful requests and cascading rate limits during automated graph node retries, the function computes a provider-agnostic request_key() and verifies whether this exact request has already encountered a non-retryable refusal during the current run. If a previous refusal exception exists in memory, previous_refusal() returns the stored exception, which is immediately re-raised without making an outbound network request.

docs.title: Phase 4: Provider Dispatch and Usage Metering
docs.text:
# Usage of this call = ledger delta for the provider: it includes every billed request the call
    # made (Anthropic truncation retry, resend after fallbacks were disabled), even when it raises.
    before = usage_snapshot(provider)
    returned = False
    try:
        with usage_step(step):
            if provider == "GEMINI":
                response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "ANTHROPIC":
                response_text = _call_llm_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "OPENROUTER":
                response_text = _call_llm_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
                response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        returned = True
    except LLMRefusalError as e:
        if not e.retryable:
            remember_refusal(refusal_key, e)
        raise
    finally:
        call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
        measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
        if measured:
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
            _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)
        elif returned:  # answered, but the provider reported no usage
            emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")

Execution snapshots the provider's token ledger prior to dispatch and wraps provider invocation inside a usage_step(step) context block. Calls branch to specialized adapters (_call_llm_gemini, _call_llm_anthropic, _call_llm_openrouter) or fall back to the generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP bridge (_call_llm_provider). If an LLMRefusalError occurs and is designated non-retryable, it is recorded in the refusal registry. In the finally block, the exact ledger difference (usage_delta) is computed to account for intermediate retries or truncated token consumption, emitting formatted billing metrics.

docs.title: Phase 5: Response Persistence and Cache Commit
docs.text:
elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")

    # Update cache if enabled. Empty and truncated responses (llm_common.TruncatedResponse)
    # are never cached — they would be replayed on every later run.
    if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[key] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
    return response_text

Following successful text retrieval, the function evaluates whether the response should be committed to disk. If use_cache is active, the response is non-empty, and the returned object is not an instance of TruncatedResponse (which indicates premature token cutoff), the cache dictionary is updated with key and serialized atomically via save_cache(). Finally, the raw text is returned to the caller.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete, formatted text prompt to be evaluated by the LLM. * use_cache (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether to check local cache prior to execution and persist valid responses afterwards. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort configuration ("low", "medium", "high", "max", etc.), mapped to provider-specific thinking configurations. Defaults to None. * step (str | None, optional): Label identifying the calling workflow node (e.g., matching definitions in utils/thinking.py) used to attribute token consumption. Defaults to None (mapped to "other").

Returns: * str: The string output received from the language model backend, or an instance of TruncatedResponse (a str subclass) if the provider ran out of generation tokens.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: If the provider explicitly declines generation, hits billing cutoffs, or encounters terminal rate limits. * ValueError: If required environment variables or provider configurations are missing or malformed. * ImportError: If a required vendor SDK package (such as anthropic or google-genai) is missing from the environment. * Exception: Catch-all for uncaught connection errors, HTTP errors, timeouts, or unexpected API payload structures.

Example: 

# Extracted from self-test block in utils/call_llm.py
test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

emit("SELFTEST_LLM_CALL")
response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
emit("SELFTEST_LLM_RESPONSE", response=response1)

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Loads and returns the in-memory singleton dictionary representing llm_cache_v2.json. Reads and deserializes the JSON file from the filesystem on first invocation. Subsequent calls immediately return the globally cached reference _cache without repeating disk I/O. If the file is missing, an empty dictionary is initialized. If deserialization fails due to corrupted JSON or I/O permissions, a warning is emitted and an empty cache is returned to allow execution to proceed.

def load_cache():
    global _cache
    if _cache is not None:
        return _cache
    try:
        with open(cache_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            _cache = json.load(f)
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("CACHE_LOADED", count=f"{len(_cache):,}", file=cache_file)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        _cache = {}
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_LOAD_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache load error: {e}", dest="LOG")
        _cache = {}
    return _cache

The function manages lazy loading of the global _cache instance. Upon read failure, it leverages utils.output.emit to warn the operator while falling back gracefully to an in-memory dictionary, preventing catastrophic failure of the pipeline when cache files are corrupted.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: In-memory dictionary mapping SHA-256 hash strings to prior text responses.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; errors are trapped and logged.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() cache lookup in utils/call_llm.py
cache = load_cache()
if key in cache:
    cached_response = cache[key]

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Persists the provided cache dictionary to disk using an atomic file replacement strategy. The cache payload is first serialized to a temporary file (llm_cache_v2.json.tmp) and then atomically moved onto llm_cache_v2.json using os.replace. This prevents cache file corruption if the application process is terminated unexpectedly during disk writes.

def save_cache(cache):
    global _cache
    _cache = cache
    # Write to a temp file and atomically replace, so an interrupted run never leaves a truncated cache.
    tmp_path = f"{cache_file}.tmp"
    try:
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
        os.replace(tmp_path, cache_file)
    except (OSError, TypeError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache save error: {e}", dest="LOG")

The implementation updates the module-level _cache reference, performs a synchronous json.dump to a .tmp file, and invokes os.replace to guarantee POSIX atomic replacement semantics across platforms. File access or serialization exceptions (OSError, TypeError) are trapped and emitted via the logging system.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The mapping of SHA-256 cache keys to cached LLM response strings.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; write and serialization failures are trapped and emitted as warnings.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() response caching in utils/call_llm.py
cache = load_cache()
cache[key] = response_text
save_cache(cache)

docs.title: notice_legacy_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:

Description: Audits the working directory for the existence of the deprecated, prompt-keyed llm_cache.json (pre-v2 format). If detected, it determines the file size in megabytes and emits a non-fatal notification informing the user that the legacy cache is ignored by v2 engines and can be cleaned up to reclaim disk space.

def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:
    """Point out a leftover pre-v2 cache file: it is never read, so it only takes disk space."""
    try:
        size = os.path.getsize(LEGACY_CACHE_FILE)
    except OSError:
        return
    from utils.output import emit

    emit("CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND", file=LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, size=f"{size / 1_048_576:,.1f}", current=cache_file)

The function wraps os.path.getsize in an exception guard. If the legacy file does not exist or raises an OSError, execution silently returns. When found, it translates bytes into megabytes and delegates display formatting to emit("CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND", ...).

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised.

Example: 

# Extracted from the self-test entrypoint in utils/call_llm.py
if not check_llm_auth():
    sys.exit(1)
notice_legacy_cache()

docs.title: _cache_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:

Description: Computes a deterministic SHA-256 hash identifying an LLM prompt invocation. The scope string binds the provider name, model identifier, and normalized thinking level, concatenated with the prompt content.

def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The function guarantees strict isolation between models and reasoning modes. Even if identical prompt text is supplied, running against different providers or switching thinking effort levels will result in distinct SHA-256 hex digests.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The exact input prompt text. * provider (str): Target provider identifier (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OLLAMA"). * model (str): The provider-specific model name string. * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort level, or None (mapped to "default").

Returns: * str: A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.

Raises: * No custom exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() in utils/call_llm.py
key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    if key in cache:
        cached_response = cache[key]

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Sends an HTTP POST request to an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoint (such as Ollama or local proxy hosts) configured via environment variables. Handles authorization headers, reasoning budget parameter adaptation, parameter stripping for models rejecting sampling flags, JSON payload parsing, defensive response structure checks, token usage telemetry registration, and HTTP transport error handling.

docs.title: Phase 1: Provider Environment Configuration and Validation
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

The helper derives variable names dynamically from LLM_PROVIDER (e.g., OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_API_KEY). It verifies that the model and base URL are defined, raises descriptive ValueError instances if missing, and appends /v1/chat/completions to the stripped base URL.

docs.title: Phase 2: Request Payload and Thinking Parameter Assembly
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Ollama reasoning models accept low/medium/high; xhigh/max clamp to high.
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        effort = _clamp_level(thinking_level.lower(), ["low", "medium", "high"]) or "medium"
        payload["think"] = effort
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    if rejects_sampling_params(model):
        # Claude Opus 4.7+ / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5 / Fable reject sampling parameters (400).
        payload.pop("temperature", None)

The HTTP header dictionary is populated with standard JSON content types and optional Bearer authentication. For OLLAMA with reasoning enabled, the thinking level is clamped to allowed strings (low, medium, high) using _clamp_level and mapped to both think and reasoning_effort keys while resetting temperature to 1.0. For modern models that reject sampling parameters entirely (verified via rejects_sampling_params(model)), the temperature parameter is stripped.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTP Transmission and Error Handling
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        response.raise_for_status()  # HTTP status first: an HTML 502 page must not look like a JSON bug
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit

            emit(
                "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
                status_code=response.status_code,
                preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
            )
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None

        # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
            raise RuntimeError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

Requests are dispatched with a connection timeout of 10 seconds and read timeout of 300 seconds. HTTP errors are caught via response.raise_for_status(). Response bodies are parsed into JSON with fallback logging if invalid payloads or HTML error pages are returned. A defensive check verifies that the returned JSON contains a non-empty choices list, guarding against providers that respond with HTTP 200 while embedding an error payload.

docs.title: Phase 4: Usage Recording and Response Parsing
docs.text:
usage = response_json.get("usage") or {}
        from utils.llm_common import record_usage
        from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, observe_prompt_tokens

        prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
        record_usage(
            provider,
            model,
            input_tokens=prompt_tokens,
            output_tokens=usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0,
            thinking_tokens=(usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0,
            cache_read=(usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0,
            cost=None,
            measured=bool(usage),
        )
        if usage:
            observe_prompt_tokens(provider, model, count_tokens_raw(prompt), prompt_tokens)
        choice = response_json["choices"][0]
        text = (choice.get("message") or {}).get("content") or ""
        if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
            from utils.llm_common import TruncatedResponse

            return TruncatedResponse(text)
        return text
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

Extracted usage metrics (input tokens, completion tokens, reasoning tokens, and cached tokens) are fed to record_usage(). Token observation metrics calibrate local token estimators via observe_prompt_tokens(). If finish_reason is "length", the text is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse object. The surrounding except blocks normalize network, connection, timeout, and HTTP exceptions into detailed standard exceptions.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt payload to send in the user message. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level string, clamped to allowed values for compatible providers. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Extracted response content string, or a TruncatedResponse instance if truncated by maximum token limits.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables are absent, or if JSON decoding fails. * RuntimeError: If the returned JSON payload lacks the expected choices array. * Exception: Normalized exception for network errors, timeouts, or HTTP status failures.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() provider dispatch fallback in utils/call_llm.py
else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
    response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: _call_llm_anthropic()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Lazy-imports the Anthropic driver from utils.llm_anthropic and delegates prompt execution to call_anthropic. Ensures runtime environments that do not utilize Anthropic are not required to install the anthropic Python package.

docs.title: _emit_call_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:

Description: Formats and logs a single console record reflecting token metrics, deviation from prior estimates, thinking tokens, cache read hits, and financial cost incurred by an individual LLM call.

def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:
    """One console line per LLM call: billed input vs the estimate, output (thinking), cached, cost.
    `measured` = requests with provider-reported usage (the deviation is per measured request)."""
    from utils.output import emit, get
    from utils.token_utils import format_cost

    per_request = usage["input"] / measured
    deviation = f"{(per_request - estimate) / estimate:+.0%}" if estimate else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN")
    emit(
        "LLM_CALL_USAGE",
        step=step,
        input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
        estimate=f"{estimate:,}",
        deviation=deviation,
        requests=get("LLM_CALL_REQUESTS", count=measured) if measured > 1 else "",
        output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
        thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
        cached=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
        cost=format_cost(usage),
    )

The function computes the per-request input token average against measured calls and calculates percentage deviation from the estimated token count. It assembles localized strings via utils.output.get and triggers emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE", ...) to output a formatted status line to the terminal.

Parameters: * step (str): The name of the calling pipeline node or step. * estimate (int): The estimated input token count. * usage (dict): Ledger delta dictionary containing recorded token metrics. * measured (int): Count of HTTP requests in this invocation that returned official usage numbers.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * No custom exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() finally block in utils/call_llm.py
call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
if measured:
    record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
    _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)

docs.title: In-Memory and Persistent Cache Dictionary (llm_cache_v2.json)
docs.text:
The local disk cache stored in llm_cache_v2.json and kept in memory via _cache is a key-value mapping of SHA-256 strings to model responses.

Field Type Description [sha256_hash_key] str A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 hash computed by _cache_key(). [value] str The complete text response generated by the LLM.

Example shape in JSON: 

{
  "a3b8c9d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0": "This is a cached completion response."
}

docs.text:
Internal scope structure used to seed hashlib.sha256 in _cache_key().

Segment Format Description provider str Name of the provider (e.g., GEMINI, ANTHROPIC, OLLAMA). model str Configured model identifier (e.g., gemini-2.5-flash, claude-3-7-sonnet). thinking_level str Lowercase thinking level, or "default" if unspecified. delimiter \n Newline separating scope metadata from the prompt. prompt str The full user prompt text.

docs.title: OpenAI-Compatible HTTP Request Payload
docs.text:
The dictionary structure transmitted to generic OpenAI-compatible completion endpoints via requests.post.

Key Type Description model str Model identifier string retrieved from the environment variable <PROVIDER>_MODEL. messages list[dict[str, str]] Message history containing a single user turn: [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. temperature float Sampling temperature (0.7 by default; set to 1.0 if reasoning is enabled; stripped if model rejects sampling). think str (optional) Reasoning effort for Ollama servers ("low", "medium", "high"). reasoning_effort str (optional) Alternative reasoning parameter for Ollama/OpenAI reasoning endpoints.

docs.title: Provider Usage Ledger Delta Object (call_usage)
docs.text:
Dictionary produced by usage_delta(before, after) representing token usage accumulated during an execution.

Key Type Description calls int Total count of outbound API calls dispatched. unmeasured_calls int Count of outbound API calls whose provider returned no usage block. input int Cumulative prompt/input tokens billed. output int Cumulative output/completion tokens generated. thinking int Tokens generated as internal reasoning/thinking steps. cache_read int Prompt tokens satisfied by provider-side prompt caching.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive strategies across network transport, response parsing, and execution retries:

  • Non-Retryable Refusal Memorization: When a provider encounters a non-retryable refusal (such as credit depletion or safety blocks), an LLMRefusalError is caught, and remember_refusal(refusal_key, e) records it in memory. If graph execution retries the node, previous_refusal() intercepts the call and re-raises the error before issuing another HTTP request.
  • Corrupt Cache Resilience: When loading llm_cache_v2.json, json.JSONDecodeError and OSError exceptions are caught, an error warning is emitted, and _cache is reset to an empty dictionary, allowing execution to proceed without caching rather than crashing the pipeline.
  • Atomic Cache Writing: save_cache() writes JSON contents to f"{cache_file}.tmp" and replaces the target file via os.replace. This atomic operation avoids file truncation or corruption if the execution is interrupted.
  • Truncated Response Caching Exclusion: Empty responses or instances of TruncatedResponse (where finish_reason == "length") bypass cache persistence entirely (not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False)). This ensures incomplete generations are not saved to disk and replayed in subsequent runs.
  • Transport Normalization: In _call_llm_provider(), network errors are trapped and mapped to clear exception messages distinguishing connection failures, timeouts, invalid JSON, and HTTP status codes.

docs.title: crawl_github_files.py
docs.text: Source: utils/crawl_github_files.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the LLM inference abstraction layer established in call_llm.py, the crawl_github_files.py module functions as the remote repository ingestion engine for the codebase analysis pipeline. It extracts source trees, verifies file properties, and loads source file contents into memory from GitHub repositories before downstream tokenization, abstraction mapping, and documentation generation take place. The module supports two primary ingestion pathways: native Git cloning over SSH for authenticated or firewalled environments, and deep API-driven tree navigation via the GitHub REST API v3 for targeted subpaths and commit-pinned trees.

The architecture accommodates large remote repositories by implementing size-gated memory loading, rate-limit backoff handling, and filtering mechanisms. Path filtering operates across multiple tiers: standard Git exclude specifications (.gitignore parsed via pathspec), explicit inclusion globs, and targeted exclusion globs evaluated via fnmatch. When targeting subdirectories within monorepos, the crawler supports relative path re-basing so that extracted downstream node artifacts reflect module-relative hierarchies rather than top-level repository nesting.

The module emits granular telemetry throughout its lifecycle via utils.output functions (emit, emit_raw, get), capturing progress events, directory skips, size ceiling violations, and encoding failures. Traversal results are compiled into a normalized dictionary mapping relative file paths to decoded UTF-8 string buffers, accompanied by operational metadata describing file counts and filtering configurations.

docs.title: DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (Module-level constant)

DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1_048_576  # 1 MB

Description: Defines the default upper boundary (1 megabyte in bytes) for file buffers retrieved during crawling operations. Files exceeding this threshold are bypassed to avoid memory exhaustion during large codebase ingestions.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: 

def crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=None,
    max_file_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE,
    use_relative_paths: bool = False,
    include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
    exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
):

Description: Coordinates the retrieval and filtering of remote source code files from GitHub repositories. Depending on the syntax of repo_url, the function either clones the repository into a managed temporary directory via Git over SSH or traverses the remote file tree over the GitHub REST API v3. Files matching exclusion criteria, violating size limits, or failing UTF-8 decoding are recorded and omitted from the returned dictionary.

docs.title: Phase 1: Pattern Normalization and URL Classification
docs.text:
# Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    # ... should_include_file definition ...

    # Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

The function normalizes include_patterns and exclude_patterns into standard Python sets if passed as single string instances. It evaluates the protocol and format of repo_url using prefix and suffix matching: URLs prefixed with git@ or terminating in .git are routed directly to the SSH clone pipeline, while web URLs are routed to the GitHub REST API pipeline.

docs.title: Phase 2: SSH Repository Ingestion and Local Traversal
docs.text:
if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

            # ... counter initialization and .gitignore loading ...

            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                dirs.sort()

                for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)

In the SSH workflow, git.Repo.clone_from performs a full clone of the remote repository into a managed tempfile.TemporaryDirectory. If the cloned root contains a .gitignore file, its lines are parsed into a pathspec.PathSpec object using the gitwildmatch dialect. The code recursively walks the local directory via os.walk, pruning directory trees in-place if they match .gitignore rules or directory exclusion patterns (normalizing patterns ending in /*). For surviving files, the implementation checks pattern inclusion, enforces the max_file_size cap via os.path.getsize, and reads the content using utf-8-sig encoding to handle UTF-8 Byte Order Marks (BOM). Files failing text decoding or encountering read errors are categorized as non-text and excluded.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTPS URL Resolution and Reference Parsing
docs.text:
# Parse GitHub URL to extract owner, repo, commit/branch, and path
    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
    path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip("/").split("/")

    if len(path_parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")

    # Extract the basic components
    owner = path_parts[0]
    repo = path_parts[1]

    # Setup for GitHub API
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"token {token}"

    # ... fetch_branches and check_tree definitions ...

    # Check if URL contains a specific branch/commit
    if len(path_parts) > 3 and path_parts[2] == "tree":

        def join_parts(i):
            return "/".join(path_parts[i:])

        branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
        branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

        if len(branches) == 0:
            return None

        relevant_path = join_parts(3)
        filter_gen = (name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name))
        ref = next(filter_gen, None)

        if ref is None:
            tree = path_parts[3]
            ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

        if ref is None:
            emit_raw("ERROR", "The given path does not match with any branch and any tree in the repository.\nPlease verify the path is exists.")
            return None

        part_index = 5 if "/" in ref else 4
        specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
    else:
        ref = None
        specific_path = ""

When handling HTTPS GitHub URLs, the URL is decomposed into its owner and repository names using urllib.parse.urlparse. If the URL targets a subpath containing /tree/, the crawler disambiguates whether the segment following /tree/ references a Git branch (including branches containing slashes like feature/test) or an explicit Git tree/commit SHA. It fetches branch definitions via fetch_branches and confirms commit tree existence via check_tree. Any remaining path elements trailing the resolved reference are isolated into specific_path to restrict crawling to that directory subtree.

docs.title: Phase 4: Remote API Navigation and Content Extraction
docs.text:
# --- Try to fetch .gitignore ---
    gitignore_spec = None
    try:
        gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
        gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
        gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
        if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
            gi_data = gi_resp.json()
            if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
                gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())
                emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository (API)")
    except Exception:
        pass

    # ... fetch_contents definition ...

    # Start crawling from the specified path
    fetch_contents(specific_path)

The crawler queries GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore to load remote ignore rules, decoding the returned base64 blob into a pathspec.PathSpec rule engine. Traversal initiates by passing specific_path into the recursive fetch_contents helper, which processes directory trees and file metadata returned by the GitHub Contents API.

docs.title: Phase 5: Result Assembly and Telemetry Summary
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = api_counters["processed"] + api_counters["excluded"] + api_counters["size_limit"] + api_counters["non_text"]
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=api_counters["processed"])
    if api_counters["excluded"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=api_counters["excluded"])
    if api_counters["size_limit"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=api_counters["size_limit"])
        for sf in api_skipped_size:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)
    if api_counters["non_text"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=api_counters["non_text"])
        for sf in api_skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": 0,
            "skipped_files": [],
            "base_path": specific_path if use_relative_paths else None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
        },
    }

Both SSH and API pathways compile total execution metrics across processed entries, excluded patterns, size limits, and non-text skips. Summary blocks are emitted via emit(), and an aggregate dictionary containing the relative file-to-content map alongside crawling statistics is returned to the caller.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Full GitHub repository URL or SSH connection string (e.g., 'https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/main/python/packages/autogen-core' or 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git'). * token (str, optional): GitHub Personal Access Token used for HTTP Authorization headers to prevent rate-limiting on public repositories or grant access to private repositories. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowed size in bytes per file before triggering a skip. Defaults to 1_048_576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True, trims the specific_path prefix from returned dictionary keys. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Single glob pattern or set of patterns (e.g., {"*.py", "*.md"}) that a file name must match to be retained. If None, all files pass inclusion. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob patterns specifying file names, file paths, or directories to ignore during crawling. If None, no exclusions are applied.

Returns: * dict: Structured payload containing the extracted file mapping under "files" and operational summary statistics under "stats". Returns None or an error payload if repository resolution fails.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised when repo_url cannot be partitioned into valid owner and repository path segments. * Exception: Raised when GitHub API requests return rate limit status codes (403, 429) and no token is available to proceed.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (__main__ execution block)
github_token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
repo_url = "https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/6c38dc93f40a47f4d1350adca9ec0d72502e223f/pydantic"

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=github_token,
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 MB in bytes
    use_relative_paths=True,  # Enable relative paths
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},  # Include Python and Markdown files
)

files = result["files"]
stats = result["stats"]

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: 

def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file satisfies filtering criteria based on file name inclusion patterns, .gitignore path specifications, and explicit file exclusion globs.

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The function executes three filtering steps. First, if include_patterns is present, file_name must match at least one glob pattern via fnmatch.fnmatch; otherwise, include_file remains True. Second, if a gitignore_spec is provided and reports a match against the relative file_path, the candidate is immediately excluded. Third, if exclude_patterns are defined, file_path is evaluated against each pattern; a positive match causes the function to reject the file.

Parameters: * file_path (str): Relative path of the file within the repository root or target subdirectory. * file_name (str): Basename of the file. * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec, optional): Compiled PathSpec instance matching .gitignore rules.

Returns: * bool: True if the file passes all inclusion and exclusion checks; False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (SSH traversal loop)
if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
    count_excluded += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
    continue

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: 

def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict] | list:

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API to retrieve branch metadata for the target repository, enabling reference resolution for multi-segment branch names.

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get branches of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository.",
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function executes an HTTP GET request against /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches with a 30-second connection and read timeout. It intercepts status codes 403 and 429, raising an explicit Exception if no API token is configured. If the repository is inaccessible (HTTP 404) or encounters unexpected error codes, diagnostic failure messages are emitted via emit_raw, and an empty list is returned to halt branch resolution.

Parameters: * owner (str): Repository owner (organization or user account). * repo (str): Repository name.

Returns: * list[dict] | list: A list of dictionaries representing GitHub branch descriptors if successful; otherwise, an empty list.

Raises: * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are exceeded and no authentication token is provided.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (HTTPS branch resolution)
branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)
