docs.title: code_view()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:

Description: Strips docstrings, block comments, and trailing comments while preserving original line count and indices. Agnostically strips Python triple quotes (""", '''), C-style block comments (/* ... */), and trailing line comments (#, //, --). Block string assignments like HELP = """...""" are replaced with HELP = "" to maintain syntactically valid declaration heads.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    last = {}  # closer → (line, column) of its last occurrence
    for closer in set(_BLOCK_CLOSERS.values()):
        for number in range(len(lines) - 1, -1, -1):
            column = lines[number].rfind(closer)
            if column >= 0:
                last[closer] = (number, column)
                break
    view, closing = [], None
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        out, position = "", 0
        if closing:
            end = line.find(closing)
            if end < 0:
                view.append("")
                continue
            position, closing = end + len(closing), None
        elif line.lstrip().startswith(("#", "//")):
            view.append(line)
            continue
        # ... token loop parsing strings and comment openers ...
        while True:
            match = _CODE_TOKEN_RE.search(line, position)
            if not match:
                out += line[position:]
                break
            token, start = match.group(), match.start()
            if token in ("#", "//", "--"):
                out += line[position:start]
                break
            closer = _BLOCK_CLOSERS.get(token)
            glob = token == "/*" and start and (line[start - 1].isalnum() or line[start - 1] in "_.*/$}")
            if not closer or glob or last.get(closer, (-1, -1)) < (number, match.end()):
                out += line[position : match.end()]
                position = match.end()
                continue
            out += line[position:start] + ('""' if closer != "*/" else " ")
            end = line.find(closer, match.end())
            if end < 0:
                closing = closer
                break
            position = end + len(closer)
        view.append(out.rstrip())
    return view
The routine scans forward while verifying that block delimiters match closing tags located via a reverse pass (last). Delimiters inside single-line strings or wildcard glob patterns (such as lib/*.sh) are preserved.

docs.title: declaration_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def declaration_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Language-agnostic heuristic checking whether a source code line appears to declare a reader-visible symbol (classes, functions, interfaces, constants, type definitions). Evaluates leading modifiers, keywords (_DECLARATION_WORDS), C-family return types, and assignment patterns.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def declaration_like(line: str) -> bool:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return False
    if stripped.startswith("#"):
        return stripped.startswith(("#define ", "#macro "))
    if not (stripped[0].isalpha() or stripped[0] in "_@$"):
        return False
    unindented = line[:1] not in (" ", "\t")
    constant = _CONSTANT_RE.match(stripped)
    if constant and not re.search(r"(?:^|\s)[a-z]+\s+[a-z]+[^()\[\]{}]*\.$", constant.group(1)):
        return True
    if _SQL_CREATE_RE.match(stripped) or _EXPORTED_FUNCTION_RE.match(stripped):
        return True
    if unindented and (_C_FUNCTION_RE.match(stripped) or _SIGNATURE_RE.match(stripped)):
        return True
    modifiers, word, separator, rest = _lead(stripped)
    if word is None and modifiers and _CONSTANT_RE.match(rest):
        return True
    if word is None or word in _CONTROL_WORDS:
        return bool(modifiers) and _METHOD_RE.match(rest) is not None
    names_next = bool(separator) and not separator.strip() and bool(re.match(r"[A-Za-z_$(]", rest))
    if (word in _DECLARATION_WORDS and names_next) or (word in _NAMELESS_DECLARATIONS and separator):
        return True
    if unindented and word in _TOP_LEVEL_WORDS and names_next:
        return True
    text = f"{word}{separator}{rest}"
    if unindented and modifiers and _TYPED_VALUE_RE.match(text):
        return True
    if modifiers:
        return _METHOD_RE.match(text) is not None
    if not text.rstrip().endswith("{") or " => " in text or _METHOD_RE.match(text) is None:
        return False
    inside = text[text.find("(") + 1 : text.rfind(")")] if ")" in text else ""
    return not re.search(r"=>|->|[\"'`]|\w\s*\(", inside)
The heuristic filters out control-flow structures, callback invocations (such as describe('x', () => {), and inline expressions, identifying lines likely to introduce named symbols.

docs.title: import_statement_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def import_statement_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a line is an import statement across various programming languages. Validates keyword-led imports (import, from, require, use), dynamic import calls, and shell source dots (. ./file.sh). Filters out prose sentences, block openers (import (), assignments (source = x), and attribute accesses (import.meta).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def import_statement_like(line: str) -> bool:
    stripped = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", line.strip())  # @testable import X
    if stripped.startswith("#") and not stripped[1:2].isalpha():
        return False
    if stripped.startswith(("'", '"', "`")):
        return False
    if _IMPORT_CALL_RE.search(stripped) and not stripped.startswith(("//", "/*", "*")):
        return True
    if re.match(r"^\.\s+[\"'$./\w]", stripped):  # shell: . ./lib/env.sh
        return True
    if not _import_like(stripped):
        return False
    words = _words(stripped.lstrip("#@"))
    while words and words[0] in _MODIFIERS:
        words = words[1:]
    after = stripped.lstrip("#@").split(words[0], 1)[1].lstrip()
    if not after or after in ("(", "{", "["):
        return False
    if after[0] in _NOT_IMPORT_AFTER:
        return False
    if after[0] == "." and words[0] != "from" and after[1:2] not in ("/", "."):
        return False
    if after[0] == "(" and (
        words[0] not in ("require", "import", "include", "load", "source", "library", "use") or not re.match(r"\(\s*[\"'`\w$./@~]", after)
    ):
        return False
    if len(_words(after)) > 6 and not _PATH_TOKEN_RE.search(after):
        return False
    if words[0] == "from" and re.match(r"[\w.]+,", after):
        return False
    if re.search(r"[A-Za-z]\.$", after) and len(_words(after)) >= 3 and not re.search(r"[\"'<`/;]", after):
        return False
    return words[0] != "export" or " from " in f" {stripped} " or after[:1] in ("'", '"')
This check protects against false positives in documentation comments and natural language sentences that start with words like from, source, or use.

docs.title: import_block_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def import_block_lines(lines: list[str]) -> set[int]:

Description: Detects 0-based line indices located inside Go-style import ( ... ) blocks containing bare quoted paths without import keywords.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def import_block_lines(lines: list[str]) -> set[int]:
    """0-based lines inside an ``import ( ... )`` block (Go): bare quoted paths with no keyword of their own."""
    found, inside = set(), False
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if re.match(r"^import\s*\($", stripped):
            inside = True
        elif inside and stripped == ")":
            inside = False
        elif inside and _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line):
            found.add(number)
    return found
Maintains an internal boolean state tracking the opening import ( and closing ) delimiters, registering lines matching _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.

docs.title: enclosing_blocks()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def enclosing_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str | None]:

Description: Performs single-pass structural indentation tracking across lines to determine the enclosing scope kind ("function", "container", or None at top-level) for each line. Control flow blocks (if, for, while) are passed through to find the enclosing function or container.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def enclosing_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str | None]:
    kinds, stack = [], []  # stack of (indent, kind)
    for line in lines:
        kind = _block_kind(line) if line.strip() else None
        if kind is None:
            kinds.append(None)
            continue
        indent = _indent(line)
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        kinds.append(next((k for _i, k in reversed(stack) if k != "control"), None))
        stack.append((indent, kind))
    return kinds
Uses a monotonic stack tracking (indent, kind) pairs. When indentation decreases, outer scopes are popped from the stack, allowing detection of local functions and container-nested methods without a formal grammar parser.

docs.title: completeness_hints()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Identifies 1-based line numbers containing import-like or declaration-like syntax that were not covered by verified claims. Generates follow-up prompts to recover symbols or imports missed during initial extraction.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
    view = code_view(lines)
    imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)
    enclosing = enclosing_blocks(view)
    declarations = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if n not in imports and enclosing[n] != "function" and declaration_like(line)}

    import_numbers, import_texts = set(), set()
    for entry in checked.get("dependencies", []):
        span = range(entry["line"] - 1, entry.get("end_line", entry["line"]))
        import_numbers.update(span)
        import_texts.update(_collapse(lines[n]) for n in span if n < len(lines))
    import_texts.update(_collapse(_as_text(item.get("evidence"))) for item in _claim_list(claims or {}, "dependencies"))
    symbol_numbers = set()
    for entry in checked.get("symbols", []):
        symbol_numbers.update(range(entry["line"] - 1, entry.get("end_line", entry["line"])))
        symbol_numbers.update(n - 1 for n in entry.get("ambiguous_lines", []))
    uncovered = {n for n in imports if n not in import_numbers and _collapse(lines[n]) not in import_texts}
    uncovered |= {n for n in declarations if n not in symbol_numbers}
    return {
        "import_lines": sorted(n + 1 for n in imports),
        "declaration_lines": sorted(n + 1 for n in declarations),
        "uncovered": sorted(n + 1 for n in uncovered),
    }
Excludes comments and block strings via code_view() and local variables inside functions via enclosing_blocks(). Marks an import line as covered if either its line index or exact whitespace-collapsed text matches an existing dependency claim.

docs.title: unexplained_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:

Description: Scans source content for unique symbol names owned by exactly one other module in the project where no verified dependency link exists between the modules.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:
    words = set(_words(content))
    linked = {edge["module"] for edge in depends_on}
    own = table.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
    found = []
    for name, module in sorted(table.symbol_owner.items()):
        if module != source_path and module not in linked and name not in own and (name in words or name.split(".")[-1] in words):
            found.append({"name": name, "module": module})
    return found
Identifies implicit dependencies—such as same-package or same-namespace symbols in languages like Go, Java, or C++ that do not require explicit import statements.

docs.title: merge_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:

Description: Merges two extraction attempts (such as initial extraction and a completeness follow-up) into a unified claims dictionary, deduplicating records matching on identity keys.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:
    merged = {}
    for key in CLAIM_KEYS:
        seen, items = set(), []
        for item in [*_claim_list(first or {}, key), *_claim_list(second or {}, key)]:
            marker = tuple(_collapse(_as_text(item.get(field))) for field in _IDENTITY_FIELDS[key])
            if marker not in seen:
                seen.add(marker)
                items.append(item)
        merged[key] = items
    merged["unparsed"] = (first or {}).get("unparsed", 0) + (second or {}).get("unparsed", 0)
    return merged
Identity keys are defined by _IDENTITY_FIELDS (e.g., (parent, name, signature) for symbols). When duplicates occur, the entry from first is retained, and unparsed error counters are summed.

docs.title: normalize_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes package, crate, and module names by folding case, stripping whitespace, applying Unicode NFC normalization, and substituting hyphens (-) with underscores (_).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:
    """Case-folded, ``-`` as ``_``: package, crate and distribution names compare equal across spellings
    (``shop-core`` in Cargo.toml, ``shop_core`` in ``use shop_core::store``)."""
    return _nfc(text).strip().casefold().replace("-", "_")
Ensures cross-language package declarations match import statements across varied naming conventions (e.g., Cargo package shop-core matching Rust import use shop_core::store).

docs.title: verify_manifest_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def verify_manifest_claims(claims: dict, content: str, manifest_path: str) -> dict:

Description: Verifies project manifest claims (provides and aliases) against raw manifest text (e.g., package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml). Verifies that declared package names are assigned via manifest keys and that alias target paths exist.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def verify_manifest_claims(claims: dict, content: str, manifest_path: str) -> dict:
    index = SourceIndex(content)
    flat = _collapse(content)
    result = {"provides": [], "aliases": [], "rejected": []}
    unparsed = claims.get("unparsed", 0) if isinstance(claims, dict) and isinstance(claims.get("unparsed"), int) else 0
    claimed = unparsed
    result["rejected"].extend({"kind": "unparsed", "reason": "reply item that is not valid YAML"} for _ in range(unparsed))
    for item in _claim_list(claims, "provides"):
        claimed += 1
        name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
        matches = [m for m in (index.locate(evidence) if name else []) if _collapse(name) in _collapse(index.text(m[0], m[1]))]
        if not matches:
            result["rejected"].append({"kind": "provides", "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "name/evidence not in the manifest"})
            continue
        line = _collapse(index.text(matches[0][0], matches[0][1]))
        if not _declares_name(line, name):
            result["rejected"].append(
                {"kind": "provides", "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "the line does not declare the name (a dependency?)"}
            )
            continue
        entry = _as_text(item.get("entry")).strip()
        kept = {"name": name, "line": matches[0][0] + 1}
        if entry and any(_declares_name(line_text, entry, _ENTRY_KEYS) for line_text in index.collapsed if _collapse(entry) in line_text):
            kept["entry"] = entry
        result["provides"].append(kept)
    for item in _claim_list(claims, "aliases"):
        claimed += 1
        alias, target, evidence = (_as_text(item.get(key)).strip() for key in ("alias", "target", "evidence"))
        matches = [
            m
            for m in (index.locate(evidence) if alias and target else [])
            if _collapse(alias) in _collapse(index.text(m[0], m[1])) and _collapse(target) in _collapse(index.text(m[0], m[1]))
        ]
        if not matches:
            result["rejected"].append(
                {"kind": "aliases", "alias": alias, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "alias/target/evidence not in the manifest"}
            )
            continue
        base = _as_text(item.get("base")).strip()
        kept = {"alias": alias, "target": target, "line": matches[0][0] + 1}
        if base and _collapse(base) in flat:
            kept["base"] = base
        result["aliases"].append(kept)
    result["claimed"] = claimed
    result["found"] = claimed - len(result["rejected"])
    return result
Uses _declares_name to ensure that words matching name are declarations rather than external package dependency requirements.

docs.title: manifest_rules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Converts verified manifest claims across all project manifests into normalized package rules and alias transformation structures for ModuleTable.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:
    packages, aliases = [], []
    for path, verified in (manifests or {}).items():
        directory = posixpath.dirname(path)
        for provided in verified.get("provides", []):
            if "*" in provided["name"]:
                continue
            entry = provided.get("entry")
            entry_path = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, entry)) if entry else None
            packages.append({"segments": _name_segments(provided["name"]), "name": provided["name"], "dir": directory, "entry": entry_path})
        for alias in verified.get("aliases", []):
            key = alias["alias"]
            if key.startswith(("./", "../")) or not key.split("*", 1)[0]:
                continue
            mode = "star" if "*" in key else "prefix" if key.endswith("/") else "exact"
            template = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, alias.get("base") or ".", alias["target"]))
            aliases.append({"prefix": key.split("*", 1)[0], "template": "" if template == "." else template, "mode": mode, "dir": directory})
    packages.sort(key=lambda package: -len(package["segments"]))
    return packages, aliases
Packages are ordered by segment length in descending order, ensuring that more specific nested packages match before root packages.

docs.title: ModuleTable
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ModuleTable:

Description: Cross-module resolution engine storing project module paths, directory trees, file extensions, manifest aliases, and globally unique owned symbols.

docs.title: ModuleTable.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):

Description: Initializes module lookup tables, builds directory mappings, processes manifest package rules, and identifies globally unique top-level symbols across the project.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
class ModuleTable:
    def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):
        self.paths = list(paths)
        self.contents = contents or {}
        self.packages, self.aliases = manifest_rules(manifests)
        self.segments = {path: _segments(path) for path in self.paths}
        self.extensions = {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path in self.paths if os.path.splitext(path)[1]}
        self.by_dir = defaultdict(list)
        for path in self.paths:
            self.by_dir[posixpath.dirname(path)].append(path)
        owners = defaultdict(set)
        self.top_symbols, self.all_symbols = {}, {}
        for path, symbols in symbols_by_path.items():
            self.all_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols}
            self.top_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols if symbol.get("kind") not in _OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS}
            for name in self.top_symbols[path]:
                if len(name) >= 3:
                    owners[name].add(path)
        self.symbol_owner = {name: next(iter(paths)) for name, paths in owners.items() if len(paths) == 1}
        self.owned = defaultdict(set)
        for name, path in self.symbol_owner.items():
            self.owned[path].add(name)
        for package in self.packages:
            package["extensions"] = {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path in self.paths if not package["dir"] or path.startswith(package["dir"] + "/")}
The constructor filters out method names (_OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS) and identifiers under three characters to prevent ambiguous resolution. Symbols defined in exactly one module populate symbol_owner, enabling unambiguous reverse symbol-to-module lookups.

docs.title: ModuleTable.normalize()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Normalizes target import specifiers across diverse syntax styles (utils.output, ./client, @/http, crate::store::Repo, App\Db) into an ordered segment list and recognized file extension.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
        text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,")
        for prefix in ("@/", "~/", "$/"):
            text = text.removeprefix(prefix)
        ext = os.path.splitext(text)[1]
        if ext in self.extensions:
            text = text[: -len(ext)]
        else:
            ext = ""
        text = text.replace("::", "/").replace("\\", "/").replace(".", "/")
        parts = [part.strip() for part in text.split("/")]
        return [part for part in parts if part and part not in ("*", "crate", "super", "self") and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)], ext
Strips delimiters, brackets, and scope sigils, transforming namespace and filesystem separators into standard forward slashes.

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_manifest(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set, prefer_local: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves an import target using workspace manifest rules and path aliases.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def resolve_manifest(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set, prefer_local: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        text = re.sub(r"^[A-Za-z][\w+.-]*:(?![/:\\])", "", target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
        if not text or text.startswith(("./", "../", ".\\", "..\\")) or re.match(r"^\.+\w", text):
            return None
        written = [part for part in re.split(r"::|[./\\:]+", _nfc(text).strip()) if part]
        source_dir = posixpath.dirname(source_path)
        if prefer_local and len(written) == 1 and self._resolve_rooted(posixpath.join(source_dir, written[0]), source_path, source_words):
            return None
        in_scope = [alias for alias in self.aliases if not alias["dir"] or source_path.startswith(alias["dir"] + "/")]
        for alias in sorted(in_scope, key=lambda alias: (-alias["dir"].count("/") - bool(alias["dir"]), -len(alias["prefix"]))):
            prefix, template, mode = alias["prefix"], alias["template"], alias["mode"]
            if mode == "exact":
                if text != prefix and not text.startswith(prefix + "/"):
                    continue
                rest = text[len(prefix) :].lstrip("/")
            elif not text.startswith(prefix):
                continue
            else:
                rest = text[len(prefix) :]
            if "*" in template:
                base = posixpath.normpath(template.replace("*", rest, 1))
            else:
                base = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(template, rest)) if rest else template
            resolved = self._resolve_rooted(base, source_path, source_words)
            if resolved:
                return resolved[0], prefix
        segments = _name_segments(text)
        extension = os.path.splitext(source_path)[1]
        for package in self.packages:
            if package["segments"] and segments[: len(package["segments"])] == package["segments"] and extension in package["extensions"]:
                found = self._resolve_in_package(package, written[len(package["segments"]) :], source_path, source_words)
                if found:
                    return found, package["name"]
        if len(segments) > 1 and any(len(p["segments"]) > 1 and p["segments"][0] == segments[0] for p in self.packages):
            if self.namespace_members(text, source_path, source_words) or self._matches_whole(text, source_path):
                return None
            return [], ""
        if (self.packages or self.aliases) and text[:1] in ("@", "#", "~", "$"):
            return [], ""
        return None
Evaluates path aliases in nested-scope order before falling back to package-name segment matching.

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Resolves an import target to project module paths via relative matching, suffix matching, directory packages, or symbol ownership.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def resolve(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
        relative = self._resolve_relative(target, source_path, source_words)
        if relative is not None:
            return relative
        parts, ext = self.normalize(target)
        for size in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
            tail = parts[-size:]
            hits = self._suffix_hits(tail, ext, source_path)
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return (hits, "path") if self._corroborated(target, parts, size, hits[0], source_path, source_words) else ([], "external")
            if hits:
                return [], "ambiguous"
            dirs = [d for d in self.by_dir if d and d.split("/")[-size:] == tail]
            if len(dirs) == 1:
                members = [path for path in self.by_dir[dirs[0]] if path != source_path]
                index_file = self._index_file(dirs[0])
                used = [path for path in members if path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words)]
                if used:
                    return used, "package"
        if parts and parts[-1] in self.symbol_owner and self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]] != source_path:
            return [self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]]], "symbol"
        return [], "external"
Applies _corroborated to suffix hits to confirm that dropped segments match declared namespaces or imported symbol names before accepting a match.

docs.title: ModuleTable.used_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:

Description: Identifies owned symbol names of path that appear in the token stream of source_path and are not declared locally.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:
        names = self.top_symbols.get(path, set()) - self.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
        return {name for name in names if name in source_words or name.split(".")[-1] in source_words}
Assists in verifying directory imports and namespace imports by confirming that the consuming file references symbols declared in the candidate module.

docs.title: ModuleTable.namespace_members()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Locates project modules declaring a namespace matching target where source_path uses at least one symbol uniquely owned by that module.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
        name = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").removesuffix(".*").removesuffix("::*")
        if len(re.split(r"::|[./\\]", name)) < 2:
            return []
        return [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path
            and declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), name)
            and self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words) & self.owned[path]
        ]
Resolves namespace imports common in C# (using Acme.Accounting;) and Java wildcard imports.

docs.title: evidence_names_module()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def evidence_names_module(evidence: str, target_path: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, how: str, relative_style: bool = False, per_line: bool = False) -> bool:

Description: Enforces the evidence rule: an alleged dependency edge is valid only if the quoted source evidence explicitly names the resolved module. The check passes if the line names the file stem or directory within a path or import statement, references a symbol uniquely owned by the target module, or names a declared namespace while consuming that module's symbols.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def evidence_names_module(
    evidence: str, target_path: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, how: str, relative_style: bool = False, per_line: bool = False
) -> bool:
    words = set(_words(evidence))
    checked = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", evidence) if relative_style else evidence
    name = target_path.split("/")[-2] if how == "package" and "/" in target_path else _stem(target_path)
    extension = "" if how == "package" else os.path.splitext(target_path)[1]
    lines = split_lines(checked) if per_line else [checked]
    word_clause = not relative_style and any(
        _import_like(line) and _plain_occurrence(_without_bindings(line), name, extension, table.extensions) for line in lines
    )
    if name in set(_words(checked)) and (_names_path(checked, name, extension, table.extensions) or word_clause):
        return True
    own = table.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
    if any(table.symbol_owner.get(word) == target_path and word not in own for word in words | set(_DOTTED_RE.findall(evidence))):
        return True
    used = table.used_names(target_path, source_path, set(_words(table.contents.get(source_path, ""))))
    if not used:
        return False
    directory = posixpath.dirname(target_path)
    siblings = [path for path in table.by_dir.get(directory, []) if path != target_path]
    names_directory = directory and _names_directory(checked, directory)
    if names_directory and not any(_names_path(checked, _stem(path), os.path.splitext(path)[1], table.extensions) for path in siblings):
        return True
    if _import_like(evidence):
        for dotted in _DOTTED_RE.findall(evidence):
            if declares_namespace(table.contents.get(target_path, ""), dotted):
                return True
    return False
Under the relative-import convention (relative_style=True), bare strings are ignored to prevent local binding names (e.g., import config from 'config') from falsely verifying local modules.

docs.title: declares_namespace()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a file contains a top-level namespace or package declaration matching dotted.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:
    """Whether *content* has a namespace/package/module declaration line naming *dotted*
    (``namespace Acme.Accounting``, ``package com.acme.billing;``, ``namespace App\\Repo;``)."""
    for line in split_lines(content):
        words = _words(line)
        if words and words[0] in _NAMESPACE_WORDS and dotted in line:
            return True
    return False
Scans lines for namespace keywords (namespace, package, defmodule) followed by the candidate identifier.

docs.title: scan_import_candidates()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:

Description: Identifies project modules named on import lines in a source file, acting as a recall diagnostic to highlight imports missed by extraction.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:
    found = set()
    for line in split_lines(content):
        if not (_import_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line)):
            continue
        if relative_style:
            line = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", line)
        words = set(_words(line))
        for path in table.paths:
            if path == source_path:
                continue
            stem = _stem(path)
            if stem in words and _names_path(line, stem, os.path.splitext(path)[1], table.extensions):
                found.add(path)
    return found
Scans import statements for known module stems that meet the path qualifier criteria in _names_path.

docs.title: relative_import_extensions()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:

Description: Detects file extensions in the repository that use relative path syntax (./ or ../) in their import statements.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:
    return {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path, claims in located.items() if any(_is_relative(claim["target"]) for claim in claims)}
When a language uses relative imports (common in JavaScript/TypeScript), bare target names are treated as external packages rather than matching local files.

docs.title: target_written()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Confirms that a claimed target is written verbatim within the evidence line rather than being an LLM paraphrase.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:
    text = _collapse(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
    if not text:
        return False
    if re.search("[\"'`]", text) and text in _collapse(evidence):
        return True
    first = (_words(text) or [""])[0]
    quoted = [q for q in re.findall(r"(?=[\"'`<]([^\"'`<>\s]+)[\"'`>])", evidence) if re.search(r"[/.]", q) or (first and first in _words(q))]
    if quoted:
        bare = _bare_path(text)
        if any(_bare_path(q) == bare or q.endswith("/" + bare) for q in quoted):
            return True
        if any(_bare_path(q).startswith(bare + "/") and re.search(r"[$#%]\{|\{\w", _bare_path(q)[len(bare) :]) for q in quoted):
            return True
    code = _without_bindings(re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", evidence))
    if quoted and not _words(code):
        return False
    wanted, have = _words(text), _words(code)
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if position < len(wanted) and word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
    return bool(wanted) and position == len(wanted) and not quoted
Handles quoted module specifiers, dynamic template strings (e.g., require(`./plugins/${name}`) matching ./plugins), and language keywords across code statements.

docs.title: judge_dependency()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def judge_dependency(claim: dict, source_path: str, source_words: set, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool, shadowed: frozenset = frozenset()) -> tuple[str, list]:

Description: Evaluates an individual dependency claim, returning a status category: "depends_on" for verified internal modules, "external" for third-party dependencies, or "rejected" with failure reasons.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def judge_dependency(
    claim: dict, source_path: str, source_words: set, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool, shadowed: frozenset = frozenset()
) -> tuple[str, list]:
    target, evidence = claim["target"], claim["evidence"]
    if _BARE_NAME_RE.match(target) and normalize_name(target) in shadowed:
        return "external", []
    written = target_written(target, evidence)
    per_line = claim.get("match") == "tokens"
    manifest = table.resolve_manifest(target, source_path, source_words, prefer_local=not relative_style)
    if manifest is not None:
        targets, _prefix = manifest
        if not targets:
            return "external", []
        if written and _imports_target(evidence, target):
            return "depends_on", [(module, "manifest") for module in targets]
        return "rejected", [(module, "evidence does not import the declared package or alias") for module in targets]
    if relative_style and _BARE_NAME_RE.match(claim["target"]):
        return "external", []
    targets, how = table.resolve(claim["target"], source_path, source_words)
    if not targets and how == "external" and _import_like(claim["evidence"]):
        targets, how = table.namespace_members(claim["target"], source_path, source_words), "namespace"
        if targets:
            return "depends_on", [(target, how) for target in targets]
    if not targets:
        return ("rejected", [(None, "target matches several modules")]) if how == "ambiguous" else ("external", [])
    if not written:
        own = table.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
        words = set(_words(evidence)) | set(_DOTTED_RE.findall(evidence))
        path_target = target.strip().replace("\\", "/")
        kept = [
            (module, how)
            for module in targets
            if any(table.symbol_owner.get(word) == module and word not in own for word in words)
            or (module.endswith(path_target) and evidence_names_module(evidence, module, source_path, table, how, relative_style, per_line))
        ]
        return ("depends_on", kept) if kept else ("rejected", [(module, "target is not written in the evidence") for module in targets])
    kept = [(module, how) for module in targets if evidence_names_module(evidence, module, source_path, table, how, relative_style, per_line)]
    if kept:
        return "depends_on", kept
    return "rejected", [(module, "evidence does not name the module") for module in targets]
Checks for shadowed external package names, queries manifest rules, falls back to table.resolve(), and enforces evidence_names_module().

docs.title: shadowed_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:

Description: Identifies bare package names that match external imports and do not correspond to internal project modules within the source file.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:
    def last(claim):
        segments = _name_segments(claim["target"])
        return segments[-1] if len(segments) > 1 else None

    external = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "external"} - {None}
    internal = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "depends_on"} - {None}
    return frozenset(external - internal)
Prevents local usages like store.ErrNotFound from falsely matching an internal module when store represents an external import like example.com/other/store.

docs.title: verify_dependencies()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def verify_dependencies(located: dict, contents: dict, table: ModuleTable) -> dict:

Description: Resolves and audits located dependency claims across all project modules. Evaluates edges, detects shadowed names, categorizes internal vs. external dependencies, and tracks missed import candidates.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def verify_dependencies(located: dict, contents: dict, table: ModuleTable) -> dict:
    results = {}
    relative_extensions = relative_import_extensions(located)
    for path, claims in located.items():
        words = set(_words(contents.get(path, "")))
        depends_on, external, rejected, seen = [], [], [], set()
        relative_style = os.path.splitext(path)[1] in relative_extensions
        verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style) for claim in claims]
        shadowed = shadowed_names(claims, verdicts)
        if shadowed:
            verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style, shadowed) for claim in claims]
        for claim, (verdict, detail) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True):
            if verdict == "external":
                external.append({"name": claim["target"], "line": claim["line"]})
            elif verdict == "rejected":
                rejected.extend(
                    {"kind": "dependency", **claim, **({"module": module} if module else {}), "reason": reason} for module, reason in detail
                )
            else:
                for module, how in detail:
                    if module not in seen:
                        seen.add(module)
                        depends_on.append(
                            {"module": module, "target": claim["target"], "line": claim["line"], "evidence": claim["evidence"], "via": how}
                        )
        missed = sorted(scan_import_candidates(contents.get(path, ""), path, table, relative_style) - seen)
        results[path] = {"depends_on": depends_on, "external": external, "rejected": rejected, "missed": missed}
    return results
Executes a two-pass evaluation over judge_dependency() when shadowed names are detected, ensuring clean partition between local modules and third-party libraries.

docs.title: facts_hash()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:

Description: Computes a 32-character hexadecimal MD5 digest over the prompt signature, file path, and file content.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(f"{signature}|{path}|{content}".encode()).hexdigest()
Used by caching layers to invalidate cached extraction facts when prompt definitions, paths, or file contents change.

docs.title: source_commit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:

Description: Retrieves the Git HEAD commit SHA from a target repository checkout directory via git rev-parse HEAD.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:
    if not local_dir or not os.path.isdir(local_dir):
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", local_dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return (out.stdout.strip() or None) if out.returncode == 0 else None
Executes a subprocess call isolated to local_dir, returning the 40-character commit SHA, or None if the directory is not a Git repository or the call fails.

docs.title: load_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:

Description: Reads a previously generated facts.json file and extracts the requested top-level section if the schema version matches FACTS_SCHEMA.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            document = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}
    entries = document.get(section) if isinstance(document, dict) else None

docs.title: save_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:

Description: Atomically serializes the facts.json document to disk using a temporary file (.tmp) followed by an atomic filesystem replacement.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = f"{path}.tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(document, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    os.replace(tmp_path, path)

docs.title: SourceIndex._words_in_order()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:

Description: Verifies that a list of identifier tokens appears in exact sequential order across a range of lines.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:

docs.title: _has_words()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether the identifier tokens comprising name appear in sequential order within text.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    wanted, have = _words(name), _words(text)
    if not wanted:
        return False
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
            if position == len(wanted):
                return True
    return False

docs.title: _names_in()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies the presence of name within text, handling both alphanumeric identifiers and punctuated names such as C++ operators (operator==, []).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    if re.fullmatch(r"\w+", _nfc(name)):
        return _has_words(text, name)
    return _squash(name) in _squash(text) and (not _words(name) or _has_words(text, name))

docs.title: _verify_symbols()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _verify_symbols(symbols: list[dict], index: SourceIndex) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Topologically verifies symbol declarations and member scopes against a file's SourceIndex. Ensures parent containers are located before their member functions or fields.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _verify_symbols(symbols: list[dict], index: SourceIndex) -> tuple[list, list]:
    kept, rejected, placed = [], [], {}
    pending, unscoped = list(symbols), False
    while pending:
        pending_names = {_as_text(item.get("name")).strip() for item in pending}
        waiting = []
        for item in pending:
            name, parent = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("parent")).strip()
            if not unscoped and parent and parent != name and parent not in placed and parent in pending_names:
                waiting.append(item)
                continue
            signature = _as_text(item.get("signature"))
            matches, scoped = [], False
            tops = sorted(entry["line"] - 1 for entry in kept if not entry["parent"])
            containers = sorted((entry["line"] - 1, entry["name"]) for entry in kept if entry["kind"] in _CONTAINER_KINDS)
            if parent in placed:
                start = placed[parent]
                end = next((line for line in tops if line > start), None)
                matches = [m for m in index.locate(signature, start, end) if name and _names_in(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name)]
                scoped = bool(matches)
            if not matches:
                matches = [m for m in index.locate(signature) if name and _names_in(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name)]
                if parent:
                    matches = [m for m in matches if parent in _words(index.text(m[0], m[1])) or _enclosing(containers, m[0]) in (None, parent)]
            # ... match verification and rejection handling ...
            if not matches or (len(matches) > 1 and parent and not scoped):
                reason = "signature not in source" if not index.locate(signature) else "signature matches several lines; the parent does not tell them apart"
                rejected.append({"kind": "symbol", "name": name, "parent": parent, "signature": signature, "reason": reason})
                continue
            first, last, how = matches[0]
            text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, signature)
            entry = {"name": name, "kind": _as_text(item.get("kind")).strip() or "symbol", "parent": parent, "line": first + 1, "signature": text}
            kept.append(entry)
            placed.setdefault(name, first)
        unscoped = len(waiting) == len(pending)
        pending = waiting
    kept.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["line"])
    return kept, rejected
Resolves parent scoping loops using waiting lists. When a member's parent has been placed, searches are restricted to lines between the parent and the next top-level declaration.

docs.title: _lead()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:

Description: Splits a stripped code line into declaration modifiers, first non-modifier word, trailing separator, and remaining text.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:
    text, modifiers = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", stripped.lstrip("$")), []
    while True:
        text = re.sub(r"^(\w+)\(\w+\)\s+", r"\1 ", text)  # private(set) var → private var
        lead = _WORD_AT_RE.match(text)
        if not lead:
            return modifiers, None, "", text
        word, separator = lead.group(1), lead.group(2)
        rest = text[lead.end() :]
        is_modifier = word in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS or (word == "case" and re.match(r"(?:class|object)\b", rest))
        if is_modifier and separator and not separator.strip():
            modifiers.append(word)
            text = rest
            continue
        return modifiers, word, separator, rest
Strips annotations like @Override and compound modifiers like private(set), isolating the defining keyword and identifier.

docs.title: _block_kind()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:

Description: Categorizes the scope kind opened by a code line: "function", "container", "control", "other", or None.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if not re.search(r"\w", stripped) or stripped[0] in ")]}" or re.fullmatch(r"end\b\W*", stripped):
        return None
    _modifiers, word, separator, rest = _lead(stripped)
    if word in _FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return "function"
    if word in _CONTAINER_WORDS:
        return "container"
    if word in _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS:
        return "control"
    if _CLOSURE_RE.search(stripped) or (word and _METHOD_RE.match(f"{word}{separator}{rest}") and re.search(r"[)\]{:]\s*$", stripped)):
        return "function"
    return "other"
Evaluates leading words against _FUNCTION_WORDS, _CONTAINER_WORDS, and _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS, also detecting closures and anonymous callbacks.

docs.title: _declares_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a declaration key appears immediately preceding a name within a manifest line, confirming it represents a definition rather than a dependency.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:
    before = line.split(_collapse(name), 1)[0]
    words = _words(before)[-3:]
    key_at = max((before.rfind(word) for word in words if word.casefold() in (keys or _NAME_KEYS)), default=-1)
    return key_at >= 0 and not re.search(r"[{(]", before[:key_at])
Verifies that keys like name or module precede the target name without intervening opening brackets or parentheses.

docs.title: ModuleTable._suffix_hits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Finds registered modules whose path segments terminate with tail. Performs exact case matching first, falling back to case-insensitive matching. Sibling modules in the source's directory take precedence when multiple matches occur.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:
        for fold in (str, str.casefold):
            wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
            hits = [
                path
                for path in self.paths
                if path != source_path and (not ext or path.endswith(ext)) and [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted
            ]
            if len(hits) > 1:
                near = [path for path in hits if posixpath.dirname(path) == posixpath.dirname(source_path)]
                if len(near) == 1:
                    return near
            if hits:
                return hits
        return []
Resolves includes like #include "config.h" by preferring local directory siblings over identically named files elsewhere in the project.

docs.title: ModuleTable._index_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:

Description: Identifies the primary index or module entry file in a directory based on standard naming conventions (_INDEX_STEMS).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:
        members = {_stem(path): path for path in self.by_dir.get(directory, [])}
        return next((members[stem] for stem in _INDEX_STEMS if stem in members), None)
Checks for filenames matching mod, index, __init__, init, main, or lib in order of preference.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves relative import targets (./x, ../x, leading dots, Rust super) against the source file's directory.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").replace("\\", "/")
        parent = re.match(r"^super(?:::(.*))?$", text)
        if parent:
            directory = posixpath.dirname(source_path)
            if _stem(source_path) in _INDEX_STEMS:
                directory = posixpath.dirname(directory)
            rest = [part for part in (parent.group(1) or "").split("::") if part and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)]
            for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
                base = posixpath.join(directory, *rest[:size])
                hits = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base]
                if len(hits) == 1:
                    return hits, "path"
            index_file = self._index_file(directory)
            return ([index_file], "package") if index_file and index_file != source_path else ([], "external")
        dots = re.match(r"^(\.+)(\w[\w.]*)$", text)
        if dots:
            text = "../" * (len(dots.group(1)) - 1) + "./" + dots.group(2).replace(".", "/")
        if not text.startswith(("./", "../")):
            return None
        base = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(source_path), text))
        resolved = self._resolve_rooted(base, source_path, source_words)
        if resolved is not None:
            return resolved
        if dots:
            return [], "external"
        return None
Handles Python relative imports (..core.engine) by converting leading dots to relative path segments before resolution.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_rooted()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves normalized root-relative paths to exact module files or directory entry points.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        base = "" if base in (".", "") else base
        stem_match = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base or path == base)]
        if not stem_match:
            stem_match = [
                path
                for path in self.paths
                if path != source_path and posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.basename(path).split(".")[0]) == base
            ]
        if len(stem_match) == 1:
            return stem_match, "path"
        if not stem_match and base in self.by_dir:
            index_file = self._index_file(base)
            used = [
                path for path in self.by_dir[base] if path != source_path and (path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
            ]
            if used:
                return used, "package"
        return None
Matches file paths across extensions (e.g., resolving ./types to types.d.ts), falling back to directory index files and referenced member modules.

docs.title: ModuleTable._matches_whole()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether every segment of target aligns with the path suffix of a registered module or directory.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:
        parts, _ = self.normalize(target)
        return bool(parts) and (
            any(path != source_path and self.segments[path][-len(parts) :] == parts for path in self.paths)
            or any(d.split("/")[-len(parts) :] == parts for d in self.by_dir if d)
        )
Validates Maven/Java package declarations like com.acme.shipping.Label against physical path structures.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_in_package()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Resolves sub-paths within a manifest package, checking package roots, nested subdirectories, re-exported barrel files, and owned symbols.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
        directory = package["dir"]
        under = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (not directory or path.startswith(directory + "/"))]
        root = self._package_root(package, under, source_path, source_words)
        if not rest:
            return root
        for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
            tail = rest[:size]
            for fold in (str, str.casefold):
                wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
                hits = [path for path in under if [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted]
                if len(hits) == 1:
                    return hits
                dirs = [
                    d
                    for d in self.by_dir
                    if (not directory or d == directory or d.startswith(directory + "/"))
                    and [fold(part) for part in d.split("/")[-len(tail) :]] == wanted
                ]
                if len(dirs) == 1:
                    index_file = self._index_file(dirs[0])
                    used = [
                        path
                        for path in self.by_dir[dirs[0]]
                        if path != source_path and (path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
                    ]
                    if used:
                        return used
                if hits or dirs:
                    break
        if len(rest) == 1 and len(root) == 1 and rest[0] in _words(self.contents.get(root[0], "")):
            return root
        owner = self.symbol_owner.get(rest[-1])
        return [owner] if owner in under else []
Falls back to package root modules when single-segment targets match symbols re-exported by index barrel files.

docs.title: ModuleTable._package_root()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Identifies the primary entry module for a manifest package, evaluating explicit entry targets, index files, or package-named files.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
        directory, entry, last = package["dir"], package["entry"], package["segments"][-1] if package["segments"] else ""
        if entry:
            hits = [path for path in under if path == entry or os.path.splitext(path)[0] == os.path.splitext(entry)[0]]
            if hits:
                return hits[:1]
        for sub in ("", "src", "lib", last, f"src/{last}"):
            index_file = self._index_file(posixpath.join(directory, sub).rstrip("/") if sub else directory)
            if index_file and index_file in under:
                return [index_file]
        for sub in ("", "src", "lib"):
            base = posixpath.join(directory, sub, last).strip("/")
            named = [path for path in under if os.path.splitext(path)[0].casefold() == base.casefold()]
            if len(named) == 1:
                return named
        return [path for path in under if self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words)]
Searches common convention subdirectories (src, lib) and matches filenames sharing the package's stem name.

docs.title: ModuleTable._corroborated()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:

Description: Confirms suffix matches when leading segments of a qualified target are omitted during resolution.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
    def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:
        if size < len(parts):
            dropped = parts[: len(parts) - size]
            alias = not re.match(r"\w", dropped[0]) and not (self.packages or self.aliases)
            return alias or declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), dropped[-1]) or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        if len(parts) == 1 and not _is_relative(target):
            directory, source_dir = posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.dirname(source_path)
            ancestor = not directory or source_dir == directory or source_dir.startswith(directory + "/")
            return ancestor or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        return True
Requires proof that the target file declares the dropped namespace prefix or that the consuming module references symbols defined in that file.

docs.title: _names_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a module name appears in an evidence line as part of a path or qualified reference rather than a standalone word.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        before = evidence[match.start() - 1] if match.start() else ""
        after = evidence[match.end() :]
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", after)
        if written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension:
            continue
        if before in _QUALIFIERS or (extension and after.startswith(extension)) or (after and after[0] in _CLOSERS):
            return True
    return False
Requires boundary characters matching _QUALIFIERS (., /, \, :, ", ', <, `) or trailing closers, filtering out plain variable names.

docs.title: _plain_occurrence()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Confirms a name appears in evidence without referencing another documented file extension (e.g., ensuring socket in socket.h does not falsely match socket.cpp).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", evidence[match.end() :])
        if not (written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension):
            return True
    return False
Prevents cross-extension false positives when multiple source files share the same base stem.

docs.title: _names_directory()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether evidence references a directory by its terminal segments (e.g., verifying internal/store matches "example.com/shop/internal/store").

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:
    tail = [re.escape(part) for part in directory.split("/")[-2:]]
    return re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"(?:\.|/|\\|::)".join(tail) + r"(?!\w)", evidence) is not None
Requires multi-segment matching to prevent standard library modules (like net/http) from falsely matching local subdirectories like internal/http.

docs.title: _import_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether an evidence line begins with an import-related keyword, skipping visibility modifiers.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:
    words = _words(evidence.lstrip().lstrip("#@"))
    while words and words[0] in _MODIFIERS:
        words = words[1:]
    return bool(words) and words[0] in _IMPORT_WORDS
Matches leading keywords against _IMPORT_WORDS (import, require, include, using, use).

docs.title: _without_bindings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:

Description: Strips local alias bindings (as billing, => x, using Env =) from an import statement to isolate the target module reference.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:
    line = re.sub(r"\bas\s+[\w$]+", " ", line)
    line = re.sub(r"=>\s*[\w$]+", " ", line)
    return re.sub(r"^(\s*(?:global\s+)?(?:using|import)\s+)[\w$]+\s*=(?!=)", r"\1", line)
Prevents local binding aliases from interfering with module name matching in evidence_names_module().

docs.title: _bare_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:

Description: Strips leading relative and absolute path prefixes (./, ../, /).

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"^(?:\.{1,2}/|/|\.+)+", "", text)
Standardizes path strings for target-written comparisons.

docs.title: _imports_target()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:

Description: Confirms an evidence line imports a target module via an import statement, a Go import-block path, or an inline qualified call.

# Sourced from utils/facts.py
def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:
    lines = split_lines(evidence)
    quoted = re.escape(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>"))
    if any(import_statement_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line) for line in lines) or re.search(rf"[\"'`<]{quoted}[\"'`>]", evidence):
        return True
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith(("//", "#", "/*", "*", "--", ";")):
            continue
        code = re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", line)
        if re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){quoted}(?:::|\.)\w", code):
            return True
    return False
Filters out comments and string literals, confirming the target reference is part of an executable import or qualified access.

docs.title: FactClaim
docs.text:
Normalized representation of a verified single-file fact claim stored within verify_file_claims return dictionaries.

Field Type Description name str Name of the verified symbol, config key, or error type (absent on dependency items). target str Import specifier as claimed by the LLM (present only on dependency items). kind str Semantic kind (e.g., "class", "function", "config", "symbol"). parent str Name of enclosing container symbol, or empty string if top-level. visibility str \| None Visibility modifier (e.g., "public", "private"), or None. line int 1-based start line index where the claim was verified in source. end_line int 1-based end line index if the match spans multiple lines (optional). signature str Verbatim source excerpt corresponding to the symbol signature. evidence str Verbatim source excerpt verifying dependencies, config, or errors. match str Tier that matched the claim: "exact", "joined", or "tokens". truncated bool Present and True if the excerpt exceeded 300 characters and was trimmed. ambiguous_lines list[int] 1-based line numbers of alternative matching lines for top-level symbols.

docs.text:
The top-level JSON document structure saved to facts.json by save_facts() and built by build_facts_document().

Field Type Description schema int Version identifier for the facts format (constant FACTS_SCHEMA = 1). project str Name of the analyzed project repository. commit str \| None 40-character Git HEAD commit SHA, or None. note str Operational description explaining verification semantics and coverage. modules dict[str, dict] Map of repository-relative module paths to their verified facts and coverage metrics. manifests dict[str, dict] Map of manifest paths to their verified provides and aliases rules.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
facts.py avoids raising unhandled exceptions during verification, treating extraction discrepancies as data points rather than fatal failures:

  • Unparsed LLM Responses: If an LLM response cannot be parsed as valid YAML upstream, an integer count is recorded in claims["unparsed"]. verify_file_claims() and verify_manifest_claims() convert these directly into rejected claim records ({"kind": "unparsed", "reason": "reply item that is not valid YAML"}), keeping coverage statistics balanced.
  • Corrupted or Missing Files: load_facts() handles file access and JSON parsing errors by catching (OSError, ValueError) and returning an empty dictionary ({}). Similarly, source_commit() handles Git subprocess failures by catching (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) and returning None.
  • Ambiguous Symbol Resolution: When a member's signature matches multiple locations in a file and parent scope boundaries cannot disambiguate them, the claim is rejected with "signature matches several lines; the parent does not tell them apart". Top-level signatures matching multiple lines are retained at their first occurrence and annotated with ambiguous_lines.
  • Atomic Persistence: save_facts() guards against corrupted state files caused by process termination during I/O by writing to a temporary file (.tmp) before calling os.replace().

docs.title: files.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/files.py

Following the sanitization and filtering boundary established in exclude_patterns.py, which eliminates non-essential assets, binaries, and sensitive paths from the crawling boundary, utils/files.py provides deterministic data restructuring and selective content extraction utilities. These helpers bridge raw filesystem ingestion outputs with downstream Large Language Model (LLM) context preparation pipelines.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/files.py module defines core transformation routines that operate on sequential collections of repository source files. During the codebase analysis workflow, source files extracted by crawl_local_files.py or crawl_github_files.py are normalized into indexed tuples of (path, content). Because production repositories often contain hundreds of files whose collective token volume exceeds model context windows, the pipeline cannot eagerly inject entire codebases into single prompt invocations. Instead, utils/files.py facilitates a two-stage topological ingestion model: high-level structural exploration followed by targeted content retrieval.

The first stage relies on build_directory_tree(), which parses file path hierarchies and compiles a canonical, human-readable directory tree string where each file name is mapped to its explicit zero-based integer index (e.g., basename (idx:0)). Upstream graph nodes in nodes.py—such as IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, and routing components—inject this compact tree string into initial reasoning prompts. This layout provides LLMs with global structural context regarding project topology, package organization, and file naming semantics while consuming a minimal fraction of the token budget.

The second stage is executed through get_content_for_indices(). Once an upstream LLM reasons over the structural directory tree and identifies a subset of files critical to a specific module or architectural abstraction, it emits a sequence of file indices. get_content_for_indices() acts as an index-bounded projection layer, extracting only the specified file payloads from the source collection and formatting them into key-value pairs formatted as "{index} # {path}". This approach isolates downstream inference passes from irrelevant source code, maximizes prompt cache hits across repeated invocations, and enforces safety bounds against model-generated index hallucinations.
