docs.title: prune_stale_pages()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prune_stale_pages(api_docs_path, chapter_files):

Description: Deletes .md files under docs/api/ that are not part of the current build, and removes any directories left empty as a result. Files are tracked by filesystem device and inode numbers to prevent accidental deletion on case-insensitive filesystems.

Parameters: * api_docs_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to the docs/api directory. * chapter_files (list[dict]): List of active chapter dictionaries.

Returns: * None: Removes stale files and empty subdirectories from disk.

Example: 

def prune_stale_pages(api_docs_path, chapter_files):
    def identity(path):
        st = os.stat(path)
        return st.st_dev, st.st_ino

    keep = set()
    for filename in ["index.md", *(cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files)]:
        path = os.path.join(api_docs_path, filename)
        if os.path.exists(path):
            keep.add(identity(path))
    for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(api_docs_path, topdown=False):
        for name in files:
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            if name.endswith(".md") and identity(path) not in keep:
                os.remove(path)
                emit("MKDOCS_PRUNED_STALE", path=path)
        if os.path.normcase(root) != os.path.normcase(api_docs_path) and not os.listdir(root):
            os.rmdir(root)

The function defines an internal identity() helper that calls os.stat to extract (st_dev, st_ino) tuples. It populates a keep set with the identities of index.md and all active chapter files. It then performs a bottom-up directory traversal (topdown=False) using os.walk. Any .md file whose file identity is missing from keep is deleted, and any empty subdirectories (excluding the root api_docs_path) are removed with os.rmdir.

Visibility: Public Signature: def write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui):

Description: Emits documentation in standalone format, writing an index.md file, individual numbered chapter files, and a consolidated full_content.md file with a table of contents and internal anchor tags.

def write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui):

    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_STANDALONE")
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))

    index_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "index.md")
    with open(index_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(index_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=index_filepath)

        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)

    toc_lines = [f"# {ui['toc']}\n"]
    full_content_lines = []

    full_content = "\n".join(toc_lines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(full_content_lines)
    full_content_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "full_content.md")
    with open(full_content_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(full_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=full_content_filepath)

The function writes index.md and each individual chapter file to the target output directory. It then builds full_content.md by reading chapter titles, generating an index of anchor links (#chapter-N), inserting <a id="chapter-N"></a> anchors before each chapter's content, and separating chapters with horizontal rules (---).

docs.title: _sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _sentences(text: str):

Description: Generator that yields sentences from a prose block. It detects sentence endings while skipping common whole-word abbreviations (such as "e.g." or "vs.") that would otherwise cause false-positive splits.

Parameters: * text (str): Prose text to segment.

Yields: * str: Individual sentence strings extracted from the text.

Example: 

def _sentences(text: str):
    start = 0
    for match in _SENTENCE_END_RE.finditer(text):
        piece = text[start : match.start()]
        if not piece or _ends_with_abbreviation(piece):
            continue
        yield piece
        start = match.end()
    if text[start:]:
        yield text[start:]

The generator scans for punctuation boundaries using _SENTENCE_END_RE (which matches ., !, ? before whitespace, as well as CJK full-stop characters 。, ！, ？). For each candidate boundary, it checks whether the preceding text segment terminates with an abbreviation via _ends_with_abbreviation(). If an abbreviation is detected, the boundary is skipped and scanning continues; otherwise, the sentence segment is yielded.

docs.title: _ends_with_abbreviation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ends_with_abbreviation(piece: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a text segment ends with a recognized whole-word abbreviation from _ABBREVIATIONS (e.g., "e.g.", "i.e.", "approx.").

Parameters: * piece (str): Text segment preceding a punctuation mark.

Returns: * bool: True if the segment ends with a whole-word abbreviation; otherwise False.

Example: 

def _ends_with_abbreviation(piece: str) -> bool:
    lower = piece.lower()
    for abbreviation in _ABBREVIATIONS:
        if lower.endswith(abbreviation):
            before = lower[: -len(abbreviation)][-1:]
            if not before or not before.isalnum():
                return True
    return False

The helper converts the input segment to lowercase and checks it against each abbreviation in _ABBREVIATIONS. If a match is found, it inspects the character immediately preceding the abbreviation string. If that character is empty or non-alphanumeric, the match is confirmed as a standalone abbreviation rather than a word ending (e.g., distinguishing "e.g." from "piano.").

docs.title: _is_prose()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _is_prose(text: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a text line contains complete sentences and terminal punctuation rather than acting as a bare label or header line.

Parameters: * text (str): String line to inspect.

Returns: * bool: True if sentence punctuation is detected; otherwise False.

Example: 

def _is_prose(text: str) -> bool:
    """True when *text* holds sentence punctuation, i.e. is prose rather than a bare label line."""
    stripped = text.rstrip("*_ ")
    return any(mark in text for mark in (". ", "! ", "? ", *_CJK_STOPS)) or stripped.endswith((".", "!", "?"))

The function strips trailing Markdown styling markers (*, _, spaces) from the input string. It returns True if the text contains standard mid-text sentence endings (., !, ?), contains any CJK full-stop characters, or ends with terminal punctuation (., !, ?).

docs.title: _section_members()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _section_members(sections: list) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:

Description: Flattens nested section trees into a list of top-level section tuples, rolling child section modules up into their parent sections and deduplicating modules so each appears only in the first section that references it.

Parameters: * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical section trees.

Returns: * list[tuple[str, list]]: A list of (section_name, [module_names]) tuples for all top-level sections.

Example: 

def _section_members(sections: list) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:
    owned = set()

    def modules_of(section):
        found = list(section.get("modules", []))
        for child in section.get("children", []):
            found += modules_of(child)
        return found

    groups = []
    for section in sections:
        members = []
        for name in modules_of(section):
            if name not in owned:
                owned.add(name)
                members.append(name)
        groups.append((section["name"], members))
    return groups

The function defines an inner recursive helper modules_of() that gathers all module names from a section and its nested children. The outer loop tracks claimed module names in an owned set. If a module is referenced across multiple sections, it is assigned exclusively to the first section that encountered it.

docs.title: _mermaid_label()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _mermaid_label(text) -> str:

Description: Sanitizes plain-text labels for use in quoted Mermaid diagram nodes, replacing characters that interfere with Mermaid's syntax parser with numeric entity codes.

Parameters: * text (Any): Source label string or object.

Returns: * str: Sanitized string safe for inclusion in Mermaid node declarations.

Example: 

def _mermaid_label(text) -> str:
    text = " ".join(str(text).split())
    for char, code in (("#", "#35;"), ('"', "#quot;"), ("`", "#96;"), ("<", "#lt;"), (">", "#gt;")):
        text = text.replace(char, code)
    return text

The helper collapses all internal whitespace into single spaces. It then escapes special characters using numeric entities: # becomes #35;, " becomes #quot;, backticks become #96;, and angle brackets </> become #lt; and #gt;. Escaping # first prevents double-encoding of subsequent entity prefixes.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module uses defensive error handling patterns to prevent invalid model responses, file system differences, or Markdown parsing anomalies from halting the documentation build:

  • LLM Grouping Failure Fallback: In write_mkdocs_output(), LLM-assisted section clustering is wrapped in a broad try-except Exception as e block. If parsing fails, an invalid schema is returned, or the network call drops, the error is logged to dest="LOG" via emit_raw() alongside a full stack trace. The pipeline then emits GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK and falls back to the deterministic, flat navigation layout provided by prep_res["nav_snippet"].
  • Empty Section and Null Nav Guard: prune_sections() drops modules that do not match known chapters, as well as sections left with no modules or children. This prevents MkDocs from encountering null YAML navigation items (- "Section Name":), which causes mkdocs build to abort with "Expected nav to be a list, got None".
  • Safe Frontmatter Parsing: split_frontmatter() catches exceptions raised by yaml.safe_load(). If a chapter opens with a horizontal divider (---) or contains invalid frontmatter (such as an impossible date), the exception is suppressed and the content is retained as regular Markdown body text.
  • Mermaid Syntax Escaping: In _mermaid_label(), characters that conflict with Mermaid's syntax parser (#, ", `, <, >) are replaced with their corresponding numeric entity codes (#35;, #quot;, #96;, #lt;, #gt;). This prevents unescaped characters in code identifiers or comments from breaking diagram rendering.
  • Cross-Platform Inode Tracking: In prune_stale_pages(), files are tracked by their filesystem device and inode numbers (st_dev, st_ino). This ensures that case-only file renames on case-insensitive filesystems (such as macOS or Windows) do not cause active files to be mistakenly identified as stale and deleted.

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the generation and layout assembly handled by mkdocs.py, the utils/output.py module serves as the centralized terminal presentation, telemetry broadcasting, and persistent file logging engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It decouples hardcoded console output and operational notifications from core pipeline logic, routing all human-facing messaging through a structured, multi-lingual localization catalog.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/output.py implements a unified, level-aware messaging bus designed to handle simultaneous standard output rendering and persistent file-based audit logging. The architecture abstracts string presentation behind symbolic keys defined in an external CSV catalog (utils/strings.csv). By standardizing user messages around unique identifier keys, the system supports dynamic multi-language localization, safe variable interpolation, and centralized level styling without scattering formatting logic across workflow nodes or low-level transport adapters.

A critical design challenge addressed by the module is managing output during early runtime initialization—specifically before command-line parsing, project directory creation, or log file configuration occurs. Standard library logging systems often drop early telemetry or require complex early-handler setups. utils/output.py solves this by introducing a bounded in-memory buffer (_pending_log) that holds preflight entries (such as credential checks, environment verification, and auto-translation records). Once configure_logging() executes, the buffered messages are atomically flushed into the newly initialized run log, ensuring continuous audit trails without data loss.

The module also handles cross-platform encoding constraints and console routing rules. On non-interactive or redirected standard output streams (notably on Windows environments where non-UTF-8 code pages like CP-1252 would trigger UnicodeEncodeError when printing localized CJK or accented Latin text), the module safely reconfigures stdout and stderr streams to UTF-8. Message routing supports multiple destination targets (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, and debug-gated variants DBOTH, DSTDOUT), pairing ANSI terminal color sequences with unadorned, ISO-8601-timestamped file logs.

flowchart TD initNode["Initialize output system: init()"] --> streamCheck["Reconfigure non-TTY streams to UTF-8"] streamCheck --> loadCSV["Load strings.csv into memory"] loadCSV --> autoTransCheck{"auto_translate flag active?"} autoTransCheck -- Yes --> runAutoTrans["Invoke i18n.auto_translate()"] autoTransCheck -- No --> callerLoop["Caller invokes emit(), emit_raw(), or get()"] runAutoTrans --> callerLoop subgraph SubgraphRouting["Message Routing Engine"] routeStart["Evaluate destination: BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT"] routeStart --> debugCheck{"Is destination D-prefixed?"} debugCheck -- Yes, debug active --> stripDPrefix["Strip prefix: DBOTH to BOTH, DSTDOUT to STDOUT"] debugCheck -- Yes, debug inactive --> divertToLog["Set destination to LOG only"] debugCheck -- No --> evaluateDest{"Target destination?"} stripDPrefix --> evaluateDest divertToLog --> evaluateDest evaluateDest -- STDOUT or BOTH --> renderTerminal["Apply ANSI color code and print to terminal"] evaluateDest -- LOG or BOTH --> writeBuffer["Pass to _write_log()"] end subgraph SubgraphLogging["File Logging Pipeline"] logStart["_write_log(level, text)"] logStart --> handleCheck{"Is _log_file initialized?"} handleCheck -- No --> bufferQueue["Append to _pending_log (capped at 5,000 lines)"] handleCheck -- Yes --> flushFile["Format timestamp: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,fff"] flushFile --> writeDisk["Write line to disk and flush"] end callerLoop --> routeStart writeBuffer --> logStart classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class initNode entryNode class routeStart entryNode class logStart entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True) -> None

Description: Initializes the output subsystem by setting module-level configuration state, ensuring UTF-8 stream compliance across operating system pipes, loading the localization database from strings.csv, and optionally triggering large language model auto-translation for missing localization tokens. Must be invoked from the application entry point (main()) before invoking any messaging helpers.

Parameters: * language (str): Target localization language name (e.g., "english", "vietnamese"). Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether downstream LLM translation calls should leverage response caching. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (Any): Configured reasoning/thinking effort level forwarded to downstream LLM translation invocations. Defaults to None. * debug (bool): Global switch enabling verbose diagnostic outputs and activating DBOTH / DSTDOUT console routing targets. Defaults to False. * auto_translate (bool): If True, synchronously scans and translates missing string catalog entries during initialization. When False, defers translation until credentials and arguments are validated. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly; failures during string loading or translation degrade gracefully to English fallback values.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/output.py initialization usage:
init(
    language="vietnamese",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level=None,
    debug=False,
    auto_translate=False,
)


def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _ensure_utf8_streams()
    _load_strings()
    if auto_translate:
        _auto_translate()
The init() function establishes the runtime state required for all subsequent output operations across the system. It canonicalizes the language parameters by generating a capitalized display representation (_language) alongside a normalized lowercase column key (_lang_col) matching CSV schema headers. It then dynamically anchors the catalog path to utils/strings.csv using the file's directory path. Stream sanity checks (_ensure_utf8_streams) and catalog parsing (_load_strings) are executed immediately. If auto_translate is enabled, the helper immediately attempts to resolve missing localization definitions via downstream LLM integration.

docs.title: translate_missing_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def translate_missing_strings() -> None

Description: Public entry point to trigger the automated translation of missing string entries in strings.csv using the configured target language and LLM provider. Used when init() was called with auto_translate=False to defer model inference until CLI arguments and LLM authentication keys have passed validation checks.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly.

Example: 

# Defers translation until authentication preflight succeeds
init(language="vietnamese", auto_translate=False)
# ... validate CLI flags and LLM credentials ...
translate_missing_strings()


def translate_missing_strings():
    """Auto-translate strings missing for the configured language (LLM call); see init(auto_translate=False)."""
    _auto_translate()
This utility acts as a clean public wrapper delegating execution to the internal _auto_translate() helper. It enables the primary application workflow in main.py to decouple output subsystem initialization from active network calls. Because language model translation relies on verified credentials and established provider endpoints, postponing catalog translation guarantees that missing keys will not trigger premature network exceptions before authentication preflights conclude.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key: str, suffix: str = "", **kwargs) -> None

Description: Retrieves a translatable template string from the in-memory catalog using a symbolic key, interpolates keyword variables safely, appends an optional unformatted suffix, and directs the resulting message to terminal standard output and/or the run log file according to catalog destination rules and debug switches.

Parameters: * key (str): Identifier key matching an entry in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER"). * suffix (str): Optional string appended directly to the end of the formatted message (e.g., raw token counts or duration statistics). Defaults to "". * **kwargs: Key-value pairs for string template interpolation via Python .format() substitution.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised. If key is missing from strings.csv, prints an [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] warning directly to standard output.

Example: 

# Emit a localized progress message with dynamic parameters and token breakdown
emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", suffix=" [1,420 tokens]", chapter_num=1, name="flow")


def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
The emit() function serves as the standard emission interface for all cataloged pipeline events. When invoked, it looks up the key in the module's _strings cache and passes the raw template along with kwargs to _format_safe(). If a routing destination begins with D (such as DBOTH or DSTDOUT), it checks the active _debug state: if debug mode is active, the prefix is stripped to allow console printing; otherwise, the destination is demoted to LOG to keep console output clean while preserving audit history. Terminal output applies ANSI color sequences mapped to the entry's level (COLORS.get(level)), while file logging via _write_log() records the plain message tagged with the uncolored level name.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level: str, text: str, dest: str = "BOTH") -> None

Description: Emits a pre-formatted string directly to console and/or file destinations without referencing strings.csv. Designed for dynamic structural outputs, diagnostic banners, tables, and un-templatized operational details.

Parameters: * level (str): Log level determining ANSI terminal coloration ("PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG", "FILE_WRITE", or "UI"). * text (str): Pre-formatted text payload to display and log. * dest (str): Output destination routing target ("BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG"). Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Output a dynamic crawl summary table directly to both console and log file
emit_raw("SUCCESS", "Crawled 142 local files successfully (8.4 MB total)", dest="BOTH")


def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
emit_raw() bypasses catalog lookups entirely to accommodate dynamic runtime data, such as ASCII trees, table formatting, or batch processing summaries. If the supplied level is set to "DEBUG" and global debug mode is disabled, the function diverts the destination to "LOG". This ensures verbose debugging diagnostics are persistently captured in the run log without cluttering standard output. ANSI color formatting and destination routing follow the exact same mechanics as emit().

docs.title: is_debug()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_debug() -> bool

Description: Queries the module's internal debug status flag. Used by external components to conditionally construct expensive debug messages or gate verbose diagnostic collections.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * bool: True if --debug mode is enabled; False otherwise.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Gate expensive token layout calculation behind debug check
if is_debug():
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Tiktoken breakdown: {detailed_token_map}")


def is_debug():
    """Return True when --debug is active (used to gate verbose diagnostics outside this module)."""
    return _debug
This query helper allows calling modules to inspect the active debugging state without directly mutating or accessing private module-level state variables. It prevents upstream callers from incurring formatting overhead—such as generating serialized JSON payloads or inspecting large data structures—when debug output is suppressed.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key: str, **kwargs) -> str

Description: Retrieves a translated string template for a given key, performs variable substitution with supplied keyword arguments, and returns the raw string without printing or logging. Primarily utilized to obtain localized headings, section titles, and interface labels embedded inside generated Markdown documents.

Parameters: * key (str): Catalog key identifier defined in strings.csv. * **kwargs: Key-value pairs for template variable interpolation.

Returns: * str: The localized, interpolated string. If the key is not found in the catalog, returns key as a fallback.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Retrieve localized section header for MkDocs index generation
section_title = get("UI_MODULE_OVERVIEW", module_name="Authentication")


def get(key, **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
get() exposes the localization engine directly to document-generation modules like mkdocs.py. Unlike emit(), it does not write to standard output or persist lines to _log_file. If a key is absent from the in-memory cache, it safely degrades by returning the raw key identifier, preventing template generation pipelines from failing due to missing UI strings.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str

Description: Configures and opens a dedicated, timestamped file log on disk. Flushes any log entries accumulated in the in-memory buffer (_pending_log) prior to configuration and prints initial execution metadata headers.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the target project or repository being analyzed. Sanitized for filesystem safety. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Operating pipeline mode (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: Absolute or relative path to the newly created log file.

Raises: * OSError: If log directory creation or file handle allocation fails due to filesystem permissions.

Example: 

# Initialize disk logging for a project workflow run
log_filepath = configure_logging(project_name="my_repo", mode="api-reference")
# Output: logs/my_repo_api_reference_20260330_141500.log


def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    global _log_file

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_path = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Close any existing log file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()

    _log_file = open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: SIM115

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    sep = "=" * 80
    emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"Log file: {log_path}", dest="LOG")
    if _pending_log:
        _log_file.write("".join(_pending_log))
        _log_file.flush()
        _pending_log.clear()

    return log_path
configure_logging() manages log file creation and initialization for each run. It resolves the output directory from the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs/) and creates it if necessary using os.makedirs. Project names and modes are sanitized to alphanumeric and safe delimiter characters (-_) to prevent path traversal or filesystem errors. Any previously open file handle assigned to _log_file is closed. It then opens the target path in append mode with explicit utf-8 encoding. Initial metadata headers are logged, and all buffered log messages stored in _pending_log are written to disk and flushed before clearing the memory buffer.

docs.title: shutdown()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def shutdown() -> None

Description: Closes the open log file handle and releases associated filesystem resources. Should be executed within the finally block of the top-level application entry point to ensure all buffered entries are committed to disk.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Ensure clean resource release upon application exit
try:
    run_pipeline()
finally:
    shutdown()


def shutdown():
    """Close the log file handle and release resources.

    Should be called at the end of main() in a finally block to ensure
    the log file is properly flushed and closed.
    """
    global _log_file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()
        _log_file = None
shutdown() guarantees that the active log file descriptor is properly flushed and closed upon system termination. It safely inspects _log_file, invokes .close(), and resets the reference to None. This prevents file locking issues or truncated trailing logs across repeated runs or automated test suites.

docs.title: _write_log()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_log(level: str, text: str) -> None

Description: Internal logging worker that formats a single log entry with a microsecond-precision timestamp and level marker. If configure_logging() has not yet been executed, the entry is queued in _pending_log (bounded to PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES). Once configured, entries are written directly to _log_file and flushed.

Parameters: * level (str): Log level category identifier (e.g., "PROGRESS", "ERROR", "INFO"). * text (str): Uncolored text payload of the message.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Internal invocation from emit() or emit_raw()
_write_log("INFO", "Discovered 42 files matching inclusion criteria")


def _write_log(level, text):
    """Write a timestamped line to the log file (buffered until configure_logging opens it)."""
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f")[:-3]
    line = f"{ts} - {level} - {text}\n"
    if _log_file is None:
        _pending_log.append(line)
        if len(_pending_log) > PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES:
            del _pending_log[0]
        return
    _log_file.write(line)
    _log_file.flush()
_write_log() handles log record serialization. Timestamps are formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,fff by truncating microsecond measurements to milliseconds. When _log_file is None, entries are appended to the _pending_log list. To prevent memory leaks during long-running workflows that do not configure logging, the list is capped at PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000) using a FIFO eviction pattern (del _pending_log[0]). When the file is active, lines are immediately written and flushed to guarantee real-time log persistence.

docs.title: _ensure_utf8_streams()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ensure_utf8_streams() -> None

Description: Inspects sys.stdout and sys.stderr to identify non-interactive, redirected, or piped execution environments, reconfiguring their output encodings to utf-8 when necessary.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Executed automatically during init()
_ensure_utf8_streams()


def _ensure_utf8_streams():
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", "") or "").lower().replace("-", "")
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure") and encoding != "utf8" and not stream.isatty():
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
This utility prevents encoding crashes on Windows platforms when output is piped to another process or redirected to a file. Interactive consoles on modern Python runtimes (PEP 528) use UTF-8 by default, but redirected streams often fall back to legacy system codepages like CP-1252. If a non-TTY stream does not use UTF-8, _ensure_utf8_streams() invokes stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This ensures Unicode characters (such as CJK text or accented characters) can be safely output without raising UnicodeEncodeError.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template: str, kwargs: dict) -> str

Description: Safely interpolates keyword variables into a template string using template.format(**kwargs), gracefully suppressing formatting errors if keys are missing or malformed.

Parameters: * template (str): Template string containing {placeholder} tokens. * kwargs (dict): Dictionary of keyword arguments to interpolate into the template.

Returns: * str: The formatted string, or the original unaltered template if an interpolation error occurs.

Raises: * No exceptions raised; catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError.

Example: 

# Safely handles missing template variables without throwing exceptions
formatted = _format_safe("Processing {current} of {total}", {"current": 5})
# Returns "Processing {current} of {total}" if 'total' is missing


def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template
_format_safe() provides error isolation for string formatting. Dynamic templates loaded from strings.csv can contain placeholder variables (e.g., {project}, {count}). If caller invocations omit an expected keyword argument or the template contains unbalanced braces, standard .format() raises KeyError, IndexError, or ValueError. This helper traps those exceptions and returns the raw template string as a fallback, ensuring that messaging errors never interrupt core pipeline processing.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings() -> None

Description: Parses utils/strings.csv using csv.DictReader and populates the internal _strings catalog dictionary. Implements localized fallback resolution, defaulting to English values if the target language column entry is missing or empty.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If the CSV file is inaccessible due to invalid permissions (file existence is checked prior to reading).

Example: 

# Reload the internal string cache after file modifications
_load_strings()


def _load_strings():
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")
_load_strings() initializes and populates the in-memory string catalog. It opens _csv_path using utf-8-sig encoding to transparently strip any Byte Order Marks (BOM) introduced by text editors or Microsoft Excel. It iterates through each row, skipping blank lines and comment rows starting with #. For each valid key, it checks the configured language column (_lang_col); if empty, it falls back to the "english" column. Entries are stored in _strings as dictionaries containing "text", "level", and "dest". If a non-English language is fully translated, a success notification is emitted.

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate() -> None

Description: Lazily imports utils.i18n.auto_translate to translate any missing string entries in strings.csv for the configured language, subsequently reloading the cache via _load_strings() if new translations were written.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * Traps errors downstream; does not propagate translation exceptions.

Example: 

# Internal invocation triggered by init() or translate_missing_strings()
_auto_translate()


def _auto_translate():
    """Auto-translate missing strings via LLM and write back into strings.csv."""
    from utils.i18n import auto_translate

    if auto_translate(_lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level):
        # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
        _load_strings()
_auto_translate() integrates localization updates into the output module. To prevent circular import cycles between output.py, i18n.py, and call_llm.py, auto_translate is imported dynamically inside the function body. If auto_translate() returns True (indicating that new translations were generated and persisted to the CSV file), _auto_translate() calls _load_strings() to refresh the in-memory cache so subsequent emit() calls use the updated translations.

docs.text:
Mapping of semantic output levels to their corresponding ANSI escape sequences:

Level Key ANSI Escape Code Rendered Appearance Intended Context "PROGRESS" "\033[96m" Cyan LLM invocations, active pipeline steps, crawl loops "SUCCESS" "\033[92m" Green Successful step completions, cache hits, finish notices "WARNING" "\033[93m" Yellow Non-fatal alerts, context window limits, fallbacks "ERROR" "\033[91m" Red Fatal failures, API rejections, unhandled exceptions "INFO" "" Standard Console Configuration parameters, file counts, telemetry headers "DEBUG" "\033[90m" Gray Ignored paths, fine-grained AST parsing, debug logs "FILE_WRITE" "" Standard Console File serialization logs (- Wrote {path}) "UI" "" Standard Console Markdown headers and UI labels (never styled)

docs.title: Module State Registry
docs.text:
The module maintains runtime state across multiple module-level variables:

Variable Type Default Value Description _strings dict[str, dict[str, str]] {} In-memory cache mapping string keys to their configuration dictionaries. _language str "English" Capitalized display name of active localization language. _lang_col str "english" Lowercase column header used for CSV lookups. _log_file io.TextIOWrapper or None None Open file handle pointing to the active log file on disk. _pending_log list[str] [] FIFO queue holding log entries generated before log file initialization. PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES int 5000 Maximum capacity of _pending_log before dropping the oldest entries. _csv_path str or None None Absolute filesystem path resolving to utils/strings.csv. _use_cache bool True Global flag indicating if translation LLM calls should use caching. _thinking_level Any None Reasoning effort level passed to translation LLM calls. _debug bool False Global flag controlling verbose debug output and destination routing.

docs.title: Internal String Record (_strings Entry Schema)
docs.text:
Shape of the dictionary stored for each entry in the _strings map:

Field Type Description text str Localized string template containing optional {placeholder} markers. level str Semantic level name corresponding to a key in the COLORS table. dest str Routing destination determining terminal and/or log file output. 
# Example structure of an entry in _strings
{
    "text": "Call LLM: writing chapter {chapter_num} ({name})",
    "level": "PROGRESS",
    "dest": "BOTH",
}

docs.title: Destination Routing Targets
docs.text:
Supported destination values configured in strings.csv or passed to emit_raw():

Target Identifier Terminal Visibility File Log Visibility Debug Gated? Notes "BOTH" Yes Yes No Standard operational notifications. "STDOUT" Yes No No Interactive notices that should bypass log files. "LOG" No Yes No Verbose telemetry and raw diagnostic traces. "DBOTH" Conditional Yes Yes Diverts to LOG unless --debug is active. "DSTDOUT" Conditional No Yes Suppressed completely unless --debug is active. "UI" No No No Never emitted directly; accessed via get().

docs.title: Non-Interactive Stream Transcoding
docs.text: On Windows platforms, redirected standard output streams often default to legacy single-byte codepages (e.g., CP-1252), causing UnicodeEncodeError when non-ASCII characters are encountered. The module resolves this by checking stream.isatty() in _ensure_utf8_streams() and reconfiguring non-TTY streams using stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This ensures Unicode strings are safely output without raising encoding exceptions.

docs.title: Safe Template Variable Substitution
docs.text:
Templates loaded from strings.csv rely on bracketed placeholders (e.g., {project_name}). The internal helper _format_safe() intercepts formatting exceptions: 

try:
    return template.format(**kwargs)
except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
    return template
If caller invocations omit required parameters or include mismatched types, the exception is caught and the original template string is returned as a fallback. This guarantees that missing formatting variables do not cause runtime failures during output emission.

docs.title: Missing Key and Unknown Entry Fallbacks
docs.text: If an unrecognized key is passed to emit() or get(), the module falls back gracefully instead of raising exceptions: * emit() prints a raw warning: [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]. * get() returns the raw key string, allowing document generation pipelines to continue without interruptions from missing UI labels.

docs.title: Bounded In-Memory Buffering
docs.text: Log entries generated before log file initialization are held in _pending_log. To prevent unbounded memory consumption during long-running workflows without file logging, the buffer is capped at 5,000 lines (PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES). Once this threshold is reached, older entries are dropped using a FIFO queue strategy (del _pending_log[0]).

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text: Source: utils/prompts.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Operating directly downstream from telemetry logging in output.py and alongside inference routing in call_llm.py, utils/prompts.py provides the prompt templating infrastructure and defensive response parsing pipeline for the entire codebase analysis framework. Large language models (LLMs) frequently produce slightly malformed outputs—such as unquoted YAML indicator characters, unescaped colons in code signatures, incomplete fenced blocks due to context cutoffs, or non-standard index ranges. This module bridges external model inference with strict internal Python data contracts by loading prompt markdown templates, assembling dynamic inline prompts, and executing resilient, multi-tiered parsing algorithms.

The module implements specialized parsers for critical workflow stages: index resolution (parse_file_index and parse_file_indices), module grouping (parse_grouping_response), and ground-truth fact extraction (parse_facts_response). For structured responses such as YAML, it implements strict pre-validation checks against response truncation markers (e.g., TruncatedResponse emitted by llm_common.py). If standard YAML deserialization fails, the module executes a progressive recovery pipeline—stripping invalid syntax, wrapping raw indicator values, converting plain quotes into YAML block scalar syntax (|-), and isolating broken list elements so that valid entities are salvaged while unparseable items are tallied rather than aborting the pipeline.

Syntax Sanitization"] quoteIndicators["Double-Quote Indicator Values (@, #, *, etc.)"] stripBackticks["Unwrap Invalid Role Backticks"] attemptBaseLoad{"yaml.load(text, BaseLoader)"} end subgraph Salvage ["3. docs.title: parse_file_index()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_file_index(idx_value):

Description: Extracts the first integer encountered from a loose file index representation returned by an LLM. Large language models often annotate returned index values with explanatory comments (e.g., "3 # path/to/file.py") or return range notations (e.g., "0-3"). This function strips extraneous formatting using regular expressions and returns the first integer found as a primitive int, or None if no numerical digits are present.

Parameters: * idx_value (Any): The raw index value returned by the LLM, typically an int, str, or composite scalar.

Returns: * int | None: The first resolved integer from the input, or None if no digits exist.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions; non-digit inputs safely resolve to None.

Example: 

def parse_file_index(idx_value):
    """Extract the first integer from an LLM-returned file index value.

    Handles multiple formats the LLM may produce:
    - Plain int: 3
    - Annotated string: "3 # path/to/file.py"
    - Range notation: "0-3" → returns first number only (caller handles ranges)

    Returns:
        int or None if no digits found.
    """
    nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_value))
    return int(nums[0]) if nums else None
The implementation converts idx_value to a string and searches for consecutive digit sequences using re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_value)). If one or more digit sequences are found, the initial sequence is converted to an integer and returned. If the list is empty (such as when passed an empty string, boolean, or prose without numbers), it returns None.

docs.title: parse_file_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_file_indices(idx_value) -> list[int]:

Description: Strictly parses a single entry from a file index collection returned by an LLM, expanding valid single values and ranges into a list of integers. Unlike parse_file_index(), which greedily takes the first digit run, parse_file_indices() guards against path hallucinations (e.g., extracting 2 from src/v2/api.py). It accepts non-negative integers, annotated index strings (e.g., "3 # path"), and ascending range expressions (e.g., "0-3", "4..7", "1 to 5", or expressions using en-dashes \u2013), bounded by a safety threshold of 10,000 entries.

Parameters: * idx_value (Any): The candidate entry to evaluate, which may be a boolean, integer, string, or arbitrary object.

Returns: * list[int]: A list of resolved integer file indices. Returns an empty list [] for negative integers, booleans, invalid ranges, or arbitrary prose.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions; invalid inputs fail safely to an empty list.

Example: 

def parse_file_indices(idx_value) -> list[int]:
    """Strictly parse one entry of an index list the LLM returned → the indices it names.

    An int, an annotated number ("3 # path") or an ascending range ("0-3", "4..7", expanded). Anything
    else — a negative number, a path with a digit in it (src/v2/api.py), prose — names no index, instead
    of the first digit run picking an unrelated file."""
    if isinstance(idx_value, bool):
        return []
    if isinstance(idx_value, int):
        return [idx_value] if idx_value >= 0 else []
    text = str(idx_value) if isinstance(idx_value, str) else ""
    single = _INDEX_RE.match(text)
    if single:
        return [int(single.group(1))]
    span = _INDEX_RANGE_RE.match(text)
    if span and int(span.group(1)) <= int(span.group(2)) and int(span.group(2)) - int(span.group(1)) < 10000:
        return list(range(int(span.group(1)), int(span.group(2)) + 1))
    return []
The logic begins by checking for booleans (which inherit from int in Python) and immediately returns an empty list to prevent True and False from resolving to 1 or 0. For integers, it returns a single-item list if non-negative. Strings are matched against _INDEX_RE (^\s*(\d+)\s*(?:#.*)?$) for annotated single numbers, and _INDEX_RANGE_RE (^\s*(\d+)\s*(?:-|\.\.|\u2013|to)\s*(\d+)\s*(?:#.*)?$) for range notations. When a range matches, the span is validated to ensure the start index is less than or equal to the end index and the total span is under 10,000 items, returning an expanded list via range().

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):

Description: Loads a prompt markdown template from the project's prompts/ hierarchy on disk. The directory is selected based on the execution mode: advanced if advanced_mode=True, tutorial by default, or an explicit directory override passed via mode (e.g., api-reference or common). Files are read using utf-8-sig encoding to handle UTF-8 Byte Order Marks cleanly. A debug message is emitted to the audit log destination via utils.output.emit_raw.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base filename of the template without the .md extension (e.g., "extract_facts"). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether to read from prompts/advanced/. Defaults to False. * mode (str | None, optional): Explicit subdirectory name inside prompts/. Overrides advanced_mode when provided. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw text content of the loaded prompt template file.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the targeted markdown template file does not exist. * OSError: If filesystem permissions prevent reading the file.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
    from utils.output import emit_raw

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"load_prompt_template | loaded '{template_name}.md' from prompts/{prompt_dir}/", dest="LOG")
    return content
The function navigates two levels up from utils/prompts.py using os.path.dirname to locate the project root, constructing an absolute path to prompts/{prompt_dir}/{template_name}.md. It reads the entire content within a context manager using utf-8-sig. To prevent circular import loops with output.py, emit_raw is lazily imported inside the function scope to record diagnostic log entries.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response):

Description: Extracts and parses a YAML document embedded within Markdown triple-backtick fences (```yaml ... ```) from an LLM response string. The function first verifies that the response was not cut off by an output token ceiling by inspecting the .truncated attribute (an attribute set by TruncatedResponse instances from llm_common.py). It then isolates the content between the ```yaml opening fence and the closing ``` fence, deserializing it using yaml.safe_load.

Parameters: * response (str | TruncatedResponse): The raw text response received from an LLM provider.

Returns: * Any: The deserialized Python data structure (typically a dict or list).

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if response.truncated is True, if the response does not contain the required Markdown YAML code fence delimiters, or if yaml.safe_load fails to parse the string.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    # A reply cut off at max tokens (llm_common.TruncatedResponse) can still contain a parseable
    # fenced prefix that silently drops items — raise so the node retries instead.
    if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
        raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e
The method guards against incomplete outputs by checking getattr(response, "truncated", False). Truncated responses could otherwise yield a syntactically valid YAML subset that silently discards downstream entries. It isolates the YAML substring via successive .split() operations and safely deserializes it. If string splitting or parsing raises an exception, it wraps the failure inside a descriptive ValueError.

docs.title: parse_grouping_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_grouping_response(response):

Description: Parses the structured response generated by group_modules.md, extracting module groupings across three top-level keys: sections, descriptions, and dependencies. If the entire block fails standard YAML parsing, the function initiates a lenient salvage sequence. It un-backticks invalid YAML role strings (e.g., converting role: `utility` to role: utility) and splits the document into independent top-level key blocks using regex lookaheads. Each block is parsed in isolation, ensuring that a malformed description scalar does not compromise the recovered section list or dependency map.

Parameters: * response (str | TruncatedResponse): The LLM response string containing fenced YAML with module groupings.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing the recovered top-level keys, guaranteed to contain at least a valid sections list.

Raises: * ValueError: If the response was truncated, if no ```yaml fence is present, or if the sections list cannot be recovered.

Example: 

def parse_grouping_response(response):
    """Parse the group_modules.md reply (sections + descriptions + dependencies).

    When the whole block is not valid YAML, each top-level block (sections:, descriptions:,
    dependencies:) is parsed on its own and the ones that parse are kept, so one malformed
    description costs neither the grouped sidebar nor the dependencies. A section role written in
    backticks (invalid YAML) is unwrapped first. Raises when sections cannot be recovered, and for
    truncated replies.
    """
    try:
        return parse_yaml_response(response)
    except ValueError:
        if getattr(response, "truncated", False) or "```yaml" not in response:
            raise
        yaml_str = response.split("```yaml", 1)[1].split("```", 1)[0]
        yaml_str = re.sub(r"(?m)^(\s*(?:-\s+)?role\s*:\s*)`([^`\n]*)`", r"\1\2", yaml_str)
        parsed = {}
        for chunk in re.split(r"(?m)^(?=(?:sections|descriptions|dependencies)\s*:)", yaml_str):
            try:
                part = yaml.safe_load(chunk)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if isinstance(part, dict):
                parsed.update(part)
        if not isinstance(parsed.get("sections"), list):
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no sections list in the grouping reply") from None
        return parsed
The function delegates to parse_yaml_response() initially. Upon encountering a ValueError, it checks for unrecoverable conditions (truncated flag or missing fences). If recoverable, it extracts the raw YAML substring and cleans invalid backtick syntax using re.sub(). It then segments the string with re.split(r"(?m)^(?=(?:sections|descriptions|dependencies)\s*:)", yaml_str) and parses each chunk independently via yaml.safe_load(). If the aggregated dictionary lacks a valid sections list, a terminal ValueError is raised.

docs.title: build_facts_focus_note()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_facts_focus_note(lines: list[tuple[int, str]], limit: int = FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT) -> str:

Description: Constructs a prompt instruction note for follow-up fact-extraction requests executed by extract_facts.md. When an initial extraction pass omits lines that appear to contain declarations or imports, this helper formats up to limit (defaulting to FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT = 60) lines into a numbered context block. Lines exceeding _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS (200 characters) are trimmed with an ellipsis to prevent context window bloat while preserving line number citations.

Parameters: * lines (list[tuple[int, str]]): A list of tuples where each element contains a 1-based line number (int) and the source code string (str). * limit (int, optional): Maximum number of lines to explicitly render in the note. Defaults to FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT (60).

Returns: * str: A formatted Markdown instruction block containing line citations and follow-up guidance for the LLM.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def build_facts_focus_note(lines: list[tuple[int, str]], limit: int = FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT) -> str:
    """The {focus_note} of an extract_facts.md follow-up: the uncovered lines a first pass left out."""

    def shown_line(text: str) -> str:
        text = text.strip()
        return text if len(text) <= _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS else text[: _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS - 3] + "..."

    shown = "\n".join(f"  {number}: {shown_line(text)}" for number, text in lines[:limit])
    more = f"\n  ... and {len(lines) - limit} more such lines" if len(lines) > limit else ""
    return (
        "FOLLOW-UP: a first pass over this file reported nothing for the lines below, which look like declarations "
        "or imports. Report ONLY the facts on these lines, with the same four lists and rules; a line that is not a "
        "declaration a reader looks up (a local variable, a statement) gets nothing.\n"
        f"Lines:\n{shown}{more}\n"
    )
The helper defines an inner shown_line() closure that strips whitespace and truncates lines exceeding 200 characters. It formats the visible slice up to limit as indented strings (" {number}: {text}"). If the candidate list exceeds the threshold, an overflow count note ("... and N more such lines") is appended. The resulting string directs the LLM to focus strictly on those line numbers for declaration discovery.

docs.title: parse_facts_response()
docs.text: Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_facts_response(response, keys: tuple = FACTS_KEYS) -> dict:

docs.title: Phase 1: Pre-Validation and Boundary Resolution
docs.text:
Validates response termination markers and locates opening/closing YAML fences.

    if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
        raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    match = _FACTS_BLOCK_RE.search(response) or _FACTS_OPEN_RE.search(response)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no ```yaml block in the facts reply")
    indent = match.group(1)
    yaml_str = _quote_indicator_values("\n".join(line.removeprefix(indent) for line in match.group(2).split("\n")))
    unparsed = 0
This phase checks response.truncated, raising a ValueError immediately on cut-off generations. It uses _FACTS_BLOCK_RE or _FACTS_OPEN_RE to capture the indentation level and content within the code fence. The captured text is stripped of leading indentation matching the fence prefix and passed to _quote_indicator_values() to prevent YAML syntax collisions with special characters.

docs.title: Phase 2: Tiered Parsing Strategy
docs.text:
Executes a multi-tier deserialization ladder progressing from strict text loading to block scalar conversions and item-level salvage routines.

    try:
        data = _load_strings(yaml_str)
    except Exception:
        try:
            data = _load_strings(_block_quotes(yaml_str))
        except Exception:
            data, unparsed = _salvage_yaml_lists(_block_quotes(yaml_str), keys)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not any(key in data for key in keys):
        raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no fact lists in the facts reply")
This phase attempts to deserialize the sanitized string using _load_strings() (yaml.BaseLoader), which ensures numeric tokens (e.g., "404", "3.10") remain string types. If standard loading fails, it applies _block_quotes() to rewrite plain scalars into block scalars (|-) and retries. If parsing still fails, it invokes _salvage_yaml_lists(), which breaks down broken lists item by item. Finally, it validates that data is a mapping containing at least one target key.

docs.title: Phase 3: Contract Sanitization and Metric Assembly
docs.text:
Sanitizes the parsed data structures against target schema keys and calculates lost entity metrics.

    result = {}
    for key in keys:
        items = data.get(key)
        items = items if isinstance(items, list) else []
        result[key] = [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
        unparsed += len(items) - len(result[key])
    result["unparsed"] = unparsed
    return result
This phase iterates across expected schema keys (symbols, dependencies, config, errors by default). For each key, it normalizes None or non-list values to empty lists and filters the list to retain only valid dictionary records (isinstance(item, dict)). Any discarded items are added to the running unparsed counter, which is returned under the "unparsed" key in the result dictionary.

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs the prompt used by DeterministicFileMapper to classify repository files into executable code modules versus static assets, layouts, and workspace manifests. The prompt instructs the LLM to return a strict YAML block containing two lists of integer indices: code (files containing APIs, classes, or logic) and manifests (package configurations declaring project imports, such as package.json, Cargo.toml, or pyproject.toml).

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the repository or project being analyzed. * file_listing (str): Formatted directory tree string generated by files.py, mapping files to indices.

Returns: * str: The rendered instruction prompt string ready for LLM inference.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files."""
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:

"
        f"{file_listing}

"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.
"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.

"
        f"Separately, list the MANIFESTS among the other files: files that declare a package, module, crate or "
        f"workspace name, or import path aliases, for this project's own code (for example package.json, "
        f"tsconfig.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, composer.json, pom.xml, build.gradle, "
        f"*.csproj, mix.exs, pubspec.yaml, *.gemspec).

"
        f"Return ONLY YAML with the file indices of both lists:

"
        f"```yaml
code:
  - 0
  - 1
  - 3
manifests:
  - 2
```"
    )
The implementation uses an f-string template to inject the target project_name and file_listing. It explicitly enumerates file types that must be excluded (e.g., .xaml, .json, .csproj) and details specific package configuration formats for manifest identification. It concludes with a strict few-shot YAML schema example that guides the LLM to format its reply in the structure expected by parse_yaml_response().

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Constructs the prompt for generating a structured technical brief of a newly written documentation chapter. The resulting summary serves as context for downstream chapter generation passes, maintaining architectural coherence across the complete document suite. The prompt enforces a uniform 4-dimensional brief structure (Component Scope & Responsibility, Key Technical Elements, Implementation Patterns & Architecture, and System Integration & Dependencies), requiring 3–5 sentences per section and supporting target output localization.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The 1-based sequential number of the documentation chapter. * abstraction_name (str): The name of the architectural abstraction or module covered in the chapter. * chapter_content (str): The full Markdown text of the generated chapter. * language (str, optional): The target natural language for the brief. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The fully populated prompt string.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter."""
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )
The helper evaluates the language argument and conditionally prepends a directive (e.g., "Write the entire summary in Spanish. ") if the target language is not English. It then defines the 4 technical dimensions required in the brief. Finally, it appends the chapter header metadata (Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}) alongside the raw chapter content to provide the source context for the LLM.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings(text: str):

Description: Wraps yaml.load using yaml.BaseLoader. Standard YAML parsers automatically cast numeric values, version tags, and booleans (e.g., 404, 3.10, on, yes) into integers, floats, or boolean primitives. When parsing fact extractions, these tokens represent code symbols, configuration keys, or HTTP status codes that must remain exact string representations. yaml.BaseLoader guarantees that every scalar is preserved as a primitive str.

Parameters: * text (str): The raw YAML string to deserialize.

Returns: * Any: A deserialized data structure composed strictly of str, list, and dict types.

Raises: * yaml.YAMLError: If the provided text contains unrecoverable YAML syntax errors.

Example: 

def _load_strings(text: str):
    """YAML with every scalar kept as the reply's text: 404, on, 3.10 stay strings."""
    return yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)  # BaseLoader builds only str / list / dict: safe
The helper directly calls yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.BaseLoader). This avoids unintended type coercion (such as converting string ports or semantic version keys into floats) while protecting against unsafe object instantiation vulnerabilities present in yaml.Loader or yaml.FullLoader.

docs.title: _quote_indicator_values()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _quote_indicator_values(text: str) -> str:

Description: Sanitizes unquoted YAML indicator characters appearing at the start of scalar values. LLMs frequently output code identifiers like @acme/api, #db/*, or *args without quotes. In standard YAML syntax, characters such as @, `, #, *, &, !, and % are reserved indicators representing aliases, comments, or tags. This function applies _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE across key fields (name, entry, alias, target, base, parent), wrapping bare indicator values in escaped double quotes before YAML deserialization occurs.

Parameters: * text (str): The raw YAML string to sanitize.

Returns: * str: The sanitized YAML string with problematic scalar values safely enclosed in double quotes.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def _quote_indicator_values(text: str) -> str:
    return _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE.sub(lambda m: m[1] + '"' + m[2].replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"', text)
The regex _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE locates lines beginning with designated keys followed by indicator symbols. The substitution callback isolates the key prefix (m[1]) and raw value (m[2]), escapes backslashes and double quotes within the value, and encloses it in double quotes ("). Valid block indicators (such as target: |-) are matched by a negative lookahead and left unquoted.

docs.title: _block_quotes()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _block_quotes(text: str) -> str:

Description: Transforms unquoted single-line code quotes into YAML block scalars. When LLMs output code signatures or evidence strings (e.g., signature: def run(self):), the embedded colons or trailing hashes cause standard YAML parsers to fail. This function identifies single-line signature: and evidence: declarations that are not already valid whole scalars and rewrites them into literal block scalar format (|-) with appropriate indentation.

Parameters: * text (str): Raw YAML text containing potentially malformed code quotes.

Returns: * str: Rewritten YAML text where plain quotes are converted to indented block scalars.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def _block_quotes(text: str) -> str:
    return _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE.sub(lambda m: m[0] if _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE.match(m[3]) else f"{m[1]}{m[2]}: |-\n{' ' * (len(m[1]) + 2)}{m[3]}", text)
The function scans the text using _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE. If the captured value (m[3]) matches _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE (indicating it is already an enclosed quoted string or a valid block indicator), it is left untouched. Otherwise, it generates a block indicator |-, inserts a newline, and indents the quote value by two spaces beyond the key's margin (len(m[1]) + 2).

docs.title: _salvage_yaml_lists()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _salvage_yaml_lists(yaml_str: str, keys: tuple) -> tuple[dict, int]:

Description: Executes fine-grained salvage operations on severely malformed YAML payloads by decomposing the document into isolated chunks and individual list items. It splits the document at top-level key boundaries (keys). If a top-level block fails to parse, it splits the list body at item bullet boundaries (-). Each item is individually parsed with _load_strings(), collecting valid dictionary items while tallying failed entries in an unparsed counter.

Parameters: * yaml_str (str): The corrupted YAML string that failed full document parsing. * keys (tuple[str, ...]): Expected top-level keys to split and salvage (e.g., FACTS_KEYS).

Returns: * tuple[dict, int]: A 2-tuple containing: 1. dict: A dictionary mapping recovered section keys to lists of successfully parsed dictionary items. 2. int: The count of individual list items that failed parsing.

Raises: * This function does not raise exceptions; corrupted fragments increment the loss counter.

Example: 

def _salvage_yaml_lists(yaml_str: str, keys: tuple) -> tuple[dict, int]:
    """Parse each top-level key: list of a broken YAML block on its own; a list that still fails is
    parsed item by item (split at its own -  indentation) and keeps the items that parse.
    Returns (lists, number of items lost)."""
    names = "|".join(keys)
    parsed, lost = {}, 0
    for chunk in re.split(rf"(?m)^(?=(?:{names})\s*:)", yaml_str):
        head = re.match(rf"({names})\s*:", chunk)
        if not head:
            continue
        try:
            part = _load_strings(chunk)
        except Exception:
            part = None
        if isinstance(part, dict):
            parsed.update(part)
            continue
        body = chunk[head.end() :]
        first = re.search(r"(?m)^([ \t]*)- ", body)
        if not first:
            continue
        indent = first.group(1)
        items = []
        for piece in re.split(rf"(?m)^(?={re.escape(indent)}- )", body):
            if not piece.startswith(f"{indent}- "):
                continue
            text = "\n".join(line.removeprefix(indent) for line in piece.split("\n"))
            try:
                item = _load_strings(text)
            except Exception:
                lost += 1
                continue
            if isinstance(item, list) and item and isinstance(item[0], dict):
                items.append(item[0])
            else:
                lost += 1
        parsed[head.group(1)] = items
    return parsed, lost
The helper constructs a regular expression from the provided keys tuple to split top-level sections via lookaheads. If an entire section parses as a valid dictionary, it is merged immediately into parsed. If section parsing fails, it determines the item bullet indentation (indent) and splits the section body into individual items. Each item is stripped of base indentation and parsed independently. Successfully resolved dictionary items are added to items, while invalid items increment lost.

docs.title: Module-Level Constants and Regular Expressions
docs.text:
Internal constants and regular expressions defined in utils/prompts.py governing parsing limits and syntax patterns.

Identifier Type Description FACTS_KEYS tuple[str, ...] Canonical schema keys: ("symbols", "dependencies", "config", "errors"). FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT int Maximum number of uncovered lines included in a follow-up focus note (60). _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS int Maximum characters shown per source line before appending an ellipsis (200). _INDEX_RE re.Pattern Regex matching single file indices with optional comments (^\s*(\d+)\s*(?:#.*)?$). _INDEX_RANGE_RE re.Pattern Regex matching file index ranges (0-3, 4..7, 1 to 5, or en-dashes). _FACTS_BLOCK_RE re.Pattern Multi-line pattern matching balanced, fenced YAML code blocks. _FACTS_OPEN_RE re.Pattern Multi-line fallback pattern matching unclosed opening YAML fences. _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE re.Pattern Regex identifying unquoted single-line signature: or evidence: scalars. _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE re.Pattern Regex detecting scalars that are already properly quoted or formatted. _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE re.Pattern Regex matching unquoted leading YAML indicator characters (@, #, *, etc.).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/prompts.py enforces a defensive parsing philosophy: whenever an LLM response fails standard deserialization, the module uses progressive fallback strategies to salvage valid information before raising an error.

  • Truncation Pre-emption: LLM completions that reach model context ceilings (marked with truncated = True on TruncatedResponse instances from llm_common.py) can contain partially formed YAML blocks that appear syntactically valid but omit data. Both parse_yaml_response() and parse_facts_response() verify getattr(response, "truncated", False) before executing parse logic, immediately raising a ValueError so pipeline nodes retry instead of continuing with incomplete outputs.

  • Progressive YAML Recovery: When deserializing facts responses in parse_facts_response(), the system applies a three-tiered recovery ladder:

  • Strict Load: Pre-quotes indicator characters via _quote_indicator_values() and attempts standard loading via _load_strings().
  • Scalar Conversion: If strict loading fails, plain scalars in code quotes are converted to block scalars via _block_quotes().

  • Item-Level Salvage: If the block remains unparseable, _salvage_yaml_lists() segments the text into independent sections and item bullets, isolating malformed lines while capturing valid entries.

  • Non-Blocking Index Resolution: In parse_file_indices(), ambiguous or invalid inputs (such as paths containing embedded version numbers like src/v2/api.py, negative indices, or ranges exceeding 10,000 items) do not raise exceptions. They safely evaluate to empty lists ([]), preventing index extraction failures from interrupting file filtering workflows.

docs.title: thinking.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/thinking.py

Following prompt templating and response extraction in prompts.py, the pipeline must determine the cognitive reasoning depth allocated to each Large Language Model (LLM) invocation. The utils/thinking.py module defines the centralized configuration, profile hierarchy, and runtime resolution engine for per-node thinking effort—collectively referred to as "thinking flows." Modern reasoning-capable models (such as the Anthropic Claude 3.7/Sonnet/Opus families, Google Gemini 2.5/3.x series, and reasoning models served through OpenRouter) treat reasoning tokens as a primary lever for balancing generation quality, inference latency, and operational expenditure. This module establishes a provider-neutral abstraction over provider-specific reasoning controls, enabling granular or profile-based tuning across each distinct workflow step.

The module operates as a deterministic rules engine. During application initialization in main.py, CLI flags specifying execution modes, global effort levels, named profiles, and explicit per-node overrides are resolved into an immutable dictionary mapping every pipeline stage to a discrete effort level. At runtime, workflow nodes orchestrated by nodes.py and flow.py query this configuration through resolve_thinking_level(), before transport adapters such as llm_anthropic.py, llm_gemini.py, and llm_openrouter.py normalize or clamp the abstract effort level against provider-specific capabilities using clamp_level().
